carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers.meta_title: Airline Approved Pet Carriers for Cabin Travel
carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers.meta_description: Shop airline approved pet carriers for dogs, cats and small pets. Meets in-cabin size requirements for most major airlines. Free UK delivery.
carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers.intro:
Flying with a pet means working within strict cabin rules, and airlines are specific about what they'll allow under the seat in front of you. An airline approved carrier is built to those constraints from the outset: correct external dimensions, a design low enough to slide beneath a standard economy seat, and enough mesh panelling to satisfy crew doing a visual check before take-off. It's less about the pet being small enough and more about the carrier itself meeting a spec, which is why a general-purpose bag that looks about the right size can still get turned away at the gate.

### Who This Is Best For

This range suits anyone with a confirmed cabin booking for a cat, small dog or other pet travelling in-cabin rather than in the hold. It's particularly useful if you fly with the same airline regularly and already know their exact size limits, since you can match the carrier to that spec rather than guessing. First-time cabin travellers tend to do better with solid, structured sides rather than something that flexes underfoot during turbulence. If you're after a size built around a smaller breed, our [airline approved dog carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/airline-approved-dog-carriers) range and [airline approved cat carrier](/carriers/cat-carriers/airline-approved-cat-carriers) range are sized and shaped for those pets individually.

### What to Look For

- **Confirmed dimensions against your airline, not just "cabin size" claims.** Every airline sets its own limits, and a carrier marketed generically as cabin-friendly can still be a few centimetres over what a specific airline allows.
- **A low, flat profile that slides under the seat without forcing.** Extra height at the top of a carrier is often the first thing that causes a problem at check-in.
- **Mesh ventilation on at least two sides.** Cabin air can get warm on a full flight, so your pet needs proper airflow, not a single small vent.
- **A secure, lockable zip.** Airport handling is busy, and a closure that can't be fixed shut is a real risk during boarding.

Every carrier below lists its exact external dimensions so you can check it against your airline's published allowance before you buy, rather than after. Have a browse through the range, and if you're flying with a nervous flyer, the sizing and buying guide further down this page goes into a bit more detail on what tends to work best in the cabin.

faqs.question: Will this carrier definitely be accepted by my airline?
faqs.answer: Airlines set their own size and weight limits, which can differ even between two carriers with similar external dimensions. Always check your specific airline's current pet policy and confirmed dimensions before you fly, since policies do change from time to time.

faqs.question: Can my pet travel in the cabin with me?
faqs.answer: That depends on your airline's own pet policy, your pet's weight, and the destination's import rules, not on the carrier alone. Contact your airline directly to confirm eligibility before booking, ideally as early as possible since many airlines cap the number of pets allowed in the cabin per flight.

faqs.question: Does the carrier need to fit fully under the seat?
faqs.answer: Yes, in almost all cases. Crew will typically ask to see the carrier slide fully under the seat in front of you before take-off, so check the carrier's height as well as its footprint against your airline's limits.

faqs.question: What's the weight limit for an airline approved carrier?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed individually on each item's specification. Bear in mind that most airlines also set their own combined weight limit for the pet and carrier together, so check both figures.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for car journeys and vet visits too?
faqs.answer: Yes, most airline approved carriers work equally well for car travel and vet appointments thanks to their structured shape and secure closures. Just check it still suits your pet comfortably for everyday use, since it's built to a specific size spec first.

carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers.why_choose:
A carrier genuinely built to airline cabin dimensions removes most of the guesswork at check-in, provided the specific dimensions are also checked against your own airline's current published rules rather than relying on the "airline approved" label alone. That combination, correct build plus your own verification, is what actually gets a pet through the gate without a problem.

Ventilation and a secure closure matter more here than on almost any other carrier type, since your pet may be inside for the full duration of a flight with limited opportunity to be let out. Mesh panelling on more than one side and a lockable zip are both worth checking for specifically.
carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers.sizing_guide: Start with your airline's own published maximum external dimensions and combined pet-and-carrier weight limit, since these vary between airlines and are the figures that actually matter at check-in. Weigh your pet together with the empty carrier to check against that combined limit specifically, and pay particular attention to the carrier's height, since this usually determines whether it fits under the seat in front of you without being forced.

carriers/pet-backpack-carriers.meta_title: Pet Backpack Carriers for Dogs & Cats
carriers/pet-backpack-carriers.meta_description: Hands-free pet backpack carriers for dogs, cats and small animals. Great for hiking, city walks and days out. Free UK delivery over £50.
carriers/pet-backpack-carriers.intro:
A backpack carrier moves the weight of your pet off one shoulder and onto both, which makes a real difference on longer outings where a sling or a hand-held bag starts to feel like hard work after twenty minutes. Instead of a strap digging in on one side, the load sits across your back the way a hiking rucksack does, leaving both hands free for a lead, a coffee, or simply your own balance on uneven ground. It's the format most owners reach for once a trip stops being a quick errand and turns into a proper outing.

### Who This Is Best For

Backpack carriers suit owners covering real distance on foot, whether that's a weekend woodland walk, a busy train platform, or a full day out where a hand-held carrier would start to ache. They also work well for cats and small dogs that settle better facing forward with a view out, rather than tucked against your chest where they can't see much. If you're carrying a lighter cat or toy breed for shorter trips around town, our [cat backpack carrier](/carriers/cat-carriers/cat-backpack-carriers) range is built around that lower weight and a more compact frame, while the [dog backpack carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carriers) range covers a wider spread of dog sizes and sturdier support structures.

### What to Look For

- **Weight distribution across a padded hip belt, not just the shoulders.** A frame that transfers some load to your hips makes a genuine difference over an hour or more of walking.
- **Ventilation panels around the pet compartment.** Your pet is riding close to your back, which generates warmth, so mesh sides matter more here than on a stationary carrier.
- **A clearly stated maximum weight limit.** Backpack frames are only rated to carry so much before the stitching and straps are put under real strain, so check this against your pet's actual weight, not their breed's average.
- **A secure inner tether or harness clip**, so your pet can't climb or jump free mid-walk.

If your usual days out involve a fair bit of walking, a backpack carrier is likely to be the most comfortable option in this range for both of you. Take a look through what's available below, sized from compact cat-friendly frames through to larger structures built for bigger dogs, and check the weight limit and ventilation details on each listing before deciding.

faqs.question: What's the maximum weight a backpack carrier can hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed on each individual listing. Always check the weight limit against your pet's actual current weight rather than an estimate, since backpack frames are only rated to carry so much safely.

faqs.question: Will my pet be comfortable riding on my back?
faqs.answer: Comfort depends on a properly fitted harness inside the carrier and a padded hip belt on the bag itself, both worth checking before buying. A pet that's used to being handled generally settles into a backpack carrier without much fuss.

faqs.question: Can I use a backpack carrier for hiking?
faqs.answer: Yes, backpack carriers are one of the most practical formats for hiking thanks to the hands-free design and weight distribution across both shoulders. For longer or more technical routes, our dedicated hiking pet carrier range is also worth a look.

faqs.question: How is a backpack carrier different from a sling?
faqs.answer: A backpack distributes weight across both shoulders and a hip belt, making it better suited to longer trips, while a sling holds your pet closer to your body on one shoulder, which some pets find more reassuring for shorter journeys.

faqs.question: Are backpack carriers suitable for cats?
faqs.answer: Yes, many cats travel well in a backpack carrier, particularly designs with a forward-facing viewing panel. Our cat backpack carrier range is sized specifically around typical cat weights and dimensions.

carriers/pet-backpack-carriers.why_choose:
Splitting your pet's weight across both shoulders, rather than one hand or one shoulder strap, is what makes a backpack carrier noticeably more comfortable than other formats once a trip runs past twenty or thirty minutes. That difference becomes more obvious the longer the outing, which is exactly why backpacks are the format most owners reach for once a trip stops being a quick errand.

Ventilation matters more here than on a stationary carrier too, since your pet is riding close to your back for a sustained period and body heat from both of you builds up in that space. Mesh panelling positioned around the compartment, not just at the top, makes a genuine difference on warmer days.
carriers/pet-backpack-carriers.sizing_guide: Check the maximum weight rating first, since backpack frames and straps are only built to carry so much before the stitching and support genuinely come under strain. Then check the internal compartment dimensions against your pet's actual size, making sure they can sit or stand comfortably with a secure inner tether attached to their collar or harness.

carriers/pet-rolling-carriers.meta_title: Rolling Pet Carriers with Wheels for Easy Travel
carriers/pet-rolling-carriers.meta_description: Wheeled pet carriers for easy airport transfers and long walks without the strain of carrying. Suitable for dogs, cats and small pets.
carriers/pet-rolling-carriers.intro:
Not every pet enjoys being carried, and not every owner wants to hold onto several kilograms of dog or cat for an entire afternoon. A carrier with wheels solves both problems at once: your pet still travels enclosed and secure, but the weight runs along the ground on a set of wheels rather than through your arms or shoulders. It's a format that comes into its own on long airport concourses, station platforms, and any trip where you'd otherwise be swapping a heavy carrier from hand to hand.

### Who This Is Best For

Wheeled carriers suit heavier dogs and cats where lifting isn't practical for an extended period, and they're a genuine help for owners managing a bad back, a long airport transfer, or simply a lot of luggage at the same time as a pet. They also make sense for older or larger dogs who are happy to sit rather than walk for an entire journey but are too big to comfortably carry by hand. For a dog specifically, our [rolling dog carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/rolling-dog-carriers) range covers a spread of sizes built around this exact use, with a telescopic handle and a stable wheel base.

### What to Look For

- **Wheel size and construction.** Small, hard plastic wheels can struggle on gravel or uneven pavements, while slightly larger rubberised wheels roll more smoothly and quietly.
- **A telescopic handle at a comfortable height**, so you're not stooping to pull it along, particularly over a longer distance like an airport terminal.
- **Total weight capacity including the carrier itself**, since a wheeled unit is naturally heavier than an equivalent soft-sided bag before your pet even gets in.
- **Stability when stationary.** A carrier that tips over easily when left standing isn't practical at a check-in queue or a busy platform.

If carrying isn't realistic for your pet's size or for your own comfort over a longer trip, a wheeled carrier is worth a proper look. Browse the range below, and check both the wheel base and the maximum load rating against your pet's actual weight, since that's usually the detail that matters most here.

faqs.question: How much weight can a wheeled pet carrier hold?
faqs.answer: This is listed individually on each product and includes both your pet's weight and anything else you might be carrying inside. Check the stated capacity carefully rather than assuming it matches a similar-looking soft-sided carrier.

faqs.question: Are wheeled carriers allowed on planes?
faqs.answer: Some are, depending on their folded dimensions and your airline's specific policy, but many wheeled carriers are designed primarily for ground transport such as airports and train stations rather than in-cabin use. Check our airline approved pet carriers range if cabin travel is your main need.

faqs.question: Do the wheels work on rough ground?
faqs.answer: This depends on the wheel size and material, which varies between products. Larger, rubberised wheels generally cope better with gravel or uneven pavements than small hard plastic castors.

faqs.question: Can the handle be adjusted for height?
faqs.answer: Most wheeled carriers in this range have a telescopic handle with two or three height settings, though this is worth checking on the individual product page since it varies by model.

faqs.question: Is a wheeled carrier heavier than a normal one?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally. The wheels, axle and reinforced base add weight compared with an equivalent soft-sided bag, worth factoring in if you'll sometimes need to carry it without rolling it, such as up a flight of stairs.

carriers/pet-rolling-carriers.why_choose:
A wheeled carrier removes the need to carry your pet's full weight by hand for an extended period, which matters most on longer routes such as airport terminals or train platforms where swapping a heavy carrier from hand to hand becomes genuinely tiring. It's also a practical option for owners managing a bad back or simply juggling luggage alongside a pet.

Stability when stationary matters as much as how the carrier rolls, since a unit that tips over easily isn't practical to leave standing at a check-in queue or a busy platform.
carriers/pet-rolling-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your pet as you would for any carrier, then check this against the compartment's internal dimensions, and separately check the wheel base and telescopic handle height suit how you'll actually be using it. Check the total weight capacity including the carrier's own weight, since a wheeled unit is naturally heavier before your pet even gets in.

carriers/pet-sling-carriers.meta_title: Pet Sling Carriers for Small Dogs & Cats
carriers/pet-sling-carriers.meta_description: Comfortable sling carriers that keep small pets close to you. Ideal for nervous animals, puppies and kittens. Free UK delivery.
carriers/pet-sling-carriers.intro:
A sling carrier holds your pet close against your body, supported by a single wide strap worn across one shoulder or across the chest. That closeness is the whole point: for a small, lighter animal, being held snugly against a warm, moving body tends to feel far more reassuring than sitting inside a rigid box a little further away from you. It's a format built around comfort and contact rather than maximum capacity, which is why it suits smaller, lighter pets rather than anything with real bulk or weight.

### Who This Is Best For

Slings work particularly well for young puppies and kittens who are still getting used to the world, older pets who tend to prefer close physical contact over an open carrier, and any small pet on a short trip where being enclosed in a full carrier feels unnecessary. They're less suited to long walks, since the weight sits on one side of your body rather than being distributed, and they're not built for pets who wriggle a lot or try to climb out. Our [dog sling](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings) range is shaped and padded for dogs specifically, while the [cat sling](/carriers/cat-carriers/cat-slings) range uses a slightly different support shape suited to how cats prefer to sit or curl up.

### What to Look For

- **A wide, padded strap rather than a thin one.** All the weight runs through this single strap, so a narrow one will dig in far faster than a properly padded design.
- **Breathable fabric against your pet's body**, since they're held close to you with limited airflow compared with an open carrier.
- **An adjustable strap length**, so the sling sits at a comfortable height for your own build rather than one fixed position.
- **A secure closure or zip opening**, so a wriggly pet can't slip out unexpectedly mid-carry.

A sling won't suit every pet or every trip, but for a small animal who's happiest held close, it's often the calmest option in this range. Have a look through what's available below, and check the maximum weight guidance on each listing carefully, since slings are generally rated for lighter pets than a backpack or hand-held carrier.

faqs.question: What size pet is a sling suitable for?
faqs.answer: Slings are generally rated for smaller, lighter pets, typically puppies, kittens, cats and small dog breeds. Check the specific weight limit on each listing, since this varies more between sling products than with other carrier styles.

faqs.question: Which shoulder should the sling sit on?
faqs.answer: Most slings are designed to be worn across the body, with the strap over one shoulder and the pouch resting at your opposite hip, though some can be adjusted to either side depending on your preference.

faqs.question: Can a sling be used for a wriggly pet?
faqs.answer: Slings work best for pets who are used to being handled and tend to settle once held close. A pet who consistently tries to climb out may be better suited to a fully enclosed carrier with a secure zip.

faqs.question: Are slings suitable for puppies?
faqs.answer: Yes, many owners use a sling specifically for young puppies who are still adjusting to new environments, since being held close against you is often a comfortable option at that age.

faqs.question: How do I clean a sling carrier?
faqs.answer: Most slings have a removable, washable liner or panel. Check the specific care label on the product, since materials vary between machine washable fabric and options that need hand washing.

carriers/pet-sling-carriers.why_choose:
The appeal of a sling comes down almost entirely to closeness. A pet held snugly against a warm, moving body tends to feel calmer than one sitting inside a rigid carrier a little further away, which is exactly why slings tend to be the first choice for nervous pets and young animals on shorter trips.

That closeness comes with a trade-off worth being upfront about: all the weight runs through a single strap rather than being distributed, so slings suit shorter outings more than long walks, and they give a pet less room to shift position than an open carrier does.
carriers/pet-sling-carriers.sizing_guide: Check the specific weight limit on each listing carefully, since slings are generally rated for lighter pets and this varies more between products than with other formats. Adjust the strap length to sit comfortably at your own height, and look for a secure closure or internal safety tether if your pet tends to wriggle when held.

carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers.meta_title: Hard-Sided Pet Carriers for Extra Protection
carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers.meta_description: Durable hard-sided carriers offering extra protection for dogs, cats and small pets. Ideal for car travel and vet visits.
carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers.intro:
A hard-sided carrier keeps its shape no matter how it's handled, thanks to a rigid outer shell rather than fabric walls that flex and fold. That structure matters most when a carrier is being lifted in and out of a car boot, stacked with other luggage, or carried through a busy space where a bump or a knock is genuinely likely. Where a soft-sided bag can crumple under pressure, a hard-sided carrier holds its internal space steady, keeping your pet in a stable, unchanging space throughout the journey.

### Who This Is Best For

This construction tends to suit pets travelling regularly by car, owners who need to stack a carrier alongside other luggage without worrying about it losing shape, and anyone whose pet is prone to pawing or scratching at the sides, since a rigid shell holds up better to that than fabric does over time. It's also a sensible choice if your pet does better in a slightly firmer, more contained space rather than one that shifts as they move. Our [hard-sided cat carrier](/carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-carriers) range is built to this same rigid-shell design, sized specifically for cats rather than larger dogs.

### What to Look For

- **Impact resistance of the shell material.** Better hard-sided carriers use a moulded plastic that flexes slightly under pressure rather than cracking outright.
- **Ventilation built into the shell itself**, usually as grille panels on multiple sides, since a solid shell needs deliberately engineered airflow that fabric carriers get more naturally.
- **Easy-clean interior surfaces.** One advantage of a hard shell is that it wipes down properly rather than needing a full wash, worth checking on the specific product.
- **Secure clip or latch fastenings** rather than a simple zip, since these tend to hold up better under repeated use.

If durability and a stable shape matter more to you than folding the carrier flat for storage, this is the range to start with. Browse the options below, and check the ventilation panel layout on each one, since airflow is the detail hard-sided designs most often get wrong if it hasn't been properly thought through.

faqs.question: Are hard-sided carriers heavier than soft-sided ones?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since the rigid shell adds weight compared with fabric construction. This is usually worth it for the extra protection and structure, particularly for car travel, but it's a fair trade-off to weigh up against a lighter soft-sided option.

faqs.question: Do hard-sided carriers fold flat for storage?
faqs.answer: Most don't fold in the way soft-sided carriers do, since the rigid shell is what gives them their strength. Some do split into a top and bottom half for flatter storage, worth checking on the individual listing.

faqs.question: Are hard-sided carriers better for nervous pets?
faqs.answer: This depends on the individual pet. Some feel more settled in a solid, enclosed shell, while others prefer the softer give of fabric sides. If you're unsure, check the ventilation and interior space of each option carefully.

faqs.question: Can a hard-sided carrier go in a car boot?
faqs.answer: Yes, the rigid shape generally makes hard-sided carriers well suited to stacking or wedging securely in a boot alongside other luggage, more so than a soft-sided bag that can shift shape.

faqs.question: How do I clean a hard-sided carrier?
faqs.answer: Most hard shells wipe down easily with a damp cloth, one of the format's main practical advantages. Check the specific product listing for any material-specific cleaning guidance.

carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers.why_choose:
A rigid shell keeps its shape regardless of how a carrier is handled, which matters most when it's lifted in and out of a car boot, stacked with other luggage, or carried through a busy space where a knock is genuinely likely. Where a soft-sided bag can flex under pressure, a hard-sided carrier holds your pet's space stable and unchanging throughout the journey.

This construction also suits a pet who paws or scratches at the sides more than fabric does over time, and it's a sensible choice if your pet seems to prefer a firmer, more contained feel rather than a space that shifts slightly as they move.
carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your pet's length and height and check these against the shell's internal dimensions, allowing enough room to stand, turn around and lie down comfortably. Because the shell doesn't flex the way soft-sided fabric does, there's less margin for a snug fit to feel forgiving, so err toward the more generous end of your measurements.

carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers.meta_description: Lightweight, comfortable soft-sided carriers for dogs, cats and small pets. Easy to fold and store between trips.
carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers.intro:
A soft-sided carrier is built from fabric over a light internal frame rather than a rigid shell, which keeps the overall weight down and lets the carrier fold flat when it's not in use. That flexibility makes it easy to store in a cupboard between trips or squeeze into a car boot alongside other luggage, and the give in the material tends to feel a little gentler against a pet who presses or leans against the sides. It's the format most owners reach for when a carrier needs to earn its place in daily life rather than sit unused most of the time.

### Who This Is Best For

Soft-sided carriers suit pets who are already comfortable with handling and don't need the extra structure of a hard shell, and owners who want something lightweight enough to carry all day without adding noticeable bulk. They're a strong option for regular, shorter trips such as vet visits or car journeys, where a carrier needs to be picked up, used, and put away again with minimal fuss. Our [soft-sided cat carrier](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range is shaped specifically around cats, with a slightly lower profile and softer internal padding suited to how most cats prefer to sit.

### What to Look For

- **A supportive internal frame**, even in a soft-sided design, so the carrier holds its shape reasonably well when lifted rather than sagging around your pet.
- **A machine-washable or wipeable liner**, since fabric carriers need a proper clean more often than hard-sided ones.
- **Mesh panelling on at least two sides** for airflow, ideally positioned so your pet can see out without feeling too exposed.
- **Reinforced stitching at stress points** such as the handle and strap joins, usually where a soft carrier wears out first.

For everyday use where weight and easy storage matter more than maximum rigidity, a soft-sided carrier is usually the more practical choice. Have a browse through the range below, and check the liner material and stitching details on each listing, since that's generally where the better-made options separate themselves from the rest.

faqs.question: Are soft-sided carriers durable enough for regular use?
faqs.answer: Yes, most are built with reinforced stitching at the main stress points such as handles and strap joins, designed to hold up to frequent everyday use rather than occasional trips.

faqs.question: Can soft-sided carriers be washed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable liner that can be machine washed, with the outer shell wiped clean separately. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page first.

faqs.question: Do soft-sided carriers provide enough protection in a car?
faqs.answer: They provide a secure, enclosed space but less rigid protection than a hard-sided carrier. If car travel is your main use, our pet car travel carriers range covers options built specifically with that in mind.

faqs.question: How do I know if a soft-sided carrier will hold its shape?
faqs.answer: Look for a listing that mentions an internal frame or reinforced base panel, since this is what stops a soft carrier sagging or collapsing when lifted with your pet inside.

faqs.question: Are soft-sided carriers suitable for small dogs as well as cats?
faqs.answer: Yes, many soft-sided carriers in this range are suitable for both, though it's worth checking the stated weight and dimension limits against your specific pet before ordering.

carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers.why_choose:
For everyday trips such as the vet or a short car journey, a soft-sided carrier strikes a reasonable balance: light enough to carry all day without adding noticeable bulk, but with enough internal support that it doesn't sag or collapse around your pet when lifted. That balance is exactly what to check for when comparing listings.

The give in fabric sides also tends to feel gentler against a pet who presses or leans into the carrier, which some anxious pets do. A rigid shell doesn't flex the same way, so for a pet who does this regularly, the softer material can make a genuine difference.
carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your pet's length and height as with any carrier, then check these against the specific product's internal dimensions rather than the external size alone, since any internal frame or support board takes up some of that space. Look for whether a listing mentions an internal frame or reinforced base panel, since that's what determines whether the carrier holds its shape when lifted with your pet inside.

carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits.meta_title: Pet Carriers for Vet Visits, Secure & Easy-Clean
carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits.meta_description: Secure pet carriers designed for calmer vet trips, for dogs, cats and small animals. Top-loading access for easy handling. Free UK delivery.
carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits.intro:
A trip to the vet is rarely a pet's favourite outing, and the carrier itself plays a bigger part in how that trip goes than most owners expect. A carrier that's easy to get your pet into without a struggle, secure enough that they can't push their way out mid-appointment, and simple for a vet to open from the top rather than posting your pet out through a front-only door, is designed with exactly that kind of visit in mind, rather than being a general-purpose bag pressed into service for the day.

### Who This Is Best For

This range is built around short, occasional vet trips rather than long days out, so it suits any pet with a routine check-up, vaccination, or unplanned appointment ahead. It's especially worth considering for cats and small dogs who tense up at the sight of a carrier, since top access and a calmer, more enclosed design can make the whole experience noticeably less of a battle to manage. For smaller dogs specifically, our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range includes several models suited to quick, secure trips, while our [cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers) range and [small animal carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers) range cover the same short-journey needs for cats, rabbits, and other small pets.

### What to Look For

- **Top-loading access.** A carrier that opens from the top lets a vet lift your pet out gently without the awkward angle of a front-only door, which matters more than it sounds.
- **Secure, easy-to-check zips or latches**, so there's no risk of a pet pushing their way out in a busy waiting room.
- **A wipeable or removable interior liner**, since accidents happen more often on unfamiliar trips and a carrier that's simple to clean afterwards saves a lot of hassle.
- **A more enclosed feel rather than lots of open mesh**, which suits pets who prefer a den-like space over a fully open one.

None of this makes a vet visit anyone's favourite outing, but a well-designed carrier makes the practical side of getting there and back considerably easier. Browse the range below, and if your pet is on the nervier side, look at the calmer, more enclosed designs first rather than the most ventilated ones.

faqs.question: What size carrier do I need for a vet visit?
faqs.answer: Measure your pet's length and height and check this against the product's stated dimensions, leaving enough room for them to stand and turn round comfortably. A carrier that's too snug can make handling harder for the vet as well as your pet.

faqs.question: Why does top-loading access matter for a vet visit?
faqs.answer: It lets a vet lift your pet out gently from above rather than coaxing them through a single front door, which is generally quicker and less fiddly, especially for a cat or small dog reluctant to come out on their own.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for the vet and for car travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, most carriers in this range work well for both. If car travel is your main regular use, it's worth also checking our pet car travel carriers range for options with a seatbelt fixing or non-slip base.

faqs.question: How do I clean a carrier after a vet visit?
faqs.answer: Most carriers here have a removable, washable liner or a wipeable interior. Check the specific product's care instructions, particularly if your pet is prone to accidents when travelling.

faqs.question: Should I cover the carrier on the way to the vet?
faqs.answer: Some owners find a light cover over part of the carrier helps their pet feel more settled during the journey, though this comes down to individual preference. Make sure any cover doesn't block the ventilation panels.

carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits.why_choose:
A trip to the vet is rarely a pet's favourite outing, and the carrier itself plays a bigger part in how that trip goes than most owners expect. A carrier that's easy to get your pet into without a struggle, secure enough they can't push their way out mid-appointment, and simple for a vet to open from the top rather than posting your pet out through a front-only door, is designed with exactly that kind of visit in mind.

A more enclosed feel rather than lots of open mesh also tends to suit pets who prefer a den-like space over a fully open one, which matters more for a nervous pet in an unfamiliar waiting room than it does for everyday use.
carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits.sizing_guide: Measure your pet's length and height and check this against the product's stated dimensions, leaving enough room for them to stand and turn round comfortably. A carrier that's too snug can make handling harder for the vet as well as your pet, so don't size right to the tightest fit that technically works.

carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers.meta_title: Pet Carriers for Car Travel, Safe & Secure
carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers.meta_description: Secure car travel carriers that keep pets safe and steady on the road. Suitable for dogs, cats and small pets.
carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers.intro:
A moving car is one of the less predictable environments a pet will experience: sudden braking, cornering, and general road vibration all put a carrier through more real-world stress than almost any other everyday use. A carrier built for car travel is designed to stay upright and secure on the back seat or in the boot, usually with a way to strap or wedge it in place, so your pet isn't sliding around every time you brake at a junction or take a roundabout a little quicker than planned.

### Who This Is Best For

This range suits anyone who regularly drives with a pet, whether that's a daily commute, a school run with the family dog along, or occasional longer journeys to visit family or head off on holiday. It's particularly worth considering if you've previously used a carrier that slides around on the seat or tips over on a corner, since a properly secured carrier removes that problem rather than just easing it. For dogs specifically, our [dog car carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers) range includes options built with integrated seatbelt loops and a wider, more stable base for exactly this kind of use.

### What to Look For

- **A seatbelt loop or fixing point**, so the carrier can be properly secured rather than just sat on the seat and hoped for the best.
- **A wide, stable base** that resists tipping on corners, particularly important for taller carriers.
- **Non-slip feet or a rubberised underside**, which stops the carrier sliding around on a smooth boot liner or leather seat.
- **Easy-clean materials**, since car journeys are where accidents and muddy paws are most likely to end up on the carrier itself.

If your pet travels by car more than the odd occasion, a properly secured carrier is worth the investment over a standard bag balanced on the seat. Browse the range below, and check how each one attaches to your car, whether that's a seatbelt loop, a boot-specific shape, or both, before deciding which fits your usual journeys best.

faqs.question: Do I need to secure the carrier with a seatbelt?
faqs.answer: It's strongly recommended where the carrier has a seatbelt loop or fixing point, since this keeps it from sliding or tipping under braking or cornering. Check each product listing for its specific fixing method.

faqs.question: Can I put the carrier in the boot instead of the back seat?
faqs.answer: Yes, many carriers in this range are suitable for either, though a wider, stable base matters more in a boot where there's no seatbelt to help secure it in place.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a car travel carrier and a regular carrier?
faqs.answer: Car travel carriers typically have a wider base, non-slip feet, and a fixing point such as a seatbelt loop, all aimed at keeping the carrier stable specifically inside a moving vehicle.

faqs.question: Are car booster seats included in this range?
faqs.answer: Yes, alongside enclosed carriers, this range also includes booster-style car seats for dogs who are happier sitting upright and secured by harness rather than fully enclosed.

faqs.question: How do I clean the carrier after a messy journey?
faqs.answer: Most car travel carriers have a wipeable base or a removable liner, worth checking on the individual listing if muddy paws or travel sickness are a regular concern.

carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers.why_choose:
A moving car is one of the less predictable environments a pet will experience, sudden braking, cornering and general road vibration all put a carrier through more real-world stress than almost any other everyday use. A carrier built for car travel stays upright and secure on the back seat or in the boot, usually with a way to strap or wedge it in place, so your pet isn't sliding around every time you brake at a junction.

Easy-clean materials matter more here than for most other carrier types too, since car journeys are where accidents and muddy paws are most likely to end up on the carrier itself.
carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your pet as you would for any carrier, then check the carrier's external dimensions against your actual car, not just your pet, since a correctly sized carrier can still be awkward to fit in a smaller boot or narrow back seat. If the carrier will be secured with a seatbelt, check exactly how the fixing works before buying.

carriers/everyday-pet-carriers.meta_title: Everyday Pet Carriers for Dogs & Cats
carriers/everyday-pet-carriers.meta_description: Practical, comfortable everyday carriers for regular trips out with your pet. Shop dog and cat carriers built for daily use.
carriers/everyday-pet-carriers.intro:
Most trips out with a pet aren't a flight, a hike, or a dash to the vet, they're the ordinary stuff: a short walk to the shops, a visit to a friend's house, or a quick errand where your pet comes along rather than staying home. An everyday carrier is built around exactly that kind of regular, unremarkable use: light enough to grab on the way out, simple enough to get your pet into quickly, and sturdy enough to handle being used several times a week without falling apart.

### Who This Is Best For

This range suits owners who use a carrier often rather than occasionally, where the priorities shift from specialist features towards general reliability, comfort and ease of use. It's a sensible starting point if you're buying your first carrier and aren't yet sure which specialist style, such as a backpack or sling, will suit your routine best. Our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range covers a good spread of everyday-friendly options sized for smaller breeds, and if you'd prefer something lighter and easier to fold away between uses, our [soft-sided pet carriers](/carriers/pet-soft-sided-carriers) range is generally the more practical everyday choice over a rigid shell.

### What to Look For

- **A manageable weight when empty**, since you'll be carrying both the pet and the carrier itself on a regular basis.
- **A shoulder strap and carry handle together**, so you can switch grip on a longer errand rather than being stuck with one option.
- **Simple, quick-access closures**, ideally something you can open and close one-handed while managing a lead or shopping bags.
- **Durable, easy-clean fabric** that can handle frequent use without the seams or zips wearing out within a few months.

An everyday carrier doesn't need to do everything brilliantly, it just needs to do the basics reliably, trip after trip. Have a browse through the range below, and if you're weighing this up against a more specialist style, our buying guide further down this page runs through how the everyday range compares to backpack, sling and hard-sided options.

faqs.question: What makes a carrier suitable for everyday use?
faqs.answer: Generally a manageable weight, a simple one-handed closure, and fabric that holds up to frequent use without the stitching or zips wearing out quickly. This range is curated with exactly those priorities in mind.

faqs.question: Is an everyday carrier suitable for vet visits too?
faqs.answer: Yes, most carriers in this range work perfectly well for the occasional vet visit as well as regular outings, though if that's your main use, our pet carriers for vet visits range is designed more specifically around it.

faqs.question: How long should an everyday carrier last?
faqs.answer: These carriers are built for frequent use, but like any product, lifespan depends on care and how often it's used. Reinforced stitching at handles and strap joins is the main thing to check for longevity.

faqs.question: Should I choose a backpack, sling or everyday carrier?
faqs.answer: It depends on your usual trips. An everyday carrier is the flexible middle ground, while a backpack suits longer walks and a sling suits pets who prefer close contact on shorter trips.

faqs.question: Are everyday carriers suitable for small dogs?
faqs.answer: Yes, this range includes plenty of options sized for small dog breeds, alongside cats and other small pets. Check the individual size and weight guidance on each listing.

carriers/everyday-pet-carriers.why_choose:
An everyday carrier doesn't need to do everything brilliantly, it just needs to do the basics reliably, trip after trip: a manageable weight, a closure you can operate one-handed while managing a lead or shopping bags, and fabric that holds up to frequent use without the stitching or zips wearing out within a few months.

Because this range gets used more often than a specialist carrier might, durability at the handle and strap joins matters more here than headline features, since that's usually where regular use shows up first.
carriers/everyday-pet-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your pet's length, height and width as with any carrier, and check the maximum weight capacity against their actual current weight. Since this range is built for frequent use rather than one specific journey type, err toward a carrier with a little extra room rather than the tightest fit that technically works, so it stays comfortable across a range of everyday trips.

carriers/dog-carriers/airline-approved-d.intro:
Flying with a dog means working to your airline's own cabin rules, not just a general sense of what counts as small enough. This range includes carriers built to a specific IATA-style spec as well as soft-sided designs with a reinforced frame that holds its shape properly while still compressing slightly to fit under an economy seat, both aimed at meeting that kind of check rather than just looking about the right size.

### Structure Without Bulk

A carrier for cabin travel needs to be rigid enough to hold its shape when handled at check-in and boarding, but not so structured that it can't slide under the seat in front of you. Several carriers here use a reinforced internal frame under soft fabric sides to strike that balance, giving your dog a stable space without the bulk of a fully hard shell.

### Confirm With Your Airline First

Airlines set their own maximum dimensions and combined pet-and-carrier weight limits, and these genuinely differ between carriers, sometimes significantly. Always check your specific airline's current published pet policy and confirmed dimensions before booking, rather than assuming a carrier described as "airline approved" will automatically be accepted by every airline. Our blog post on [flying with a pet](/blog/flying-with-your-pet-what-uk-airlines-expect) covers what UK airlines typically expect in more detail.

### The Bigger Picture

For the full range of cabin-friendly designs across every pet we carry, not just dogs, see our [airline approved pet carriers](/carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers) collection.
carriers/dog-carriers/airline-approved-d.why_choose:
Getting this category right before you fly avoids one of the more stressful ways a trip can go wrong: arriving at check-in with a carrier that looks about right but doesn't actually meet the airline's specific dimensions or weight allowance. A carrier built and listed against a clear spec removes most of that uncertainty, provided you've still checked it against your own airline's current rules rather than assuming the label alone is enough.

Ventilation and a secure closure both matter more on a flight than on most other journeys, since your dog will be in the carrier for the full duration with limited opportunity to be let out. Mesh panelling on multiple sides and a lockable zip are both worth checking for specifically with cabin travel in mind.
carriers/dog-carriers/airline-approved-d.sizing_guide: Start with your airline's own published maximum external dimensions and combined weight limit, since these vary between airlines and are the figures that actually matter at check-in, not a general "cabin size" claim. Measure your dog and compare their weight against the airline's combined pet-and-carrier limit specifically, since carrier weight is often included in that figure. Check the carrier's height in particular, since this is usually the dimension that determines whether it slides under the seat in front of you without difficulty.

faqs.question: Will this carrier definitely be accepted by my airline?
faqs.answer: Airlines set their own size and weight limits, which can differ even between two carriers with similar dimensions. Always check your specific airline's current pet policy before you fly, since policies do change from time to time.

faqs.question: Can my dog travel in the cabin with me?
faqs.answer: This depends on your airline's own pet policy, your dog's weight, and the destination's import rules, not on the carrier alone. Contact your airline directly to confirm eligibility, ideally as early as possible since cabin space for pets is often limited.

faqs.question: Does the carrier need to fit fully under the seat?
faqs.answer: Yes, in almost all cases. Crew will typically ask to see the carrier slide fully under the seat in front of you before take-off, so check the carrier's height as well as its footprint against your airline's limits.

faqs.question: What does IATA approved mean?
faqs.answer: It means the carrier is built to a set of guidelines published by the International Air Transport Association covering size, ventilation and construction. Meeting these guidelines is a good starting point, but individual airlines can still apply their own additional rules.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for car journeys and vet visits too?
faqs.answer: Yes, most airline approved carriers work equally well for car travel and vet appointments thanks to their structured shape and secure closures, alongside meeting cabin size requirements.

carriers/cat-carriers/airline-approved-c.intro:
Cabin travel with a cat comes down to your airline's own published size and weight limits, not a general sense of what counts as small enough. Carriers in this range are built to slide under an economy seat, with mesh panelling for airflow and a secure zip closure, but it's worth treating "airline approved" as a starting point for checking your specific airline rather than a guarantee on its own.

### What Tends to Matter Most at Check-In

Height is usually the dimension that decides whether a carrier slides under the seat in front of you without a fight, more so than length or width in most cases. A zip closure on both sides makes it easier to get a nervous cat in without a struggle at the gate, and mesh panelling on the top and sides keeps air moving during what can be a long, warm wait before boarding.

### Confirm Before You Book

Airlines set their own rules on carrier dimensions, combined pet-and-carrier weight, and how many pets are allowed in the cabin per flight, and these can change. Always check your specific airline's current policy directly before booking. Our blog post on [flying with a pet](/blog/flying-with-your-pet-what-uk-airlines-expect) covers what UK airlines typically expect in more detail.

### The Wider Range

For cabin-friendly designs across every pet we carry, not just cats, see our [airline approved pet carriers](/carriers/pet-airline-approved-carriers) collection.
carriers/cat-carriers/airline-approved-c.why_choose:
A carrier built and listed against cabin travel in mind removes a lot of the guesswork at check-in, provided you've also confirmed the specific dimensions against your own airline's current rules rather than relying on the label alone. Getting this right before you travel avoids one of the more stressful ways a trip can go wrong, arriving at the gate with a carrier that looks about the right size but doesn't actually meet the airline's spec.

Because your cat will likely spend a sustained period inside the carrier during boarding and the flight itself, a secure double-zip closure and mesh panelling on more than one side matter more here than on a shorter, everyday trip.
carriers/cat-carriers/airline-approved-c.sizing_guide: Start with your airline's own published maximum external dimensions and combined pet-and-carrier weight limit, since these are the figures that actually apply at check-in. Measure your cat and weigh them together with the empty carrier to check against that combined limit specifically. Pay particular attention to the carrier's height, since this is usually what determines whether it fits under the seat in front of you without needing to be forced.

faqs.question: Will this carrier definitely be accepted by my airline?
faqs.answer: Airlines set their own size and weight limits, which can differ even between carriers with similar dimensions. Always check your specific airline's current pet policy before you fly, since policies do change from time to time.

faqs.question: Can my cat travel in the cabin with me?
faqs.answer: This depends on your airline's own pet policy, your cat's weight, and the destination's import rules, not on the carrier alone. Contact your airline directly to confirm eligibility as early as possible, since cabin space for pets is often limited.

faqs.question: Does the carrier need to fit fully under the seat?
faqs.answer: Yes, in almost all cases. Crew will typically ask to see the carrier slide fully under the seat in front of you before take-off, so check the carrier's height as well as its footprint against your airline's limits.

faqs.question: How do I keep my cat calm during a flight in a carrier?
faqs.answer: Getting your cat used to the carrier well before travel day helps considerably. A light cover over part of the carrier can also help some cats feel calmer, provided it doesn't block the ventilation panels.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for car journeys too?
faqs.answer: Yes, most airline approved cat carriers work well for car travel and vet visits too, thanks to their structured shape and secure closures, alongside meeting cabin size requirements.

carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carri.intro:
A dog backpack carrier moves the weight of your dog onto both shoulders rather than one, using padded straps (and on some designs, a waist or chest strap) the same way a hiking rucksack does. That's the main reason owners move to a backpack once a trip stops being a five-minute errand and turns into a proper outing: a sling or hand-held bag that's perfectly comfortable for twenty minutes can start to feel like hard work well before an hour is up.

### Head-Out or Fully Enclosed

Two general styles show up in this range. Some backpacks use a drawstring or elastic opening that lets your dog's head and front legs stay out the top, giving them a clear view and plenty of airflow, with an inner safety hook that clips to their collar so they can't climb out further than intended. Others are fully enclosed with mesh side panels, which suits a dog who's happier a bit more contained or who isn't keen on a lot of open air rushing past. Neither is objectively better, it comes down to how your own dog reacts to being out in the open versus tucked away.

### Longer Trips and Hiking

If your usual outings run to genuine distance rather than a walk around the block, it's worth checking our [hiking dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/hiking-dog-carriers) range too, which covers backpack-style carriers built with longer, more technical routes specifically in mind. If your outings are on two wheels rather than on foot, our [dog bike carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-bike-carriers) range is built for that different kind of movement instead.

### If Your Dog Is Still Growing

A backpack frame is built around a fairly specific weight range, so a young puppy who hasn't reached their adult size yet may be better served in the meantime by our [puppy carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers) range, sized more closely to where they are now rather than where they'll end up.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carri.why_choose:
The comfort of a backpack carrier over a longer walk comes down almost entirely to weight distribution. Splitting the load across both shoulders, and ideally a hip or chest strap too, means no single point on your body is carrying the full weight for the whole trip, which is the difference between an hour being comfortable and an hour being something you're counting down.

Because the carrier sits against your back, ventilation matters more here than on a stationary carrier, since body heat from both you and your dog builds up in that space. Mesh panelling positioned around the pet compartment, rather than just at the very top, makes a genuine difference on warmer days or longer routes.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carri.sizing_guide: Check the maximum weight rating first, since backpack frames and their straps are only built to carry so much before the stitching and support genuinely come under strain, and this figure matters more here than for a hand-held carrier. Then check the internal compartment dimensions against your dog's actual size, particularly if you're considering a head-out design, since your dog needs to be able to sit or stand comfortably with their head clear of the opening without slumping or being cramped. If you're between two sizes, sizing up generally gives more room for your dog to shift position on a longer walk, which matters more here than on a short trip.

faqs.question: How much weight can a dog backpack carrier hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed on the individual listing. Always check this against your dog's actual current weight, since backpack frames and straps are only rated to carry so much safely.

faqs.question: Is a head-out or fully enclosed backpack better for my dog?
faqs.answer: It depends on your dog's temperament. A head-out design suits a dog who likes to see what's going on and enjoys the airflow, while a fully enclosed design with mesh panels suits a dog who feels calmer a little more contained.

faqs.question: Can I use a dog backpack carrier for hiking?
faqs.answer: Yes, backpack carriers are one of the more practical formats for hiking thanks to the hands-free design and weight distribution. For longer or more technical routes, our hiking dog carriers range is also worth a look.

faqs.question: How should my dog sit inside a backpack carrier?
faqs.answer: Your dog should be able to sit or stand without their head pressing against the top of the opening, with an inner safety clip attached to their collar so they can't climb out mid-walk. Check the specific product for its internal height before buying.

faqs.question: Can a puppy travel in a backpack carrier?
faqs.answer: It depends on their current size relative to the carrier's weight and dimension range. A young or still-growing puppy is often better suited to our puppy carriers range in the meantime, moving up to a backpack once they're closer to their adult size.

carriers/cat-carriers/cat-backpack-carri.intro:
A backpack pet carrier for cats, whether you call it a cat backpack carrier or a cat carrier backpack, suits cats who are happy to be out and about for longer than a quick trip allows: a walk, a longer car journey with stops, or simply wanting both hands free. Several designs in this range are worn on the front rather than the back, keeping your cat closer to you and easier to keep an eye on, which tends to suit a backpack cat carrier better than a traditional rear-worn hiking-style backpack.

### Front-Worn vs Back-Worn

A front-worn design keeps your cat visible and close to your chest, which many cats find more reassuring than being carried behind you out of sight. It's generally the better starting point for a cat backpack carrier than a back-worn one, since most cats are more sensitive to feeling out of control of their surroundings than dogs tend to be.

### Ventilation and Security

Look for ventilated mesh panels around the compartment and an internal safety strap or buckle, since your cat is riding close to your body for a sustained period rather than a brief carry. A reinforced bottom panel also helps a cat carrier backpack keep its shape rather than sagging as you move.

### Sizing, Including Larger Cats

Most designs here suit an average-sized cat comfortably, but if you need a cat carrier backpack large enough for a bigger breed, check the internal compartment dimensions and maximum weight rating carefully before buying, or take a look at our [large cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/large-cat-carriers) range if a backpack format turns out to be too snug.

### Comparing the Format More Widely

For the same hands-free format across every pet we carry, our [pet backpack carriers](/carriers/pet-backpack-carriers) range covers backpack-style carriers more broadly, and if you're weighing this up against a closer-contact option, our [cat slings](/carriers/cat-carriers/cat-slings) range covers that alternative for shorter trips.
carriers/cat-carriers/cat-backpack-carri.why_choose:
A backpack pet carrier for cats works well mainly because it frees up both your hands while still keeping your cat close and visible, particularly with a front-worn cat backpack carrier. That visibility matters more for cats than it does for many dogs, since a cat who can't see you or gauge what's happening around them is more likely to become unsettled during a longer outing.

Ventilation deserves particular attention with any backpack cat carrier, since your cat is held against your body for a sustained period rather than a brief carry, and body heat from both of you builds up in that enclosed space. Mesh panelling positioned around the compartment, not just at the top, makes a real difference on a longer trip.
carriers/cat-carriers/cat-backpack-carri.sizing_guide: Check the maximum weight rating first, since backpack straps and the internal structure are only built to carry so much comfortably, and compare it against your cat's actual current weight. Then check the internal compartment dimensions, making sure your cat can sit or turn without pressing against the top or sides. If you specifically need a cat carrier backpack large enough for a bigger cat, prioritise those dimensions over the design you like the look of, since a cramped fit becomes more noticeable to a cat the longer they're inside. A front-worn design generally suits a cat better than a back-worn one, so factor that into your choice alongside the size itself.

faqs.question: Is a front-worn or back-worn backpack better for a cat?
faqs.answer: Front-worn carriers keep your cat closer and in view, which most cats find more reassuring than being carried behind you where they can't see you.

faqs.question: How much weight can a cat backpack carrier hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed on the individual listing. Always check this against your cat's actual current weight, since the straps and structure are only rated to carry so much safely.

faqs.question: Is there a cat carrier backpack large enough for a bigger cat?
faqs.answer: Some designs in this range suit larger cats, but always check the internal dimensions and maximum weight rating first. If your cat is on the larger side, our large cat carriers range may give a better fit than a backpack format.

faqs.question: Can a backpack pet carrier for cats be used for travel as well as walks?
faqs.answer: Yes, many owners use them for both. Check the ventilation and internal safety strap carefully if you'll be using it for longer trips.

faqs.question: How is a cat backpack carrier different from a cat sling?
faqs.answer: A backpack distributes weight and gives your cat more room to move, suiting longer outings, while a sling holds your cat closer against you on one shoulder, which some cats find more reassuring for shorter trips.

carriers/dog-carriers/rolling-dog-carrie.intro:
Choosing the right rolling dog carrier makes a real difference, especially for dogs who are more comfortable wheeled than carried. This category brings together options suited to exactly that, so you can compare like for like rather than sifting through everything at once.

A well-chosen rolling dog carrier should feel secure without feeling restrictive. That balance matters more than it might seem: too loose and your pet can feel unsteady, too tight and even short trips become uncomfortable. We've kept that balance in mind when curating this range.

Have a browse below. We've also put together a short buying guide and some frequently asked questions further down the page if you want more detail before deciding.

For the wider range of wheeled designs across all pets, see our [pet carriers with wheels](/carriers/pet-rolling-carriers) collection.
carriers/dog-carriers/rolling-dog-carrie.why_choose:
Not every dog enjoys being carried, and not every owner wants to hold onto several kilograms of dog for an entire afternoon. A rolling carrier solves both problems: your dog still travels enclosed and secure, but the weight runs along the ground on wheels rather than through your arms or shoulders. It's particularly useful over longer distances like an airport concourse or a train platform, where swapping a heavy carrier from hand to hand quickly gets tiring.

It's also a genuine help for owners managing a bad back or simply a lot of luggage at the same time as a dog, and for older or heavier dogs who are happy to sit rather than walk for an entire journey but are too big to comfortably carry by hand.
carriers/dog-carriers/rolling-dog-carrie.sizing_guide: Measure your dog as you would for any carrier and check this against the compartment's internal dimensions, but also check the wheel base and telescopic handle height suit how you'll actually be using it, since a rolling carrier's practicality depends as much on the wheels and handle as the internal space. Check the total weight capacity including the carrier's own weight, since a wheeled unit is naturally heavier than an equivalent soft-sided bag before your dog even gets in.

faqs.question: How much weight can a rolling dog carrier hold?
faqs.answer: This is listed individually on each product and includes both your dog's weight and anything else you might be carrying inside. Check the stated capacity carefully.

faqs.question: Are rolling carriers allowed on planes?
faqs.answer: Some are, depending on their folded dimensions and your airline's specific policy, though many rolling carriers are designed primarily for ground transport such as airports and train stations. Check our airline approved dog carriers range if cabin travel is your main need.

faqs.question: Do the wheels work on rough ground?
faqs.answer: This depends on the wheel size and material, which varies between products. Larger, rubberised wheels generally cope better with gravel or uneven pavements than small hard plastic castors.

faqs.question: Can the handle be adjusted for height?
faqs.answer: Many rolling carriers have a telescopic handle with two or three height settings, though this is worth checking on the individual product page since it varies by model.

faqs.question: Is a rolling carrier heavier than a standard one?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally. The wheels, axle and reinforced base add weight compared with an equivalent soft-sided bag, worth factoring in if you'll sometimes need to carry it without rolling it.

carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings.intro:
A dog sling holds your dog close against your body on a single wide strap worn across one shoulder or across the chest, rather than in a separate compartment held out in front of you. For a small, lighter dog, that closeness tends to be genuinely reassuring: being held snugly against a warm, moving body generally feels calmer than sitting inside a carrier a little further away, particularly for a dog who's naturally a bit anxious about travel.

### What to Look For in the Strap

Since all the weight runs through a single strap rather than being distributed the way a backpack does, the strap itself matters more here than on almost any other carrier format. A wide, padded strap in a breathable fabric spreads pressure across your shoulder properly, while a narrow one will start to dig in fairly quickly, especially on a longer trip. Several slings in this range also include a safety tether or clip that attaches to your dog's collar, which is worth checking for regardless of your dog's temperament.

### Best Suited To

Slings work best for smaller, lighter dogs, and particularly well for puppies who are still getting used to the world. If your household includes a very young puppy specifically, our [puppy slings](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-slings) range uses a slightly different support shape suited to how young puppies prefer to be held compared with an adult small dog.

### When a Sling Isn't the Right Fit

Because the weight sits on one side of your body, slings aren't really built for long walks the way a backpack is, and they're not the best choice for a dog who wriggles a lot or tries to climb out. If either of those describes your situation, our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range covers more enclosed, structured alternatives at the same size.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings.why_choose:
The appeal of a sling is almost entirely about closeness rather than capacity or features. A dog held snugly against you, with your own body heat and movement close by, often settles faster than one placed inside a rigid box a little further from you, which is exactly why slings tend to be the first choice for nervous dogs and young puppies on short trips.

That closeness comes with trade-offs worth being upfront about. A sling puts the full weight on one shoulder rather than spreading it, so it suits shorter outings more than long walks, and it gives a dog less room to shift position than an open carrier does, which matters for a dog who doesn't like to stay still.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings.sizing_guide: Slings are generally rated for lighter dogs than a backpack or standard carrier, so check the specific weight limit on each listing carefully, since this varies more between sling products than it does with other formats. Beyond weight, check the strap's adjustable length range against your own height, since a sling worn at the wrong height can feel awkward regardless of how well it fits your dog. If your dog tends to wriggle when held, look for a design with a secure closure and an internal safety tether rather than relying on the strap alone to keep them settled.

faqs.question: What size dog is a sling suitable for?
faqs.answer: Slings generally suit smaller, lighter dogs. Check the specific weight limit on each listing, since this varies more between sling products than with other carrier styles, and it's usually the deciding factor.

faqs.question: Which shoulder should a dog sling be worn on?
faqs.answer: Most slings are worn across the body with the strap over one shoulder and the pouch resting at your opposite hip, though some designs can be adjusted to either side depending on preference.

faqs.question: Are dog slings suitable for puppies?
faqs.answer: Yes, many owners use a sling specifically for young puppies who are still adjusting to new environments. Our puppy slings range is shaped a little differently to suit how very young puppies prefer to be held.

faqs.question: Can a sling be used for a wriggly dog?
faqs.answer: Slings work best for dogs already used to being handled who tend to settle once held close. A dog who consistently tries to climb out may be better suited to a more enclosed carrier with a secure zip.

faqs.question: How is a sling different from a backpack carrier?
faqs.answer: A sling holds your dog close on one shoulder, which suits shorter trips and dogs who want contact, while a backpack spreads weight across both shoulders, making it more comfortable over a longer walk.

carriers/cat-carriers/cat-slings.intro:
Most cats aren't natural fans of being carried out in the open, which is part of why a sling, holding your cat close against your body rather than in a compartment out in front of you, tends to suit cats who feel calmer with contact and a bit of gentle pressure around them. Several designs in this range use a double-layer cotton or similarly soft fabric specifically for that close, snug contact, since your cat is held right against you rather than sitting in open space.

### What to Check Before Choosing a Sling

A wide, padded strap matters more for cats than it might seem, since all the weight runs through one point rather than being distributed. An internal safety tether or collar clip is worth looking for too, since it's the main thing stopping a startled cat from pushing free unexpectedly. A breathable fabric matters as well, given your cat is held close with limited airflow compared with an open carrier.

### Not Every Cat Takes to a Sling

Slings suit cats who are already comfortable being handled and held. A cat who tenses up, claws, or tries to twist free is generally better served by a fully enclosed carrier with a secure zip instead. Our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range covers that more contained alternative.

### Comparing Across Pets

For a wider look at this format across every animal we carry, our [pet sling carriers](/carriers/pet-sling-carriers) collection covers slings for dogs, cats and other small pets.
carriers/cat-carriers/cat-slings.why_choose:
The appeal of a sling for a cat comes down almost entirely to contact and pressure. A cat held close against a warm, moving body, with the security of being gently supported rather than sitting freely in an open space, often settles faster than one placed in a rigid carrier a little further away, provided your cat is generally comfortable being handled in the first place.

It's worth being realistic about what a sling isn't built for too. It's not the right choice for a longer trip, since the weight sits on one shoulder rather than being spread, and it's not suited to a cat who wriggles or tries to climb free, since there's less containment than a fully enclosed carrier offers.
carriers/cat-carriers/cat-slings.sizing_guide: Check the specific weight limit on each listing carefully, since slings are generally rated for lighter cats and this varies more between products than with other carrier formats. Adjust the strap to a comfortable length for your own height before your first use, and check the sling has a secure closure or internal safety tether if your cat is prone to wriggling. If your cat regularly tries to climb out, a fully enclosed soft-sided carrier will generally give more reliable containment than persisting with a sling.

faqs.question: Are cat slings suitable for all cats?
faqs.answer: Slings suit cats who are already comfortable being handled and held close. A cat who tenses, claws or tries to twist free is usually better suited to a fully enclosed carrier with a secure zip.

faqs.question: What size cat is a sling suitable for?
faqs.answer: Slings are generally rated for lighter cats. Check the specific weight limit on each listing, since this varies more between sling products than with other carrier styles.

faqs.question: Which shoulder should a cat sling be worn on?
faqs.answer: Most slings are worn across the body with the strap over one shoulder, and can usually be adjusted to either side depending on your preference.

faqs.question: Can a cat sling be used for a vet visit?
faqs.answer: It can for a calm cat used to handling, though our pet carriers for vet visits range includes more enclosed designs that some cats find easier to be examined from directly.

faqs.question: How do I clean a cat sling?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable liner or panel. Check the specific care label on the product, since materials vary between machine washable fabric and options that need hand washing.

carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-car.intro:
A hard-sided cat carrier keeps its shape no matter how it's handled, thanks to a rigid outer shell rather than fabric walls that flex and fold. That structure matters most when a carrier is being lifted in and out of a car boot, stacked with other luggage, or carried through a busy space where a knock is genuinely likely. Where a soft-sided bag can crumple under pressure, a hard-sided carrier holds your cat's space steady and unchanging throughout the journey.

### Who This Construction Suits

A rigid shell tends to suit cats travelling regularly by car, owners who need to stack a carrier alongside other luggage without it losing shape, and any cat prone to pawing or scratching at the sides, since a shell holds up to that better than fabric does over time. It's also worth considering for larger cat breeds, where a rigid structure supports their weight more consistently than a flexible one; our [large cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/large-cat-carriers) range is built with exactly that combination of extra room and sturdier support in mind.

### What to Check For

Look for ventilation built into the shell itself, usually as grille panels on multiple sides, since a solid shell needs deliberately engineered airflow that fabric carriers get more naturally. Secure clip or latch fastenings tend to hold up better under repeated use than a simple zip, and an interior that wipes clean easily is one of the format's main practical advantages over a full wash.

### If You Want Something Lighter

If durability and a stable shape matter less to you than folding the carrier flat for storage, our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range is generally the more practical everyday choice instead. For the wider range of rigid-shell designs across every pet we sell, not just cats, see our [hard-sided pet carriers](/carriers/pet-hard-sided-carriers) collection.
carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-car.why_choose:
A rigid shell holds its shape regardless of how a carrier is handled, which matters most when it's being lifted in and out of a car boot, stacked with other luggage, or carried through a busy space where a knock is genuinely likely. Where a soft-sided bag can flex under pressure, a hard-sided carrier keeps your cat's space stable and unchanging throughout the journey.

This construction also suits a cat who paws or scratches at the sides more than a soft-sided carrier does, since there's no fabric to work at over time. It's a sensible choice too if your cat seems to prefer a firmer, more contained feel over one that shifts slightly as they move inside it.
carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-car.sizing_guide: Measure your cat's length and height as you would for any carrier, then check these against the hard shell's internal dimensions, allowing enough room to stand, turn around and lie down comfortably. Because the shell doesn't flex the way soft-sided fabric does, there's less margin for a snug fit to feel forgiving, so err toward the more generous end of your measurements rather than the tightest fit that technically works.

faqs.question: Are hard-sided cat carriers heavier than soft-sided ones?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since the rigid shell adds weight compared with fabric construction. This is usually worth it for the extra protection and structure, particularly for car travel.

faqs.question: Do hard-sided cat carriers fold flat for storage?
faqs.answer: Most don't fold the way soft-sided carriers do, since the rigid shell is what gives them their strength. Some split into a top and bottom half for flatter storage, worth checking on the individual listing.

faqs.question: Are hard-sided carriers better for nervous cats?
faqs.answer: This depends on the individual cat. Some feel more settled in a solid, enclosed shell, while others prefer the softer give of fabric sides. Check the ventilation and interior space of each option carefully.

faqs.question: Can a hard-sided cat carrier go in a car boot?
faqs.answer: Yes, the rigid shape generally makes hard-sided carriers well suited to stacking or wedging securely in a boot alongside other luggage, more so than a soft-sided bag that can shift shape.

faqs.question: How do I clean a hard-sided cat carrier?
faqs.answer: Most hard shells wipe down easily with a damp cloth, one of the format's main practical advantages. Check the specific product listing for any material-specific cleaning guidance.

carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-car.intro:
