Soft-sided cat carriers use fabric over a light internal frame rather than a rigid shell, which keeps the overall weight down and lets the carrier fold flat when it's not in use. Several designs in this range still use a firm cage structure or a wooden support board underneath the fabric to keep their shape stable in use, so "soft-sided" doesn't mean flimsy, it means the outer material flexes rather than staying rigid.

### What Makes a Soft Carrier Work Well

Mesh panelling on at least two or three sides is standard across this range, giving your cat airflow and a view out without leaving them feeling too exposed. Look for a removable, washable base mat or liner too, since fabric carriers need a proper clean more often than a hard shell, and reinforced stitching at the handle and strap joins, which is usually the first place a soft carrier shows wear.

### If Your Cat Needs Extra Structure

A soft-sided carrier suits a cat who's already comfortable with handling and doesn't need the extra rigidity of a hard shell. If your cat tends to paw or scratch at the sides, or you need something that holds its shape when stacked with other luggage, our [hard-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-carriers) range is built specifically around that firmer construction instead.

### For Kittens

A young kitten often settles well in a soft-sided carrier thanks to the gentler give in the material, and our [kitten carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/kitten-carriers) range covers sizing specific to a smaller, younger cat rather than a scaled-down adult design.
carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-car.why_choose:
For most everyday trips such as the vet or a short car journey, a soft-sided carrier strikes a reasonable balance: light enough to carry all day without adding noticeable bulk, but with enough internal support that it doesn't sag or collapse around your cat when lifted. That balance is exactly what to check for when comparing listings, since a genuinely unsupported soft carrier can feel unstable to a cat inside it.

The give in fabric sides also tends to feel gentler against a cat who presses or leans into the carrier, which some cats do when they're a little anxious. A rigid shell doesn't flex the same way, so for a cat who does this regularly, the softer material can make a genuine difference to how settled they feel.
carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-car.sizing_guide: Measure your cat's length and height as with any carrier, then check these against the specific product's internal dimensions rather than the external size alone, since the frame or support board inside a soft carrier takes up some of that space. Look specifically for whether a listing mentions an internal frame or a reinforced base panel, since that's what determines whether the carrier holds its shape when lifted with your cat inside rather than sagging. If your cat is at the larger end of average, check the weight capacity carefully, since soft-sided construction generally has a lower practical ceiling than a hard shell of a similar size.

faqs.question: Are soft-sided cat carriers sturdy enough for regular use?
faqs.answer: Yes, most are built with an internal frame or support board and reinforced stitching at the main stress points, designed to hold up to frequent use rather than occasional trips.

faqs.question: Can soft-sided cat carriers be washed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable liner or base mat that can be machine washed, with the outer fabric wiped clean separately. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page first.

faqs.question: Do soft-sided carriers give enough protection in a car?
faqs.answer: They provide a secure, enclosed space but less rigid protection than a hard-sided carrier. If car travel is your main use, our pet carriers for car travel range covers options built specifically with that in mind.

faqs.question: How do I know if a soft carrier will hold its shape?
faqs.answer: Look for a listing that mentions an internal frame, wire structure or a reinforced base panel, since this is what stops a soft carrier sagging or collapsing when lifted with your cat inside.

faqs.question: Are soft-sided carriers suitable for larger cats?
faqs.answer: Many are, but it's worth checking the stated weight and dimension limits carefully. For bigger cat breeds specifically, our large cat carriers range is sized with extra room in mind.

carriers/cat-carriers.intro:
Most cats associate a carrier with one thing: the vet. That association alone is often the biggest obstacle to a calm journey, more than the carrier's size or material, which is why the carriers in this range lean toward calmer, more enclosed designs with easy top access rather than the more open, view-focused styles that suit some dogs. A carrier that's simple to get your cat into without a struggle, and simple for a vet to open from above rather than coaxing your cat out of a single front door, tends to make the whole experience noticeably less of a battle.

### Soft-Sided or Hard-Sided

Most cat carriers on the site are soft-sided: lighter, foldable for storage, and generally gentler in feel for a cat who presses against the sides. Our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range covers this construction specifically, our largest cat carrier category after the hub itself. A rigid shell holds its shape better under pressure, such as being stacked with other luggage or handled by a cat prone to pawing at the sides, which is where our [hard-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-carriers) range comes in instead.

### If You Have a Kitten

A young kitten who's still getting used to travel often does better in something sized and shaped specifically for them rather than a smaller version of an adult carrier. Our [kitten carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/kitten-carriers) range is built around exactly that.

### For the Trip Itself

If a vet appointment is what's actually brought you here, our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range picks out the designs best suited to that shorter, calmer kind of trip across every pet we carry, with more detail on what makes a carrier easier for a vet to work with.
carriers/cat-carriers.why_choose:
Cats generally do better in an enclosed, den-like space than an open one, which is the opposite of what tends to work well for some dogs, and it's worth keeping in mind when comparing carriers that look similar on the surface. A carrier with too much open mesh can leave a nervous cat feeling exposed rather than secure, while one with a slightly more contained shape and a smaller, controllable opening tends to help them settle faster.

Top-loading access matters more for cats than almost any other pet, since it avoids the awkward back-and-forth of coaxing a reluctant cat through a single front door. A carrier that opens fully from the top lets you lower your cat in gently, and lets a vet lift them out the same way, rather than turning every entry and exit into a small negotiation.
carriers/cat-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your cat from nose to tail base for length and floor to the top of the head for height, then check these against the product's stated internal dimensions, allowing enough room for your cat to stand, turn around and lie down without pressing against the sides. Most cats feel calmer in a carrier that's snug rather than cavernous, so more space isn't automatically better here, just enough for comfortable movement. Always check the maximum weight capacity too, particularly for larger cat breeds, since this can be the limiting factor even when the dimensions look generous enough by eye.

faqs.question: What size carrier does my cat need?
faqs.answer: Measure your cat's length and height and check this against the product's stated dimensions, leaving enough room to stand and turn around comfortably without being so large that they feel exposed rather than secure.

faqs.question: Why does top-loading access matter for cats?
faqs.answer: It lets you lower your cat in gently and lets a vet lift them out from above, rather than coaxing a reluctant cat through a single front door, which is generally quicker and less stressful for both of you.

faqs.question: Should I choose a soft-sided or hard-sided cat carrier?
faqs.answer: Soft-sided carriers are lighter and fold flat for storage, suiting most everyday trips, while hard-sided carriers offer more protection and structure for regular car travel or a cat prone to pawing at the sides.

faqs.question: How do I get a nervous cat used to a carrier?
faqs.answer: Leaving the carrier out at home for a week or two beforehand, with a blanket inside, generally helps far more than only bringing it out on travel days. See our blog for more detailed tips on settling a nervous cat.

faqs.question: Do you have carriers sized specifically for kittens?
faqs.answer: Yes, our kitten carriers range is sized and shaped around a young cat still getting used to travel, rather than simply being a smaller adult carrier.

carriers/small-animal-carriers.intro:
Small animals don't travel the way dogs and cats do, and lumping them together with a generic "small pet carrier" tends to miss what actually matters for each species. A rabbit needs a solid, non-slip floor to grip rather than a mesh base to hang from. A hamster needs a lid with genuinely no gaps to squeeze through. A guinea pig settles better with hay and familiar bedding close by than with an open view out. This range is organised by species specifically because those differences change what actually makes a good carrier.

### Choosing by Species

Our [rabbit carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-carriers) range is built around a solid base and good ventilation for hopping and settling. [Guinea pig carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pig-carriers) covers a similar solid-floor approach sized for a guinea pig's shorter, wider build. [Hamster carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/hamster-carriers) prioritise secure, gap-free closures above almost anything else, given how determined a hamster can be to find a way out. For a curious, escape-minded pet, our [ferret carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/ferret-carriers) range is built with that in mind specifically, and our [reptile carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/reptile-carriers) range focuses on warmth retention and security rather than open ventilation.

### Common Ground Across This Range

Whatever the species, a few things matter consistently: a base your pet can grip rather than a loose mesh floor, a closure that genuinely holds under determined pushing or pawing, and enough ventilation to stop the inside becoming too warm on a car journey. Beyond that, the specifics vary enough between species that it's worth reading the category for your particular pet rather than shopping this hub generically.

### For a Short Trip Somewhere

If a vet appointment is what's brought you here, our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range covers the shorter, calmer style of carrier across every pet we sell, small animals included.
carriers/small-animal-carriers.why_choose:
Small animals are creatures of routine more than most pets, and travel itself, regardless of the carrier, is usually the unsettling part rather than any single design flaw. What a good carrier can do is reduce the additional stress on top of that: a solid base means your pet isn't also fighting to keep their footing, and familiar bedding inside means the space smells reassuring rather than completely foreign.

Security matters more here than with most dog or cat carriers too, since several small animals, hamsters and ferrets in particular, are genuinely capable of finding and exploiting even a small gap in a closure. A carrier that's fine for a calm rabbit can be entirely inadequate for a determined hamster, which is exactly why this range is split by species rather than just by size.
carriers/small-animal-carriers.sizing_guide: Sizing for small animals is less about matching exact body measurements and more about giving your pet a stable, secure space without excess room they could be thrown around in during transport. For rabbits and guinea pigs, floor space matters more than height, since they don't generally need to stand fully upright but do need to shift position comfortably. For hamsters and other small rodents, a compact, fully secure space is usually more reassuring than a larger one. Always check a product's specific size guidance for your species rather than assuming one small animal carrier suits all of them equally.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for different small animals?
faqs.answer: Some carriers are suitable for a range of small pets, but check the specific product listing, since bedding, ventilation and closure needs vary between species, particularly between rodents and rabbits.

faqs.question: What matters most in a small animal carrier?
faqs.answer: A solid, grippable base, secure ventilation your pet can't push through, and enough room to shift position without excess empty space they could be thrown around in during transport.

faqs.question: How do I keep my small pet calm during a trip?
faqs.answer: Lining the carrier with familiar bedding from their usual home helps considerably, since the smell is reassuring. Our blog has more detailed tips on settling a rabbit or guinea pig for a short trip.

faqs.question: Do small animal carriers need special ventilation?
faqs.answer: Yes, small animals can overheat quickly in a poorly ventilated space, particularly in a warm car. Look for mesh panelling on multiple sides rather than a single small vent.

faqs.question: Do you offer free UK delivery on small animal carriers?
faqs.answer: Yes, orders over £50 qualify for free standard UK shipping, with a small delivery charge shown at checkout for orders under that. We also offer 30-day returns.

carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers.intro:
A moving car puts a carrier through a different kind of stress than carrying it by hand: braking, cornering and general road vibration all act on it constantly rather than briefly. Dog car carriers are built to stay upright and stable through all of that, generally with a wider base than a standard carrier and a fixing point, such as a seatbelt loop, so the carrier is actually secured rather than just sat on the seat and hoped for the best.

### Crate-Style vs Standard Carrier

Several options in this range are built like a compact travel crate: a steel wire or tube frame under fabric, mesh windows on multiple sides, and a design that folds flat when not in use. These tend to suit dogs who travel by car regularly, since the structure holds up well to being loaded in and out repeatedly. Lighter, more standard carriers with a seatbelt attachment can work just as well for occasional journeys, particularly for a smaller dog.

### Placement in the Car

Where the carrier sits matters as much as the carrier itself. A wide, stable base copes better with cornering on the back seat, while the boot generally needs less concern about tipping but more about the carrier sliding around under braking, so non-slip feet or a rubberised base are worth checking either way.

### Bigger Dogs

If your dog is on the larger side, our [large dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers) range includes options built with car travel and general handling both in mind, worth comparing if weight capacity is a bigger factor for you than car-specific fixings alone. For the full picture on secure car travel across every pet we sell, not just dogs, see our [pet carriers for car travel](/carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers) collection.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers.why_choose:
A dog car carrier earns its place by removing the guesswork from what happens the moment you pull away from the kerb. A carrier without a proper fixing point can slide across the seat on a roundabout or tip over under harder braking, which is unsettling for your dog even if nothing actually goes wrong, and repeated unsettling journeys tend to make a dog more anxious about car travel over time rather than less.

Cleaning is worth thinking about here too, more than with other formats, since car journeys are where muddy paws, travel sickness and general mess are most likely to end up on the carrier itself. A removable, washable base mat or a wipeable interior saves a genuine amount of hassle over a carrier that needs a full wash after every messy trip.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your dog as you would for any carrier (length, height and shoulder width), then check these figures alongside the carrier's external dimensions against your actual car, not just your dog, since a correctly sized carrier can still be awkward to fit in a smaller boot or narrow back seat. If the carrier will be secured with a seatbelt, check exactly how the fixing works before buying, since some use a loop that threads through the existing belt while others need a separate strap. For dogs who travel by car often, a wider base generally matters more than extra height, since stability under cornering is usually the bigger practical concern.

faqs.question: Do I need to secure a dog car carrier with a seatbelt?
faqs.answer: It's strongly recommended wherever the carrier has a seatbelt loop or fixing point, since this stops it sliding or tipping under braking or cornering. Check each product listing for its specific fixing method.

faqs.question: Can a dog car carrier go in the boot instead of the back seat?
faqs.answer: Yes, many carriers in this range suit either position, though a wide, stable base matters more in a boot where there's no seatbelt to help hold it in place.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a dog car carrier and a regular carrier?
faqs.answer: Car carriers typically have a wider base, non-slip feet, and a seatbelt loop or similar fixing, all aimed at keeping the carrier stable specifically inside a moving vehicle, rather than being designed primarily for hand-carrying.

faqs.question: How do I clean a dog car carrier after a messy journey?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable base mat or a wipeable liner, worth checking on the individual listing if muddy paws or travel sickness are a regular concern for your dog.

faqs.question: Are these carriers suitable for larger dogs too?
faqs.answer: Some are, though it's worth checking the stated weight capacity carefully. For dogs over around 25kg, our large dog carriers range includes options built with both car travel and higher weight capacities in mind.

carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers.intro:
Small dog carriers are built around dogs up to roughly 10kg, which covers everything from toy breeds to smaller adult dogs of breeds that only reach a modest size. It's also our largest single dog carrier category, which means there's a genuine spread of formats here rather than one design repeated in different colours: soft-sided bags, sling-style carriers, and structured carriers with a supportive base all show up at this size, since a lighter dog opens up more practical options than a heavier one does.

### Choosing Between Formats at This Size

At under 10kg, weight stops being the limiting factor it is for bigger dogs, so the decision usually comes down to how your dog prefers to travel rather than what a carrier can physically support. A dog who likes being held close against you on shorter outings is often happiest in our [dog sling](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings) range, which distributes weight across one shoulder for a more contained, reassuring feel. A dog who's a bit bigger, or a household with a dog just outside this range as they grow, should also check our [medium dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carriers) range for a bit more internal room.

### Getting the Fit Right

Even within a 10kg ceiling, there's a real difference between a 3kg toy breed and an 9kg small dog, and using the actual internal dimensions rather than the category name alone will save you a return. Check that your dog can stand, turn around and lie down without their head or tail pressing against the sides, and don't assume a carrier described as "small dog" will automatically suit every dog under 10kg equally well.

### Other Short Trips

If your main reason for buying is an upcoming vet appointment, our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range picks out the designs with the easiest top access for that specific kind of trip.
carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers.why_choose:
Small dogs are light enough that format becomes a genuine choice rather than a constraint, which is exactly why this category has the widest range of styles on the site. That's useful, but it also means it's worth being deliberate about what you're actually optimising for: a carrier that folds flat for occasional use, one built for a daily walk to the shops, or one that needs to survive being wedged into a car boot regularly are three different briefs even though the dog inside might be exactly the same size in each case.

Small dogs can also be more sensitive to a carrier that doesn't fit properly than larger dogs are, since there's less margin for error in the internal space. A carrier that's a couple of centimetres too tight is a bigger proportional squeeze for a 4kg dog than the same shortfall would be for a 20kg one.
carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog first, since 10kg is the practical ceiling for this category and a dog close to that limit is a genuinely different fit challenge to one at 3kg. Then measure length nose to tail base, height floor to the top of the head or ears, and width across the shoulders, and check all three against the product's stated internal dimensions rather than just the weight limit alone, since a lightweight dog with a long body or tall ears can still be poorly served by a carrier that's technically rated for their weight. Toy and very small breeds generally do better in a snugger, more enclosed carrier, while dogs at the upper end of this range benefit from checking they have genuine room to turn around.

faqs.question: What counts as a small dog for carrier sizing?
faqs.answer: Generally dogs up to around 10kg, though it's worth checking your dog's actual weight and body length against the specific product rather than relying on this figure alone, since build varies a lot between breeds.

faqs.question: Is a sling or a standard carrier better for a small dog?
faqs.answer: A sling suits shorter trips and dogs who prefer being held close against you, while a standard soft-sided carrier gives more room to move and is generally more practical for longer or more frequent outings.

faqs.question: Can a small dog carrier be used for a puppy?
faqs.answer: It depends on your puppy's current size rather than their expected adult size. If they're still noticeably smaller than a 10kg adult dog, our puppy carriers range is built more specifically around a growing puppy's proportions.

faqs.question: How much can a small dog carrier hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed on each individual listing, generally up to around 10kg. Always check the stated capacity rather than assuming based on the category alone.

faqs.question: Are small dog carriers suitable for everyday use?
faqs.answer: Yes, many are designed with frequent use in mind, with durable stitching and simple closures. If daily use is your main priority, look for reinforced stitching at the handle and strap joins when comparing listings.

carriers.intro:
A pet carrier only has one job, but what that job actually requires changes a great deal depending on what you're carrying. A rabbit needs a solid, ventilated base to sit on rather than hang from a mesh floor. A cat generally settles faster in an enclosed, den-like space than an open one. A large dog needs a structure that can genuinely bear their weight without the seams giving way. Rather than one generic range, this is really four ranges in one, split by animal first and then by how you'll actually use the carrier day to day.

### Choosing by Pet

If you already know what you're shopping for, the fastest route is by animal. Our [dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers) range spans puppies through to larger breeds, with carriers organised by both size and format. [Cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers) covers everything from nervous kittens to bigger cat breeds, with a strong emphasis on the calmer, top-loading designs cats generally respond best to. For anything smaller, our [small animal carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers) range covers rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters, ferrets and reptiles, each with quite different ventilation and bedding needs, and [bird carriers](/carriers/bird-carriers) covers budgies, parrots and other pet birds who need somewhere to perch rather than lie down.

### Choosing by How You'll Use It

If you're shopping around a specific trip rather than a specific pet, it's often quicker to start from the journey instead. Our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range is built around short, occasional trips with easy top access, while [pet carriers for car travel](/carriers/pet-car-travel-carriers) focuses on carriers that stay stable and can be properly secured on the back seat or in the boot. If you're buying your first carrier and don't yet know which specialist style will suit your routine, our [everyday pet carriers](/carriers/everyday-pet-carriers) range is a sensible, flexible starting point rather than committing to a specialist format straight away.

### Soft-Sided or Hard-Sided

Beyond animal and use case, most carriers on the site fall into one of two broad constructions. Soft-sided carriers use fabric over a light frame, so they're lighter to carry and fold flat for storage between trips. Hard-sided carriers use a rigid shell that holds its shape under pressure, which matters more for regular car travel or when a carrier gets stacked with other luggage. Neither is universally better, it depends on how often you'll use it and what you'll be doing with it, and the buying guide below goes into this in a bit more detail.
carriers.why_choose:
A carrier that's actually built for your pet's size and species tends to get used properly, rather than becoming the thing that sits half-open in the hallway because your pet won't settle in it. The details that make the difference are usually small: a base that doesn't flex underfoot, a closure that holds under a bit of pressure, ventilation that's actually positioned where your pet can benefit from it rather than just looking like mesh from the outside.

Buying to the specific journey matters just as much as buying to the specific pet. A carrier that's perfect for a five-minute trip to the car can be genuinely uncomfortable on a longer journey, and a carrier built to survive being stacked in a car boot is more structure than most pets need for a quick vet visit. Working out which of those you actually need first narrows the choice considerably.
carriers.sizing_guide: Sizing varies enormously across this range, so there's no single measurement that applies to every pet here, but the underlying method is the same regardless of species: measure your pet at their current size (length nose to tail base, height floor to the top of the head or ears, and width across the shoulders or widest point), then check those figures and the stated weight capacity against the specific product rather than relying on the category name or breed alone. For dogs and cats, a slightly snugger fit is usually more reassuring than a loose one. For rabbits, guinea pigs and other small animals, floor space and a solid, non-mesh base generally matter more than overall height. Each animal-specific category further down this page has more detailed guidance for that pet.

faqs.question: What type of carrier does my pet need?
faqs.answer: It depends mainly on your pet's species and size, and secondarily on how you'll use it. Start with the category for your pet (dog, cat, small animal or bird), then narrow down by format, such as soft-sided, hard-sided, backpack or sling, based on your usual trips.

faqs.question: Do you sell carriers for pets other than dogs and cats?
faqs.answer: Yes, our small animal carriers range covers rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters, ferrets and reptiles, and our bird carriers range covers budgies, parrots and other pet birds, alongside the wider dog and cat ranges.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a soft-sided and hard-sided carrier?
faqs.answer: Soft-sided carriers are lighter and fold flat for storage, while hard-sided carriers use a rigid shell that holds its shape better under pressure, such as being stacked in a car boot. Most everyday trips are well served by a soft-sided carrier.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for different types of trips?
faqs.answer: Many carriers work well across several uses, but a carrier chosen specifically for car travel or vet visits will usually perform better at that particular job than a general-purpose one. Check the relevant use-based category if you have one main type of trip in mind.

faqs.question: Do you offer free UK delivery?
