carriers/dog-carriers.intro:
Dogs come in a wider range of sizes than almost any other pet, which makes the carrier itself do more of the work than it does for other animals: a carrier sized for a 3kg toy breed and one built for a 25kg dog aren't really the same product with different labels, they're built to different structural standards entirely. This range is organised around that reality, split first by size and then by format, so you're comparing carriers actually built for a dog your size rather than scaling a photo up or down in your head.

### Shopping by Size

If you know roughly what your dog weighs, size is the quickest way to narrow things down. Our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range covers dogs up to around 10kg and is our largest single dog category, while carriers for dogs between 10kg and 25kg sit in our medium range, and anything heavier moves into carriers built with a sturdier frame and wider base. If your dog is still a puppy and not yet at their adult weight, our [puppy carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers) range is sized specifically around younger, smaller dogs rather than assuming they'll grow into an adult-sized carrier straight away.

### Shopping by Format

Once size is sorted, format is usually the next decision. For longer walks or hiking, a [dog backpack carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carriers) spreads the weight across both shoulders rather than one. For dogs who settle best held close against you, our [dog slings](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings) range does exactly that on shorter trips. And if your dog mainly travels by car, our [dog car carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers) range is built with a wider base and secure fixings specifically for the back seat or boot.

### Not Sure Where to Start

If you're weighing this up against carriers for other pets too, or want to compare formats across every animal we carry, our [carriers](/carriers) hub covers the full range with a wider buying guide on soft-sided versus hard-sided construction.
carriers/dog-carriers.why_choose:
A carrier sized correctly for your dog's actual weight and build, rather than their breed's average, tends to get used without a fight. Too roomy and a lot of dogs feel less secure moving around inside it; too snug and even a short trip becomes uncomfortable, particularly for a dog who's already a bit unsettled about being carried in the first place.

Format matters just as much as size once the basics are covered. A dog who's happy being held close in a sling for a quick trip to the shops may be a completely different prospect on a two-hour walk, where the weight distribution of a proper backpack carrier makes a real difference to how comfortable the whole outing feels for both of you.
carriers/dog-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your dog from nose to the base of the tail for length, floor to the top of the head or ears (whichever is taller) for height, and across the shoulders for width, then compare these figures against the specific product's stated dimensions rather than assuming a breed name maps neatly onto a size category. Weight matters just as much as the dimensions, since a carrier's frame, straps and stitching are only rated to hold so much safely; check the maximum weight capacity even when the internal space looks generous enough. If your dog is still growing, size for their current weight rather than their expected adult weight, and plan to move up a size category as they grow rather than buying ahead.

faqs.question: How do I know which size category my dog fits into?
faqs.answer: Weigh your dog and measure their length, height and width, then compare these against the specific dimensions listed for each product rather than relying on breed alone, since two dogs of the same breed can vary a fair bit in size.

faqs.question: My dog is between two size categories, which should I choose?
faqs.answer: For most dogs it's worth checking the product's maximum weight capacity first, since this is usually the limiting factor. If your dog is close to a weight limit, sizing up generally gives a more comfortable fit than a carrier that's a tight squeeze.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a puppy carrier and a small dog carrier?
faqs.answer: Puppy carriers are sized around a young, still-growing dog and often have a more enclosed, reassuring shape, while small dog carriers are built around an adult dog's stable adult weight and dimensions.

faqs.question: Should I choose a backpack, sling or standard carrier for my dog?
faqs.answer: It depends on the trip. Backpacks suit longer walks thanks to better weight distribution, slings suit shorter trips with dogs who like close contact, and a standard carrier is usually the most flexible option for everyday use.

faqs.question: Do you offer carriers suitable for car journeys?
faqs.answer: Yes, our dog car carriers range is built with a wider, more stable base and secure fixings specifically for travelling in a vehicle, alongside the general-purpose carriers in this range.

carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carrier.intro:
Medium dog carriers cover roughly 10kg to 25kg, the point where a carrier needs a proper structural frame rather than fabric alone to hold its shape with a dog inside. Several carriers in this range use a steel wire or steel-tube frame under the fabric for exactly this reason, which also lets them fold flat for storage between trips while still holding a stable box shape in use.

### Why Structure Matters More at This Size

A dog at the lighter end of the small dog category can be carried in a fairly minimal soft bag without much issue. Once you're into medium territory, an unsupported carrier tends to sag around the dog when lifted, which is uncomfortable for them and awkward for you to carry. That's why the carriers here typically lean on a wire frame, a rigid base board, or both, and it's worth checking a product mentions this kind of support if you'll be lifting the carrier fully loaded rather than just walking a settled dog inside it.

### If Your Dog Is Near Either Edge

A dog closer to 10kg may still be comfortable in our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range, which can offer a lighter, less bulky option if the extra structure here isn't needed. At the other end, a dog approaching 25kg or heavier is worth checking against our [large dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers) range instead, since weight capacity is usually the first thing to check, not just whether your dog fits inside physically.

### Car Journeys

Several carriers at this size double as a car crate, with safety belt fixings built in alongside the usual carry handle. If most of your trips are by car rather than on foot, our [dog car carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers) range is worth comparing directly, since it's built specifically around vehicle stability rather than being a general-purpose carrier that also happens to fit in a car.
carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carrier.why_choose:
A carrier built for a medium-sized dog needs to do two things a smaller carrier doesn't have to worry about as much: hold its shape under real weight, and stay manageable to lift and carry once your dog is inside. A wire or tube frame under the fabric addresses the first point directly, keeping the internal space stable rather than collapsing inward when the carrier is picked up.

Ventilation becomes more noticeable at this size too, simply because there's more dog generating warmth inside a similarly proportioned space. Mesh panelling on multiple sides, rather than just a single small vent, makes a bigger practical difference here than it does for a much smaller carrier.
carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carrier.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog before anything else, since 10kg to 25kg is a wide band and a dog at the lower end has quite different support needs to one near the top. Then measure nose to tail base for length, floor to the top of the head or ears for height, and across the shoulders for width, checking these against the product's stated internal dimensions rather than assuming every "medium" carrier is built to the same internal size. If a carrier will double as a car crate, also check it fits your boot or back seat space before buying, since a carrier can be correctly sized for your dog but still awkward to fit in your specific vehicle.

faqs.question: What breeds typically need a medium dog carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on your individual dog's weight rather than breed alone, but dogs in the 10kg to 25kg range often include breeds like Cocker Spaniels, Beagles and similarly proportioned dogs. Always check your dog's actual current weight against the product's capacity.

faqs.question: Do medium dog carriers fold flat for storage?
faqs.answer: Many do, particularly those built around a wire or tube frame, which lets the carrier collapse down when it's not needed. Check the individual product listing, since this varies by design.

faqs.question: Can a medium dog carrier be used as a car crate?
faqs.answer: Several carriers in this range include safety belt fixings and are suitable for both car travel and general use. If car journeys are your main need, our dog car carriers range is built specifically around vehicle stability.

faqs.question: How do I know if my dog needs a medium or large carrier?
faqs.answer: Weight is usually the deciding factor. If your dog is close to or over 25kg, check our large dog carriers range instead, since the frame and stitching on a medium carrier are only rated to a certain weight.

faqs.question: Are medium dog carriers suitable for regular vet visits?
faqs.answer: Yes, most work well for occasional vet trips. If that's your main use, our pet carriers for vet visits range highlights designs with easier top-loading access across all sizes.

carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers.intro:
Large dog carriers are built for dogs over roughly 25kg, where the main challenge shifts from comfort alone to genuine structural capacity: the base, handles and stitching all need to hold up to real weight without flexing or straining. At this size, a carrier is doing a similar job to a travel crate, and it's worth treating the weight rating as a hard limit rather than a rough guide.

### What Changes at This Weight

Below around 25kg, most owners can still lift a loaded carrier by hand for short distances. Above it, that becomes impractical for a lot of people, which is why several options at this size are built to be wheeled or dragged rather than carried, or are designed primarily to sit securely in a car rather than be lifted at all. If carrying isn't realistic for your own build or your dog's weight, our [pet carriers with wheels](/carriers/pet-rolling-carriers) collection is worth comparing before committing to a carry-only design.

### Car Travel at This Size

A large dog is also more likely to be travelling mainly by car rather than being carried any real distance on foot, and our [dog car carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers) range includes wider, more stable base designs and secure fixings built with a heavier dog in mind.

### If You're Not Sure This Is the Right Size

A dog closer to the 25kg threshold may still be comfortably served by our [medium dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/medium-dog-carriers) range, particularly if they're a leaner build rather than a heavier one, so it's worth weighing your dog precisely rather than estimating before choosing between the two.
carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers.why_choose:
At this size, the weight capacity printed on the listing matters more than almost any other detail. A carrier that looks large enough by eye can still be understructured for a genuinely heavy dog, and the base, seams and handles are where that shortfall shows up first, usually at the least convenient moment.

Portability also becomes a real practical question rather than an afterthought. A carrier built for a large dog is inherently heavier and bulkier before your dog even gets in, so it's worth thinking honestly about whether you'll be lifting it by hand, wheeling it, or mainly using it as a secured car crate, since each of those favours a different design.
carriers/dog-carriers/large-dog-carriers.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog on a proper set of scales rather than estimating, since the weight capacity is the limiting factor for most large dog carriers, more so than internal dimensions. Measure length nose to tail base, height floor to the top of the head or ears, and shoulder width, and check all three against the product's stated internal space, since a large dog also needs genuine room to lie down comfortably rather than simply fitting through the door. If you'll be using the carrier mainly in a car, measure your boot or back seat space too, since not every large carrier will fit every vehicle.

faqs.question: What's the maximum weight a large dog carrier can hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed individually on each listing. Always check the stated capacity against your dog's actual current weight, not an estimate, since the frame and stitching are only rated to a specific limit.

faqs.question: How do I carry a large dog carrier if it's too heavy to lift?
faqs.answer: If lifting isn't practical, a wheeled carrier removes the need to carry the full weight by hand. Our pet carriers with wheels collection includes options built around this exact situation.

faqs.question: Are large dog carriers suitable for car travel?
faqs.answer: Many are, though our dog car carriers range is built specifically with a wider, more stable base and secure fixings if car journeys are your main use for a heavier dog.

faqs.question: Do large dog carriers fold down for storage?
faqs.answer: Some do, generally those built on a collapsible steel frame. This varies by product, so check the individual listing if storage space is a concern.

faqs.question: My dog is close to 25kg, should I choose medium or large?
faqs.answer: Weigh your dog precisely rather than estimating. If they're close to the threshold, checking the exact weight capacity of a specific medium dog carrier against your dog's current weight will usually give a clearer answer than the category label alone.

carriers/hiking-pet-carriers.intro:
A walk around the block and a proper hike put very different demands on a carrier. Hiking pet carriers are built for the second kind of trip: longer distances, less predictable terrain, and enough structure to stay comfortable for you over an hour or more rather than just the first twenty minutes. Most carriers built for this use are backpack-style, spreading weight across both shoulders rather than one, since that's what actually holds up over real distance.

### What Matters More on a Longer Route

Ventilation becomes more important the longer a route runs, since your pet is generating warmth against your back for a sustained period rather than a brief carry. A padded hip belt, where included, makes a genuine difference too, transferring some of the load off your shoulders and onto your hips the way a proper hiking rucksack does. A secure inner tether that clips to your pet's collar is also worth checking for, since an off-lead moment on uneven ground is a bigger risk on a trail than on a pavement.

### Dogs Specifically

Most of the demand for this kind of carrier comes from dog owners covering real distance on foot, and our [dog backpack carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carriers) range covers the wider spread of backpack-style options by size, from smaller dogs through to sturdier frames built for bigger breeds. For routes that are specifically longer or more demanding underfoot, our [hiking dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/hiking-dog-carriers) range narrows that down further to designs built with exactly that kind of outing in mind.

### Getting the Basics Right First

Before anything hiking-specific, the fundamentals of a good backpack carrier still apply: check the maximum weight rating against your pet's actual weight, and make sure they have enough room to sit or stand without their head or body pressing against the top or sides.
carriers/hiking-pet-carriers.why_choose:
The case for a dedicated hiking-style carrier over a general-purpose one comes down almost entirely to sustained comfort. A carrier that's fine for a short errand can start to strain at the shoulders well before an hour is up, and on a genuine hike that difference is the one that actually gets felt, both by you and by a pet who can sense when you're uncomfortable carrying them.

Terrain matters here too in a way it doesn't for a pavement walk. Uneven ground means more movement and jostling than a flat, predictable route, so a secure closure and a proper inner tether aren't just nice extras on a hiking carrier, they're doing real work in keeping your pet settled and safely inside.
carriers/hiking-pet-carriers.sizing_guide: Check the maximum weight rating first and compare it against your pet's actual current weight with a margin for a longer trip, since a carrier working right at its limit will feel more strained over an hour-long route than a short one. Then check the internal compartment against your pet's length and height, making sure they can sit or stand without pressing against the top or sides, since a cramped fit becomes more noticeable to an unsettled pet the longer a route runs. If you'll be out for more than an hour at a time, a padded hip belt is worth prioritising over other features, since it does more for your own comfort than almost anything else on the carrier.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a hiking carrier and a standard backpack carrier?
faqs.answer: Hiking carriers are generally built with the same backpack format but with sustained comfort over longer, less predictable terrain in mind, such as a padded hip belt and more robust ventilation. For shorter or more general use, a standard backpack carrier often works just as well.

faqs.question: How long can I carry my pet on a hike?
faqs.answer: This depends on your pet's size, the carrier's design and your own comfort. Take regular breaks to let your pet stretch and check they're settled, and don't treat the maximum weight rating as something to push right up against for a long route.

faqs.question: Is a hiking carrier suitable for puppies?
faqs.answer: It depends on your puppy's current size against the carrier's weight and dimension range. A young or still-growing puppy is often better suited to a smaller, more specific carrier in the meantime.

faqs.question: What should I look for in ventilation for a hiking carrier?
faqs.answer: Mesh panelling positioned around the pet compartment, not just at the very top, makes the biggest difference on a longer route, since your pet is generating warmth against your back for a sustained period.

faqs.question: Do hiking carriers work for cats as well as dogs?
faqs.answer: Some do, particularly lighter cats who settle well in a backpack-style carrier, though most of the range here is sized around dog breeds. Check our cat backpack carriers range if your cat is the one joining you outdoors.

carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers.intro:
A puppy carrier, sometimes called a puppy dog carrier bag, puppy carry bag, or simply a puppy bag, is sized around where your puppy actually is right now, not where they'll end up as an adult. A young puppy who hasn't finished their vaccination course, or who's simply not yet confident walking long distances, still needs to get to the vet, meet the world in short supervised bursts, and travel safely in the car, and a carrier built around their current small size handles all three more comfortably than an adult-sized carrier with a lot of empty space around them.

### A More Enclosed, Reassuring Shape

Puppies are still building confidence in unfamiliar situations, so carriers in this range tend toward a slightly more contained shape with a firm base and mesh windows rather than a fully open design. Getting your puppy in a carrier for the first time doesn't need to be stressful, especially with a design that folds flat when not needed and sets up quickly with a firm cage structure or wooden support board underneath the fabric, keeping the internal space stable even though the puppy carrier bag itself is lightweight.

### Sling vs Structured Carrier

For a very young puppy who wants to be held close rather than sat inside a compartment, our [puppy slings](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-slings) range does exactly that on shorter trips. A structured puppy carry bag tends to suit slightly older puppies, or trips where you need to put the carrier down and leave your puppy settled inside, such as a longer car journey or a vet waiting room.

### Coming Along on a Bike Instead?

If your puppy comes along on bike rides rather than being carried on foot, take a look at our [puppy bike carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bike-carriers) and [puppy bicycle carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bicycle-carriers) ranges instead, which are built for cycling rather than walking.

### As Your Puppy Grows

Once your puppy is approaching their adult weight, it's worth checking our [small dog carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/small-dog-carriers) range rather than continuing to size up within this category, since a carrier built around an adult dog's stable weight will generally serve you longer than a puppy-specific one they're growing out of.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers.why_choose:
A puppy carrier sized to your puppy's current weight rather than a guess at their adult size avoids the two most common problems: too much empty space, which can leave a puppy feeling less secure and more likely to slide about, or a carrier that's genuinely too tight because it was bought with growth in mind before your puppy actually needed it.

Early experiences with a carrier tend to shape how a dog feels about travel for a long time afterwards, so a calm first few times with your puppy in a carrier matter more than they might for an adult dog who's already settled into a routine. A puppy dog carrier bag that's comfortable, secure and not overwhelming in size gives a puppy the best chance of associating the carrier with something unremarkable rather than something stressful.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your puppy at their current size, not an estimate of their adult size, since carriers built for adult dogs of the same breed are often far too roomy for a young puppy and can leave them feeling unsteady rather than secure. Check length nose to tail base, height floor to the top of the head, and the stated weight capacity, and plan to move up a size, or into our small dog carriers range, as your puppy grows rather than buying ahead for a size they'll reach in a few months. A snugger fit generally suits a puppy better than a loose one, since most settle faster in a smaller, more contained puppy bag than a large one that shifts around.

faqs.question: What size carrier does my puppy need right now?
faqs.answer: Measure and weigh your puppy at their current size rather than estimating their adult weight, and choose a puppy carry bag that fits them comfortably now. You can move up to our small dog carriers range once they're closer to their adult size.

faqs.question: Is a sling or a structured carrier better for a puppy?
faqs.answer: A sling suits very young puppies who want to be held close on shorter trips, while a structured puppy carrier is better for longer journeys or times when you need to put the carrier down with your puppy settled safely inside.

faqs.question: Can my puppy travel in a carrier before finishing their vaccinations?
faqs.answer: A carrier keeps your puppy off the ground and away from other animals, which is often exactly what's needed during this period, but always follow your vet's specific guidance on when your puppy can go out and about.

faqs.question: How do I get my puppy used to being in a carrier?
faqs.answer: Leave the puppy bag out at home for short supervised periods before you need to travel, with a blanket inside, so your puppy gets used to being in a carrier before it actually matters.

faqs.question: When should I move my puppy up to a small dog carrier?
faqs.answer: Once they're approaching their expected adult weight, or if they're clearly outgrowing the internal space of their current carrier, whichever comes first.

carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-slings.intro:
A puppy sling holds a young puppy close against your body on a single adjustable strap, which for a very young dog tends to feel more reassuring than a structured carrier held a little further away from you. It's the sling format specifically shaped and sized around how a small, young puppy sits and settles, rather than a scaled-down version of a sling built for an adult dog.

### Why the Age-Specific Shape Matters

A young puppy is proportioned differently to an adult small dog, generally rounder and more compact, and a sling cut for that shape supports them more evenly than one designed around a leaner adult build. Look for a strap that adjusts to fit your own height comfortably, breathable fabric against your puppy since they're held close with limited airflow, and a safety tether that clips to a collar or harness so a wriggly puppy can't slip free mid-carry.

### If Your Puppy Wants More Room

Not every puppy settles well held close in a sling, some prefer a bit more space to shift position, in which case our [puppy carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers) range covers structured alternatives sized the same way around a young, still-growing dog.

### As They Grow

Once your puppy is closer to their adult weight, our general [dog slings](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-slings) range covers the same close-contact format built around adult dog proportions, so moving across at the right point keeps the fit comfortable rather than sizing up within a puppy-specific design.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-slings.why_choose:
For a young puppy still getting used to new places, noise and handling, the closeness of a sling can make a genuine difference to how settled they feel compared with sitting inside a carrier a little further from you. Your own body heat and movement give a puppy something familiar to settle against, which is a large part of why this format tends to work so well at this age.

Because a puppy sling is used during a relatively short window before your puppy either grows out of it or moves to a different format, an adjustable strap and a secure, easy-to-use closure matter more here than they might on a carrier you'll use for years, since you want something that's genuinely simple to get right every single time during a busy, fast-changing few months.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-slings.sizing_guide: Check the sling's weight limit against your puppy's current weight rather than their expected adult weight, since this format is built around a specific, lighter range. Adjust the strap length to sit comfortably at your own height before your first outing, since a badly positioned strap is uncomfortable for you regardless of how well it fits your puppy. If your puppy seems unsettled or tries to climb out of a sling regularly, a structured puppy carrier with a secure zip may suit them better than persisting with a sling.

faqs.question: At what age can a puppy use a sling?
faqs.answer: This depends on your puppy's size and how they respond to being held close, more than age alone. Always check the specific weight limit on the product and introduce it gradually at home before relying on it for a real trip.

faqs.question: How do I know if my puppy prefers a sling or a carrier?
faqs.answer: A puppy who settles calmly when held close against you is usually well suited to a sling. One who wriggles or tries to climb out repeatedly may feel more secure in a structured carrier with a bit more room and a proper zip.

faqs.question: Which shoulder should I wear a puppy sling on?
faqs.answer: Most puppy slings are worn across the body with the strap over one shoulder, and can generally be adjusted to whichever side feels most comfortable for you.

faqs.question: When should I move from a puppy sling to a regular dog sling?
faqs.answer: Once your puppy is approaching their adult weight, our dog slings range covers the same close-contact format built around adult dog proportions rather than a growing puppy's shape.

faqs.question: Can I wash a puppy sling?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable liner or panel. Check the specific care label on the product, since materials vary between machine washable fabric and options that need hand washing.

carriers/dog-carriers/hiking-dog-carrier.intro:
Hiking dog carriers are backpack-format carriers built around covering real distance, where sustained comfort and stability matter more than they do on a short walk to the shops. Several carriers in this range use a reinforced bottom panel to keep their shape under your dog's weight over a longer route, along with multi-point buckle systems that secure your dog at the chest, waist and legs rather than relying on a single strap.

### Front or Back Carry

Some hiking carriers are worn on your front, which keeps your dog in view and close to your chest, useful if you want to keep a closer eye on a nervous dog on uneven terrain. Others are back-worn like a standard rucksack, generally more comfortable over a longer distance since the weight sits higher and more centred on your back. Which suits you better often comes down to how reassured your dog needs to feel versus how far you're planning to go.

### What to Prioritise for Longer Routes

Adjustable shoulder, waist and chest straps all matter more here than on a shorter-use carrier, since a route lasting an hour or more will show up any part of the fit that isn't quite right. Reflective trim is also worth checking for if your walks sometimes run into low light. For the wider range of backpack-style options by size, including for shorter, more general use, our [dog backpack carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carriers) range covers the full spread.

### Comparing Across Pets

If you're comparing this format more broadly, our [hiking pet carriers](/carriers/hiking-pet-carriers) collection covers the same longer-route design across every pet type we carry, not just dogs.
carriers/dog-carriers/hiking-dog-carrier.why_choose:
The case for a dedicated hiking carrier over a standard backpack comes down to how the fit holds up over time rather than in the first few minutes. A multi-point buckle system, securing your dog at the chest, waist and legs rather than one strap alone, keeps them settled and prevents them shifting or trying to break free as the walk goes on, which matters more the longer and less predictable the terrain gets.

Your own comfort matters just as much over a real distance. Adjustable straps at multiple points, rather than a single fixed length, let you fine-tune the fit as you go, which a short-use carrier generally doesn't need to offer in the same way.
carriers/dog-carriers/hiking-dog-carrier.sizing_guide: Check the weight capacity against your dog's actual current weight with a reasonable margin, since a carrier working near its limit will feel more strained over a longer route than a short one. Multiple size options are available on several products in this range, so measure your dog's length, height and chest girth rather than assuming a single size fits every dog. Test the fit at home on a short walk before relying on it for a longer hike, adjusting the chest, waist and leg straps until your dog is secure but not restricted.

faqs.question: Should I choose a front-worn or back-worn hiking carrier?
faqs.answer: Front-worn carriers keep your dog closer and in view, useful for a nervous dog, while back-worn carriers are generally more comfortable over a longer distance since the weight sits higher and more centred.

faqs.question: How far can I hike with my dog in a carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on your dog's size, the carrier's design and your own fitness. Take regular breaks to let your dog stretch, and avoid pushing right up against the maximum weight rating for a longer route.

faqs.question: What's different about a hiking carrier compared to a standard dog backpack?
faqs.answer: Hiking carriers generally add extra securing points such as a chest and leg buckle system, a reinforced base for stability, and sometimes reflective trim, all aimed at longer, less predictable routes.

faqs.question: Is my dog too big for a hiking carrier?
faqs.answer: Check the specific weight rating on each product, since this varies by design. For heavier dogs, our large dog carriers range may be a better starting point if a backpack format isn't rated high enough.

faqs.question: Do hiking dog carriers come in different sizes?
faqs.answer: Yes, several products in this range offer multiple sizes. Measure your dog's length, height and chest girth rather than relying on breed alone before choosing.

carriers/cat-carriers/kitten-carriers.intro:
A young kitten is still forming their first impressions of the world, and the carrier is often part of that early experience, whether it's a trip to the vet for vaccinations or simply getting used to travel before it becomes a regular thing. Kitten carriers in this range are sized around a smaller, lighter cat rather than being a scaled-down version of an adult carrier, with a similarly gentle, enclosed shape that suits a kitten who's easily overwhelmed by open space.

### Two-Zone and Private Designs

Some carriers in this range include a two-zone layout, splitting the interior into a more open, breathable mesh section and a smaller, more enclosed private area a kitten can retreat into. This kind of design can help a nervous kitten feel like they have some choice and control over how exposed they are, rather than being fully visible the whole journey.

### Getting Them Used to It Early

The single biggest factor in how a kitten feels about their carrier long-term is exposure before they actually need it for a stressful trip. Leaving the carrier out at home, with a blanket inside, lets a kitten investigate in their own time. Our blog post on [helping a nervous cat get used to a carrier](/blog/helping-a-nervous-cat-get-used-to-a-carrier) goes into this in more detail.

### As Your Kitten Grows

Once your kitten reaches their adult size, our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range covers the wider adult range, generally a better long-term fit than continuing to use a kitten-specific carrier they've outgrown.
carriers/cat-carriers/kitten-carriers.why_choose:
A kitten's early experiences with a carrier tend to stick, which is exactly why getting this category right matters beyond just the current trip. A carrier that's the right size, calm in shape and easy to get a wriggly kitten into without a struggle sets up a much better pattern than one that turns every use into a stressful chase around the house.

Kittens are also more sensitive to a carrier that feels too large and open than an adult cat generally is, since a big, echoey space with lots of visible movement outside can be genuinely unsettling for a very young animal still building confidence. A snugger, more enclosed fit usually works better here than sizing up for room to grow.
carriers/cat-carriers/kitten-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your kitten's current length and height rather than guessing at their eventual adult size, since a carrier that's too large can leave a young kitten feeling less secure rather than more comfortable. Check the product's minimum as well as maximum weight guidance where given, since some carriers are built primarily around adult cat proportions and may not suit a very small kitten well. Plan to move up to our soft-sided cat carriers range once your kitten approaches their adult size rather than trying to make a kitten carrier last indefinitely.

faqs.question: What size carrier does my kitten need?
faqs.answer: Measure your kitten's current length and height rather than their expected adult size, and choose a snugger, more enclosed carrier rather than one with a lot of extra space, since most kittens feel calmer that way.

faqs.question: How do I get my kitten used to a carrier before their first vet visit?
faqs.answer: Leave the carrier out at home for a week or two beforehand with a soft blanket inside, letting your kitten investigate in their own time rather than only bringing it out on the day of a trip.

faqs.question: Is a top-loading carrier better for a kitten?
faqs.answer: Yes, top access generally makes it easier to lower a kitten in gently and lift them out again, rather than coaxing them through a single front door, which many kittens find more stressful.

faqs.question: When should I move my kitten to an adult cat carrier?
faqs.answer: Once they're approaching their adult weight and size, our soft-sided cat carriers range covers the wider adult range and will generally serve you for longer than a kitten-specific carrier.

faqs.question: Can two kittens travel together in the same carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on the specific carrier's size and weight capacity. Check the product listing carefully, and make sure there's genuinely enough room for both kittens to sit comfortably without feeling cramped.

carriers/cat-carriers/large-cat-carriers.intro:
Larger cat breeds need more than just a longer carrier, they need genuine room to turn around and lie down without their body pressing against the sides. This range is built with that extra internal space in mind, including panoramic-window designs with a reinforced steel wire frame that holds a bigger internal shape stable rather than letting it sag under a heavier cat's weight.

### Why Standard Sizing Falls Short

A carrier sized for an average domestic cat can leave a larger breed genuinely cramped, which tends to show up as a cat who's reluctant to get in or visibly uncomfortable once inside, rather than something you'd necessarily notice from the outside dimensions alone. Checking a carrier's actual internal floor space and height, not just its external size, matters more here than for an average-sized cat.

### Construction That Holds Up

A heavier cat puts more strain on a carrier's base and frame, so a reinforced wire structure or a wooden support board underneath the fabric is worth checking for specifically. If you'd prefer the extra rigidity of a fully rigid shell rather than a reinforced soft-sided design, our [hard-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/hard-sided-cat-carriers) range is built around that stiffer construction instead.

### Everyday Use

For general trips beyond specifically needing extra room, our [soft-sided cat carriers](/carriers/cat-carriers/soft-sided-cat-carriers) range is worth a glance too, in case a lighter, more foldable design suits your routine better once size is sorted.
carriers/cat-carriers/large-cat-carriers.why_choose:
Internal space matters more for a larger cat than almost any other factor, since a cat who can't properly turn around or lie flat is going to be uncomfortable regardless of how good the carrier looks or how sturdy the material is. Panoramic mesh windows on multiple sides also help here, giving a bigger cat more airflow across a larger enclosed space than a single small vent would provide.

Structural strength is the other main consideration. A carrier that's roomy but built on the same lightweight frame as a standard-sized carrier can flex or sag under a heavier cat's weight when lifted, which is uncomfortable for your cat and makes the carrier harder to manage.
carriers/cat-carriers/large-cat-carriers.sizing_guide: Measure your cat's actual length, height and width at their widest point, since larger cat breeds can vary substantially in build even at similar weights. Check the carrier's internal dimensions specifically, not just the external size, and make sure there's genuine room for your cat to stand, turn around fully and lie flat. Always check the maximum weight capacity too, since this can be the limiting factor for a larger, heavier cat even when the internal space looks generous enough.

faqs.question: What counts as a large cat breed for carrier sizing?
faqs.answer: Breeds such as Maine Coons and Ragdolls are commonly larger, but it's your cat's actual measurements and weight that matter, not the breed name. Measure length, height and width before choosing.

faqs.question: How do I know if a carrier has enough internal space?
faqs.answer: Check the product's stated internal dimensions, not just the external size, and compare them against your cat's measurements with enough room to turn around and lie flat comfortably.

faqs.question: Are large cat carriers heavier to carry?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since the extra internal space and reinforced frame add weight compared with a standard-sized carrier. Worth factoring in if you'll be carrying it any distance by hand.

faqs.question: Should I choose a hard-sided or soft-sided carrier for a large cat?
faqs.answer: Both are available in this range. A hard-sided carrier offers more rigid protection, while a reinforced soft-sided carrier is generally lighter, so it depends on how you'll mainly be using it.

faqs.question: What's the maximum weight a large cat carrier can hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed individually. Always check the stated capacity against your cat's actual current weight rather than an estimate.

carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-ca.intro:
Rabbits need something underfoot they can actually grip, not a wire or mesh floor that gives way as they shift their weight. A solid, non-slip base is the single biggest difference between a carrier that works well for a rabbit and one that leaves them feeling unsteady for the whole journey, since rabbits are naturally inclined to brace and push against a surface rather than sit passively.

### What a Good Rabbit Carrier Gets Right

Beyond the solid base, ventilation needs to be genuinely good, since rabbits are sensitive to heat and can become distressed in a stuffy space, particularly in a warm car. Look for mesh panelling on more than one side rather than a single vent. A secure, easy-to-check closure matters too, since a rabbit that manages to push a door or lid loose is both distressing and genuinely difficult to safely recover mid-journey.

### Bedding and Familiarity

Lining the base with familiar hay or bedding from home, rather than cleaning the carrier thoroughly right before a trip, helps a rabbit feel like the space is an extension of somewhere they already know rather than something completely new. Our blog post on [settling a rabbit or guinea pig for a short trip](/blog/settling-a-rabbit-or-guinea-pig-for-a-short-trip) covers this in more detail.

### If You Also Have a Guinea Pig

The same solid-base, well-ventilated approach applies to guinea pigs too, and our [guinea pig carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pig-carriers) range covers that species specifically if your household has both.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-ca.why_choose:
A rabbit's instinct when unsettled is to brace against the ground and push, which is exactly why a solid, grippable floor matters so much more here than it does for a cat or dog. A carrier with a mesh or wire base gives a rabbit nothing to push against, which tends to make them feel less secure rather than more, even if the carrier is otherwise well built.

Temperature sensitivity is worth taking seriously too. Rabbits can overheat faster than many other small pets, so genuine, multi-sided ventilation isn't a nice-to-have here, it's one of the more important things to check before buying, particularly if car journeys in warmer weather are part of your routine.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-ca.sizing_guide: Rabbits need enough floor space to sit naturally and shift position, more than they need height, so check a carrier's internal footprint against your rabbit's stretched-out length rather than just its overall external size. A larger rabbit breed needs proportionally more space than a dwarf breed, so don't assume a single "rabbit carrier" size suits every rabbit. Check the maximum weight guidance too, since the base needs to hold up to a rabbit's weight without flexing.

faqs.question: Why does the base matter so much for a rabbit carrier?
faqs.answer: Rabbits instinctively brace and push against the ground when unsettled, so a solid, non-slip base gives them something to grip, unlike a mesh or wire floor which can leave them feeling unsteady.

faqs.question: How do I stop my rabbit overheating in a carrier?
faqs.answer: Choose a carrier with mesh ventilation on more than one side, avoid direct sunlight during travel, and keep car journeys as cool and well-ventilated as reasonably possible.

faqs.question: Should I put bedding in a rabbit carrier?
faqs.answer: Yes, familiar hay or bedding from your rabbit's usual home helps them feel more settled, since the smell is reassuring rather than the carrier feeling completely unfamiliar.

faqs.question: Can I use a rabbit carrier for a guinea pig?
faqs.answer: Many rabbit carriers work well for guinea pigs too, given the similar need for a solid base and good ventilation, though our guinea pig carriers range is sized specifically for their shorter, wider build.

faqs.question: How do I clean a rabbit carrier?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable base and a removable liner or tray. Check the specific product's care instructions, and avoid cleaning it too thoroughly right before a trip if you want it to still smell familiar to your rabbit.

carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pi.intro:
Guinea pigs settle best with hay and familiar bedding close by, more so than with an open view of their surroundings, which shapes what actually makes a good carrier for them. A solid, non-slip base for their shorter, wider build, good ventilation, and enough room to line the floor with familiar bedding all matter more than a large viewing panel or an open, airy design.

### Comfort Over Visibility

Unlike some small pets who benefit from being able to see out, guinea pigs generally cope better with a calmer, more enclosed space with good airflow rather than lots of open mesh. A carrier that lets you check on them easily from the top or side, without the whole enclosure feeling exposed, tends to work best.

### Bedding Makes a Real Difference

Lining the base with hay and bedding from your guinea pig's usual home helps the carrier smell familiar rather than completely new, which matters more for a guinea pig's sense of security than almost any other single factor. Our blog post on [settling a rabbit or guinea pig for a short trip](/blog/settling-a-rabbit-or-guinea-pig-for-a-short-trip) goes into this in more detail.

### For the Rest of the Household

If you also keep rabbits, our [rabbit carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/rabbit-carriers) range follows much the same solid-base, well-ventilated approach, sized for a rabbit's longer build instead.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pi.why_choose:
Guinea pigs are particularly sensitive to sudden changes in their environment, which is why the small details, familiar bedding, a stable base, a calm rather than overly open design, matter more here than headline features. A carrier that gets these basics right tends to result in a noticeably calmer guinea pig than one chosen purely on size or price.

A solid base matters just as much for guinea pigs as it does for rabbits, since their shorter, sturdier legs don't cope well with a mesh or wire floor that shifts underfoot. Pairing that with genuine multi-sided ventilation keeps the space from becoming too warm on a longer trip.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pi.sizing_guide: Guinea pigs need floor space suited to their shorter, wider build rather than the longer footprint a rabbit needs, so check a carrier's internal dimensions specifically rather than assuming a rabbit-sized carrier will automatically work well. Leave enough room for a layer of hay or bedding on the base without crowding your guinea pig's own space. Check the weight guidance too, particularly if you're travelling with more than one guinea pig in the same carrier.

faqs.question: Should a guinea pig carrier be open or enclosed?
faqs.answer: Guinea pigs generally do better in a calmer, more enclosed design with good ventilation rather than lots of open mesh, since they can find an overly exposed space more unsettling than reassuring.

faqs.question: Can two guinea pigs travel in the same carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on the specific carrier's size and weight capacity. Check the product listing carefully and make sure there's genuinely enough room for both to sit comfortably without feeling cramped.

faqs.question: Do I need to add bedding to the carrier?
faqs.answer: Yes, lining the base with hay and familiar bedding from home helps your guinea pig feel more settled, since the smell is reassuring rather than the carrier feeling completely new.

faqs.question: How do I keep my guinea pig calm during travel?
faqs.answer: Keep the journey as smooth and quiet as reasonably possible, avoid excessive handling along the way, and see our blog for more detailed tips on settling a guinea pig for a short trip.

faqs.question: What base is best for a guinea pig carrier?
faqs.answer: A solid, non-slip base rather than a mesh or wire floor, since guinea pigs need something stable to sit on rather than a surface that shifts as they move.

carriers/small-animal-carriers/hamster-c.intro:
Hamsters are small enough, and determined enough, that security matters more for them than for almost any other pet on the site. A gap that looks negligible to you can be a genuine escape route for a hamster, so the closure and any seams or joins in a carrier deserve more scrutiny here than the overall size or styling.

### Security First

Look for a lid or door that closes fully flush with no visible gaps, and a fastening that a hamster can't push or nudge open from the inside. A compact size actually helps here rather than working against you, since a smaller, more contained space gives a hamster less opportunity to build momentum against a weak point.

### Short Trips Only

A carrier is meant for the journey itself, not extended time away from their usual cage. Keep trips as short and direct as practical, and have your hamster's regular cage set up and ready for when you arrive, rather than treating the carrier as a temporary home.

### Other Small Rodents

The same closure-first approach applies broadly to other small rodents too. If your household also includes a guinea pig, our [guinea pig carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers/guinea-pig-carriers) range is built around their different needs, chiefly a solid base and room for bedding rather than the tight security a hamster carrier prioritises.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/hamster-c.why_choose:
The case for a purpose-built hamster carrier over an improvised box or a carrier built for a different species comes down almost entirely to security. Hamsters are proportionally strong for their size and genuinely capable of finding a gap most owners wouldn't think to check, so a carrier specifically designed with that in mind removes a real source of risk rather than just adding convenience.

Ventilation still matters, but it needs to be balanced against security, mesh sections that are fine enough that a hamster can't push through or chew at easily, rather than large open gaps that prioritise airflow over containment.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/hamster-c.sizing_guide: A hamster carrier doesn't need to be large, and in fact a more compact, fully secure space is usually more reassuring for a hamster than an oversized one with room to build momentum against a weak point in the closure. Prioritise checking the fastening and any seams over the internal dimensions, and make sure the carrier is intended specifically for small rodents rather than being a general-purpose small pet carrier with wider mesh gaps.

faqs.question: What's the most important feature in a hamster carrier?
faqs.answer: A secure, gap-free closure that a hamster can't push or nudge open from the inside. Hamsters are proportionally strong for their size, so this matters more than overall carrier size or styling.

faqs.question: How long can a hamster stay in a carrier?
faqs.answer: A carrier is meant for the journey itself rather than extended time away from their usual cage. Keep trips as short and direct as practical.

faqs.question: Can I use a hamster carrier for other small rodents?
faqs.answer: Many hamster carriers work for similarly sized small rodents, though always check the specific product's size and ventilation suit your particular pet.

faqs.question: Should a hamster carrier have bedding inside?
faqs.answer: A small amount of familiar bedding from their usual cage can help, though don't overfill it, since a hamster still needs enough clear space to sit comfortably and be checked on.

faqs.question: How do I clean a hamster carrier?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable interior. Check the specific product's care instructions, and clean it between uses to keep it hygienic for your pet.

carriers/small-animal-carriers/ferret-ca.intro:
Ferrets are curious, flexible, and genuinely good at finding their way out of anything with a weak point, which makes escape-proofing the single most important quality in a ferret carrier. A ferret's narrow, flexible body can fit through gaps that would stop most other small pets, so a carrier built with a secure, fully enclosed structure matters more here than it does for almost any other animal in this range.

### What to Check For

Look for a carrier with a fastening that locks or clips securely shut rather than a simple flap or loose closure, and check any mesh panelling is fine enough that a ferret can't work their nose or paws through it and start widening a gap. A solid, secure base matters too, since ferrets are active and will investigate every part of the space they're given.

### Ventilation Without Compromise

Ferrets still need good airflow, particularly on a longer or warmer journey, so the aim is proper ventilation that's also properly secure, not a trade-off between the two. Fine, well-fitted mesh panelling on multiple sides generally achieves both.

### Comparing With Other Small Pets

If you're weighing this up against carriers built for other small animals, our [small animal carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers) hub covers the full range with more on how needs vary by species.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/ferret-ca.why_choose:
A ferret's flexibility and curiosity are exactly why a general-purpose small pet carrier can fall short. What looks like a secure closure for a rabbit or guinea pig can be a genuine escape route for a ferret, since their narrow build lets them exploit gaps other animals simply couldn't fit through.

Beyond security, ferrets are active animals even in a confined space, so a carrier that holds its shape and doesn't flex or give under investigation matters more here than it might for a calmer, less active small pet.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/ferret-ca.sizing_guide: A ferret carrier needs enough room for your ferret to turn around and reposition, but the priority should be a fully secure structure over generous space, since more internal room without matching security just gives a determined ferret more room to work at a weak point. Check the fastening and any mesh gaps carefully before checking dimensions, and make sure the carrier is genuinely described as suitable for ferrets rather than a general small pet carrier that hasn't been tested against a ferret's particular flexibility.

faqs.question: Why do ferrets need a specific type of carrier?
faqs.answer: Ferrets are unusually flexible and curious, and can fit through or work at gaps that would contain most other small pets. A carrier built with secure, gap-free closures matters more here than for other species.

faqs.question: What closure is best for a ferret carrier?
faqs.answer: A fastening that locks or clips securely shut, rather than a simple flap or loose closure, since ferrets will investigate and test any weak point they can find.

faqs.question: Do ferret carriers need good ventilation?
faqs.answer: Yes, particularly on longer or warmer journeys. Look for fine, well-fitted mesh panelling on multiple sides that provides airflow without compromising on security.

faqs.question: Can two ferrets travel together in the same carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on the specific carrier's size and weight guidance. Check the product listing to make sure there's genuinely enough secure space for both.

faqs.question: How do I clean a ferret carrier?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable interior. Check the specific product's care instructions, since ferrets can have a stronger scent than some other small pets and benefit from regular cleaning.

carriers/small-animal-carriers/reptile-c.intro:
Reptiles have different needs to almost every other pet on the site: warmth and security matter more than open ventilation or visibility, since most reptiles are more comfortable in a smaller, enclosed, secure space that helps them retain body heat during a journey. A carrier built with that in mind looks quite different to one designed for a rabbit or a bird.

### Warmth Over Airflow

Where many small animal carriers prioritise mesh ventilation, a reptile carrier generally needs less open airflow and more insulation, since reptiles rely on external warmth rather than generating much of their own. A more enclosed design that holds heat, combined with keeping the carrier itself out of cold draughts during transport, matters more here than a large viewing panel.

### Security and Escape-Proofing

A secure, fully enclosed structure with no gaps is essential, since many reptiles are proficient at finding their way through the smallest opening. Check any closure locks or fastens properly shut rather than relying on a simple flap.

### Comparing Other Small Pets

For the full range of species-specific small pet carriers, our [small animal carriers](/carriers/small-animal-carriers) hub covers rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and ferrets alongside this reptile-specific guidance.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/reptile-c.why_choose:
Temperature control is the defining consideration for a reptile carrier in a way it isn't for almost any other pet. Reptiles can't regulate their own body heat the way mammals do, so a carrier that keeps them insulated and away from cold draughts during a journey is doing genuinely important work, not just adding comfort.

Security is the other non-negotiable. A reptile that finds a gap in a carrier is both distressing to deal with and genuinely difficult to safely recover, so a fully enclosed, properly fastened design matters more here than a spacious or highly ventilated one.
carriers/small-animal-carriers/reptile-c.sizing_guide: Reptile sizing varies enormously between species, so check a carrier's specific dimensions against your particular reptile's length and typical resting posture rather than assuming a generic small pet carrier size will work. A more compact, secure space generally suits a reptile better than an oversized one, since it helps retain warmth more effectively and reduces the internal area a reptile could use to find a weak point.

faqs.question: Do reptile carriers need ventilation like other small pet carriers?
faqs.answer: Reptiles generally need less open ventilation than mammals and more warmth retention, so a more enclosed, insulated design tends to suit them better than a highly ventilated one.

faqs.question: How do I keep my reptile warm during transport?
faqs.answer: Choose a more enclosed carrier design, keep it away from cold draughts, and avoid unnecessarily long or exposed journeys, particularly in cooler weather.

faqs.question: How secure do reptile carriers need to be?
faqs.answer: Very secure. Many reptiles are proficient at finding their way through small gaps, so check that any closure locks or fastens properly shut rather than relying on a simple flap.

faqs.question: What size carrier does my reptile need?
faqs.answer: This varies significantly by species. Check a carrier's specific internal dimensions against your reptile's length and typical resting posture rather than assuming a generic small pet size will fit.

faqs.question: Can I use the same carrier for different reptile species?
faqs.answer: This depends on their relative size and temperature needs. Check the specific product listing, since requirements can vary considerably between different types of reptile.

carriers/bird-carriers.intro:
Birds need somewhere to perch, not just somewhere to sit, which is the main thing that sets a bird carrier apart from the rest of the range. A calming, mostly enclosed view out, a secure perch, and a base that's easy to keep clean between trips all matter more here than the open, ventilated designs that suit other small pets.

### Choosing by Size

Our [budgie travel cages](/carriers/bird-carriers/budgie-travel-cages) range is sized for budgies and similarly small birds, generally more compact and lightweight than what a larger bird would need. [Parrot travel cages](/carriers/bird-carriers/parrot-travel-cages) covers larger birds who need genuine room to perch comfortably rather than being squeezed into a small pet carrier. For other small pet birds on short, calm trips, our [small bird carriers](/carriers/bird-carriers/small-bird-carriers) range covers a similar size range with slightly different perch and panelling options.

### Keeping a Bird Calm in Transit

Birds tend to feel calmer with a full but gentle view out rather than being fully enclosed, since sudden darkness or a completely closed carrier can be more unsettling than reassuring for a bird used to open space in their usual cage. A clear-panelled design that still feels secure, with a perch inside rather than a flat floor, generally works best.

### For a Vet Trip

If you're travelling for a check-up specifically, our [pet carriers for vet visits](/carriers/pet-carriers-for-vet-visits) range covers the shorter, calmer style of carrier across every pet we sell, including birds.
carriers/bird-carriers.why_choose:
A perch inside the carrier, rather than a flat floor, matters more for birds than almost any other single feature, since it lets them settle into a natural resting position rather than shifting around on an unfamiliar flat surface for the whole journey. It's a detail that's easy to overlook when comparing carriers by size alone.

Hygiene also deserves more attention here than for some other pets. A tray or base that's easy to wipe clean, rather than one that needs a full wash after every use, keeps a bird carrier practical for regular trips rather than something that becomes a chore to maintain.
carriers/bird-carriers.sizing_guide: Size a bird carrier around your bird's wingspan and how they naturally perch, not just their body length, since a bird needs enough room to settle on a perch without their wings or tail pressing against the sides. Smaller birds like budgies need proportionally less space than parrots and larger species, who need genuine room to perch comfortably rather than being squeezed into a compact carrier. Check the specific product's internal dimensions against your bird's size rather than choosing by species name alone, since sizes vary within species too.

faqs.question: Do bird carriers need a perch inside?
faqs.answer: Yes, a perch lets your bird settle into a natural resting position rather than shifting around on a flat, unfamiliar surface. Check for this specifically when comparing carriers.

faqs.question: Should a bird carrier be fully enclosed or have a clear view out?
faqs.answer: Most birds feel calmer with a full but gentle view out rather than being fully enclosed, since sudden darkness can be more unsettling than reassuring for a bird used to open space.

faqs.question: What size carrier does my bird need?
faqs.answer: Size around your bird's wingspan and how they naturally perch, not just body length, and check the specific product's dimensions rather than choosing by species name alone.

faqs.question: How do I clean a bird carrier?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable tray in the base that wipes clean easily. Check the specific product's care instructions for the best way to keep it hygienic between trips.

faqs.question: Can I use a bird carrier for other small pets?
faqs.answer: Some bird carriers are also suitable for other small pets such as hamsters or guinea pigs, though check the specific product listing to confirm it suits your particular pet's needs.

carriers/bird-carriers/budgie-travel-cag.intro:
Budgies and similarly small birds need a compact, lightweight travel cage with a secure perch and a calming view out, rather than a scaled-down version of a full-size cage. A hygienic, easy to wipe clean tray in the base and breathable mesh sections both matter more for regular, shorter trips than a large footprint does.

### What to Look For

A clear-panelled design generally suits budgies well, giving them a calming full view out while still feeling secure and enclosed enough not to startle them. Look for a wide, easy opening with a secure zip or catch, since a struggling bird at the door is more stressful for both of you than a smooth, confident transfer in and out. A carry handle or adjustable strap is worth checking for too, so you have both hands free if needed.

### Folding for Storage

Since a budgie's travel cage is likely to be used only occasionally rather than daily, a design that folds flat in seconds for storage is genuinely useful between trips, rather than a bulky cage taking up permanent space.

### Bigger Birds

If you're shopping for a larger bird rather than a budgie, our [parrot travel cages](/carriers/bird-carriers/parrot-travel-cages) range is built with the extra room a bigger bird needs to perch comfortably.
carriers/bird-carriers/budgie-travel-cag.why_choose:
A budgie's small size means a travel cage can stay genuinely lightweight and compact without compromising on comfort, which matters if you're the one carrying it. The trade-off worth paying attention to is ventilation and visibility working together properly, since a budgie generally settles better with a full view out than in a more enclosed design built for other species.

Because a budgie's travel cage tends to come out only occasionally, for a vet visit or a house move rather than daily use, ease of storage between uses is a genuinely practical thing to check for rather than an afterthought.
carriers/bird-carriers/budgie-travel-cag.sizing_guide: A budgie doesn't need a large travel cage, a compact size that still gives them room to perch comfortably and turn around is generally more reassuring than an oversized one. Check the internal height specifically, since a budgie needs enough clearance above the perch without feeling cramped, and confirm the carrier is suited to budgie-sized birds rather than a general small pet carrier that hasn't been designed with a perch in mind.

faqs.question: Does a budgie travel cage need a perch?
faqs.answer: Yes, a perch lets your budgie settle naturally rather than sitting on a flat, unfamiliar surface for the journey. This is one of the main things that separates a proper bird travel cage from a general small pet carrier.

faqs.question: How do I get my budgie into the travel cage without stress?

faqs.question: Can I use a budgie cage for a slightly larger bird like a cockatiel?

faqs.question: How do I clean a budgie travel cage?

carriers/bird-carriers/parrot-travel-cag.intro:
Larger birds need genuine room to perch and move without their wings or tail pressing against the sides, which rules out simply using a budgie-sized travel cage for a bigger species. A parrot travel cage is built with that extra footprint and height in mind, alongside a sturdier perch able to take a heavier bird's grip.

### Room to Perch Properly

Check a carrier's internal height and width against your bird's wingspan and typical perching posture, not just their body length, since a cramped fit is more noticeable and more stressful for a larger bird than a small one. A sturdy, properly sized perch matters more here too, since a perch built for a lighter bird may not hold up well to a larger parrot's grip.

### Security for a Stronger Beak

Larger birds are generally stronger and more capable with their beak than small birds, so closures and any mesh panelling need to genuinely hold up to that, not just look secure. Check reviews or product details for how the carrier's fastenings are built before relying on it for a longer trip.

### Smaller Birds

If you're shopping for a budgie or a similarly small bird rather than a larger parrot, our [budgie travel cages](/carriers/bird-carriers/budgie-travel-cages) range is sized more appropriately and will feel less oversized for a smaller bird.
carriers/bird-carriers/parrot-travel-cag.why_choose:
Getting the size right matters more for larger birds than it does for most small pets, since a cramped carrier is both physically uncomfortable and noticeably more stressful for a bird used to having room to move and perch freely in their usual cage. A properly sized parrot travel cage avoids that mismatch entirely.

Build quality around the closures and perch also deserves more scrutiny here than for a smaller bird, since a larger parrot's strength and beak are genuinely capable of testing a weak fastening or a perch that isn't properly secured.
carriers/bird-carriers/parrot-travel-cag.sizing_guide: Measure your bird's wingspan and typical perching height, then check these against the carrier's internal dimensions with enough clearance that your bird's wings and tail don't press against the sides or top. A sturdy, appropriately sized perch matters as much as overall room, since a perch too thin or too lightweight for a larger bird's grip won't feel secure to them regardless of the carrier's overall size.

faqs.question: How much room does a parrot need in a travel cage?
faqs.answer: Enough that their wings and tail don't press against the sides or top when perched naturally. Check a carrier's internal height and width against your bird's wingspan, not just body length.

faqs.question: Are parrot travel cages more secure than budgie cages?
faqs.answer: They need to be, since larger birds are generally stronger and more capable with their beak. Check the fastenings and perch construction carefully rather than assuming size alone means security.

faqs.question: What kind of perch does a parrot travel cage need?
faqs.answer: A sturdy perch able to comfortably take a larger bird's grip, rather than a thin or lightweight perch designed for a small bird.

faqs.question: Can a parrot travel cage be used for a smaller bird too?
faqs.answer: It can, but a smaller bird may feel more secure in a correctly sized budgie travel cage rather than a larger, more open space designed for a bigger species.

faqs.question: How do I keep a parrot calm during travel?
faqs.answer: A carrier with a calming view out rather than being fully enclosed generally helps, alongside keeping the journey as smooth and quiet as reasonably possible.

carriers/bird-carriers/small-bird-carrie.why_choose:

strollers.intro:
A stroller solves a specific problem a carrier doesn't: it lets a pet who can't or shouldn't walk far, whether that's due to age, size, joint stiffness, or simply not being able to walk outside safely yet, still get out and enjoy fresh air and a change of scenery without the strain of a long walk on their own legs, or the ongoing effort of being carried by hand.

### Choosing by Pet

Our [dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers) range is organised by dog size and use, from compact frames for small breeds through to sturdier builds for larger dogs, plus jogging and double options. [Cat strollers](/strollers/cat-strollers) covers a more enclosed style suited to cats who enjoy the outdoors without the risks of walking freely outside. Our [small animal strollers](/strollers/small-animal-strollers) range suits rabbits and guinea pigs who benefit from time outdoors in a fully enclosed, secure space, and [multi-pet strollers](/strollers/multi-pet-strollers) covers households travelling with more than one pet together.

### What Matters Across Every Stroller

Whichever category you're shopping, a few things are worth checking regardless of pet or size: a secure harness inside the stroller so your pet can't jump out mid-walk, wheels suited to where you'll actually be walking (pavement, gravel, or a mix), and a weight capacity that comfortably covers your pet with some margin rather than being right at the limit.

### If a Carrier Might Suit Better

A stroller isn't always the right tool. For shorter trips, or a pet who's happy being carried rather than wheeled, our [carriers](/carriers) range may be a simpler, more compact option worth comparing first.
strollers.why_choose:
A stroller gives a pet the benefit of being outside, moving air, new sights and smells, without asking their body to do work they may not be up to, whether that's a young puppy not yet fully vaccinated, an older dog with stiffer joints, or a small animal who simply isn't suited to walking on a lead in the first place.

It also changes what's practical for the owner. A stroller lets you cover more ground comfortably than carrying a pet by hand for any real distance, and unlike a carrier, your pet has room to sit up, look around and shift position throughout the walk rather than staying in one fixed spot.
strollers.sizing_guide: Stroller sizing comes down to two figures that matter independently: the maximum weight capacity and the internal compartment dimensions, since a stroller can be limited by either one. Weigh your pet and measure them nose to tail for length and floor to shoulder for height, then check both figures against the specific product rather than assuming a stroller labelled for your pet's general size will automatically fit. If your pet is still growing, leave a little extra room rather than sizing exactly to their current measurements. Wheel size and frame width also matter if you'll regularly be on gravel, kerbs or need to fold the stroller down for the car.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a stroller and a carrier?
faqs.answer: A stroller lets your pet sit up and move around inside on wheels, suited to longer outings, while a carrier is generally more compact and better suited to shorter trips or being carried by hand.

faqs.question: Which pets are strollers suitable for?
faqs.answer: Dogs, cats and small animals such as rabbits and guinea pigs who benefit from outdoor time without the strain of walking themselves, or who can't walk outside safely. Choose the category built for your specific pet.

faqs.question: Do strollers have a harness inside?
faqs.answer: Most do, to keep your pet secure and prevent them jumping out mid-walk. Always check a harness is fitted correctly and your pet is comfortable before setting off.

faqs.question: Can I use a stroller on uneven ground?
faqs.answer: This depends on the wheel size and frame construction, which varies by product. Check the specific listing if you'll regularly be on gravel, grass or uneven pavements rather than smooth paths.

faqs.question: Do you offer free UK delivery on strollers?
faqs.answer: Yes, orders over £50 qualify for free standard UK shipping, with a small delivery charge shown at checkout for orders under that. We also offer 30-day returns.

strollers/dog-strollers.intro:
A dog stroller needs to match your dog's size and your usual walking routine just as much as a carrier does, since a frame built for a small breed won't hold up to a larger dog, and a stroller built for gentle pavement walks isn't the same product as one built for jogging alongside you.

### Shopping by Size

Our [small dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-strollers) range suits small and toy breeds with a more compact, lighter frame, while our [large dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-strollers) range is built with a sturdier frame and higher weight capacity for bigger dogs. If your dog is a puppy not yet fully vaccinated or confidently mobile, our [puppy strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/puppy-strollers) range is sized around their smaller, still-growing build.

### Shopping by Use

If your usual routine involves running rather than a gentle walk, our [jogging dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/jogging-dog-strollers) range is built with stability at pace in mind. For households with two dogs travelling together, our [double dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strollers) range gives each dog their own secured space side by side.

### The Wider Range

If you're comparing strollers across other pets too, our [strollers](/strollers) hub covers cat and small animal strollers alongside this dog-specific range.
strollers/dog-strollers.why_choose:
Getting the size and use case right matters as much for a stroller as it does for a carrier. A dog who's a little too big for their stroller's frame will feel cramped and unstable, while one who's a lot smaller than the stroller's intended size can move around more than is comfortable or safe inside.

Matching the stroller to how you'll actually use it matters just as much. A stroller built for gentle pavement walks isn't necessarily stable at jogging pace, and a stroller sized for one dog won't comfortably or safely carry two, which is exactly why this range is split by both size and use rather than one generic design.
strollers/dog-strollers.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog and measure them nose to tail for length and floor to shoulder for height, then check both figures against the stroller's stated weight capacity and internal compartment dimensions, since either one can be the limiting factor. For a growing puppy, size for their current weight with a little room to grow rather than their expected adult size. If your dog is close to a weight limit, moving up to our large dog strollers range generally gives a more comfortable, stable ride than a stroller working right at its maximum.

faqs.question: How do I choose between small and large dog strollers?
faqs.answer: Weigh your dog and check this against each stroller's specific weight capacity and internal dimensions, rather than relying on breed alone, since build varies a fair bit between dogs of similar size.

faqs.question: Can I use a dog stroller for jogging?

faqs.question: Can two dogs travel in the same stroller?
