faqs.question: What should I check before buying a dog stroller?
faqs.answer: Weight capacity, internal dimensions, a secure harness attachment, and wheel size suited to where you'll actually be walking, whether that's smooth pavement or more uneven ground.

strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-stroll.intro:
Small dog strollers use a lighter, more compact frame suited to toy and small breeds, generally easier to manoeuvre and fold down than a stroller built for a larger dog. That lighter build isn't just about weight capacity, it also tends to make the stroller easier to lift in and out of a car boot or up a step, which matters if you're the one managing it day to day.

### What to Check

A secure harness attachment inside the compartment matters regardless of size, since even a small dog can attempt to climb or jump out mid-walk. Check the canopy offers genuine shade and some weather protection, and that the compartment has enough room for your dog to sit up and turn around comfortably rather than being sized right to their current measurements with no margin.

### If Your Dog Is a Puppy

A young puppy not yet fully vaccinated or confidently mobile may be better suited in the meantime to our [puppy strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/puppy-strollers) range, sized more specifically around a smaller, still-growing dog.

### If Your Dog Is Closer to Medium

If your dog is at the upper end of what's typically considered small, our [large dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-strollers) range is worth checking against their actual weight before committing, since a stroller working near its limit is less comfortable than one with room to spare.
strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-stroll.why_choose:
The main advantage of a small dog stroller is manoeuvrability, both for your dog inside it and for you pushing it. A lighter frame turns more easily on busy pavements and is simpler to fold and carry when you're not using it, which matters more for small breed owners who may be using the stroller for shorter, more frequent outings rather than one long walk.

That said, lighter doesn't mean less secure. A well-built small dog stroller still needs a proper harness attachment and a stable base, since a dog who feels the stroller wobble is just as unsettled by that as a larger dog would be in a less stable frame.
strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-stroll.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog and measure them nose to tail and floor to shoulder, then check both against the stroller's stated capacity and internal dimensions rather than assuming any "small dog" stroller will fit any small dog equally well. Leave enough room for your dog to sit up, turn around and lie down without pressing against the sides or canopy. If your dog is close to the upper weight limit for this category, checking our large dog strollers range may give a more comfortable fit.

faqs.question: What size dog suits a small dog stroller?
faqs.answer: Generally toy and small breeds, though it's the specific weight capacity and internal dimensions of each product that matter most, rather than the category label alone.

faqs.question: Are small dog strollers easy to fold and store?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since the lighter frame tends to fold down more compactly than a larger stroller. Check the specific product for folded dimensions if storage space is limited.

faqs.question: Do small dog strollers have a secure harness?
faqs.answer: Most include an internal harness attachment to stop your dog jumping or climbing out mid-walk. Always check your dog is securely and comfortably fitted before setting off.

faqs.question: Can a small dog stroller be used on grass or gravel?
faqs.answer: This depends on the wheel size and construction, which varies by product. Check the specific listing if you'll regularly be off smooth pavement.

faqs.question: What if my small dog is close to the weight limit?
faqs.answer: It's worth checking our large dog strollers range instead, since a stroller working right at its maximum capacity is generally less comfortable and stable than one with a bit of margin.

strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-stroll.intro:
Large dog strollers use a sturdier frame and higher weight capacity than a standard stroller, built to stay stable under real weight rather than flexing or feeling unsteady with a bigger dog inside. This matters most for older or larger dogs who benefit from getting outside without the strain of a full walk on their own legs, such as dogs recovering from an injury or managing stiffer joints.

### Structure Over Style

At this size, frame rigidity and wheel quality matter more than they do for a smaller stroller. Larger, sturdier wheels cope better with kerbs and slightly uneven ground than small castors, and a wider wheelbase generally makes the stroller more stable when your dog shifts their weight inside.

### Two Large Dogs Together

If you're managing two dogs rather than one, our [double dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strollers) range gives each dog their own secured space, worth checking if you're currently considering two single strollers instead.

### If Weight Capacity Is Tight

If your dog is closer to a medium build, our [small dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-strollers) range may still be appropriate and offers a lighter, more manoeuvrable frame, so it's worth checking your dog's actual weight against both ranges before deciding.
strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-stroll.why_choose:
A stroller built for a larger dog needs to do more than simply be bigger. The frame, axle and wheels all need genuine structural capacity to stay stable, rather than a standard stroller scaled up in size without the underlying build to match. That structural difference is what actually determines whether the stroller feels secure to a bigger dog rather than wobbly or unstable.

Portability is worth thinking about honestly too. A large dog stroller is inherently heavier and bulkier before your dog even gets in, so consider how you'll be storing and transporting it, particularly if it needs to fit in a car boot regularly.
strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-stroll.sizing_guide: Weigh your dog precisely rather than estimating, since weight capacity is the main limiting factor for a large dog stroller, more so than internal dimensions in most cases. If you'll be transporting the stroller by car regularly, check its folded dimensions against your boot space too.

faqs.question: What's the maximum weight a large dog stroller can hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed individually. Always check the stated capacity against your dog's actual current weight rather than an estimate.

faqs.question: Are large dog strollers suitable for older dogs?
faqs.answer: Yes, many owners use a large dog stroller for older dogs managing stiffer joints, or dogs recovering from an injury who still benefit from getting outside without the strain of a full walk.

faqs.question: Do large dog strollers fold down for storage?

faqs.question: Can a large dog stroller handle uneven ground?
faqs.answer: This depends on the wheel size and frame construction, which varies by product. Larger, sturdier wheels generally cope better with kerbs and slightly uneven paths than small castors.

faqs.question: Should I choose a large dog stroller for two smaller dogs instead?

strollers/dog-strollers/jogging-dog-stro.intro:
Running with a stroller puts different demands on the frame and wheels than a standard walking pace does, more vibration, faster direction changes, and a need for the stroller to track straight without constant correction. Jogging dog strollers are built with that in mind, generally with larger, more stable wheels than a standard walking stroller.

### What Changes at Running Pace

Wheel size and quality matter more here than almost any other feature, since small castors designed for smooth pavement walking tend to struggle and vibrate at running speed. A wider, more stable wheelbase also helps the stroller track straight rather than pulling to one side as you pick up pace. A secure harness inside matters just as much here as on any stroller, arguably more so given the additional movement.

### Matching to Your Dog's Size

This range covers the jogging-specific frame and wheel upgrade, but weight capacity still varies by product, so check your dog's actual weight against the specific listing rather than assuming every jogging stroller suits every dog size. Our [dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers) hub covers the wider range by size if you need a different starting point.

### Before You Head Out

Get your dog comfortable with the stroller at a walking pace first, in a quiet area, before introducing faster movement, so the additional vibration and speed aren't a surprise on their first proper run.
strollers/dog-strollers/jogging-dog-stro.why_choose:
The case for a dedicated jogging stroller over a standard walking one comes down to how the frame behaves at pace. A standard stroller can feel unstable or vibrate uncomfortably once you pick up speed, which is unsettling for a dog inside and harder for you to control, particularly on anything other than a perfectly flat, smooth surface.

Braking and tracking straight matter more here too. A stroller that pulls to one side is a minor annoyance at walking pace but a genuine handling issue while jogging, so a wider, well-aligned wheelbase is worth prioritising specifically for this use.
strollers/dog-strollers/jogging-dog-stro.sizing_guide: Check the weight capacity against your dog's actual current weight with a reasonable margin, since a stroller working close to its limit will feel less stable at running pace than one with room to spare. Measure your dog's length and height and check these against the internal compartment dimensions, making sure they can sit securely without being cramped, since additional movement at pace makes a snug, secure fit more important than it would be for gentle walking.

faqs.question: What makes a jogging stroller different from a standard dog stroller?
faqs.answer: Generally larger, more stable wheels and a wider wheelbase designed to track straight and handle vibration at running pace, rather than the smaller castors found on a standard walking stroller.

faqs.question: How do I get my dog used to a jogging stroller?
faqs.answer: Introduce it at a walking pace first in a quiet area, letting your dog get comfortable with the movement and the harness, before building up to a full running pace.

faqs.question: Is any dog stroller suitable for running?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Standard walking strollers can feel unstable or vibrate uncomfortably at pace, which is why jogging-specific strollers use larger, sturdier wheels built for that purpose.

faqs.question: What weight capacity should I look for?
faqs.answer: Check the specific product's stated capacity against your dog's actual current weight with some margin, since a stroller working close to its limit is less stable at running pace.

faqs.question: Can I use a jogging stroller for regular walks too?
faqs.answer: Yes, a jogging stroller generally works just as well for a standard walking pace, so it can cover both uses if you sometimes run and sometimes walk.

strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strol.intro:
Two dogs travelling together need their own secured space each, not one shared compartment sized for a single dog. Double dog strollers are built with two separate sections or a divided compartment, each with its own harness attachment, so both dogs can settle without competing for room or unsettling each other during the walk.

### Why a Single Stroller Doesn't Work for Two

A stroller sized and rated for one dog isn't built to safely carry the combined weight of two, and without separate secured spaces, two dogs sharing a compartment can end up unsettled by each other's movement rather than both settling comfortably. A proper double stroller solves both problems at once.

### Checking Combined Weight

The stated weight capacity on a double stroller generally refers to the combined total for both dogs, so check this against your two dogs' actual combined weight rather than assuming it's a per-dog figure. If one or both dogs are on the larger side, it's worth comparing against our [large dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/large-dog-strollers) range too, in case a single, larger-capacity stroller suits your situation better than a double.

### Mixed Households

If your two pets aren't both dogs, our [multi-pet strollers](/strollers/multi-pet-strollers) range covers stroller options built for different pet combinations travelling together.
strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strol.why_choose:
The main benefit of a double stroller over managing two dogs separately, whether that's two single strollers or one dog walking and one carried, is straightforward practicality: one stroller to push, one route to manage, and both dogs settled in their own secured space rather than needing separate attention.

Getting the compartment layout right matters more here than on a single stroller, since two dogs who can see and settle near each other, without directly sharing space, tend to cope with the journey better than two dogs squeezed into an undivided compartment.
strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strol.sizing_guide: Weigh both dogs individually and add the totals together, then check this combined figure against the stroller's stated capacity, since double strollers are generally rated for the total weight of both dogs rather than each dog separately. Check each compartment's individual dimensions too, since a double stroller with a generous combined capacity can still have individually snug sections, so measure each dog against their specific side rather than assuming both spaces are identical.

faqs.question: Is the weight limit on a double stroller per dog or combined?
faqs.answer: Generally combined for both dogs together. Always check the specific product listing to confirm, and weigh both dogs individually before adding the totals together.

faqs.question: Do both dogs get their own space in a double stroller?
faqs.answer: Yes, double dog strollers are built with two separate sections or a divided compartment, each with its own harness attachment, rather than one shared space.

faqs.question: Can I use a double stroller for one large dog instead of two?
faqs.answer: It's not generally designed for that. If you have one larger dog, our large dog strollers range is built specifically around a single dog's higher weight capacity.

faqs.question: What if my two dogs are very different sizes?
faqs.answer: Check each compartment's individual dimensions and weight guidance rather than just the combined total, since a double stroller's two sides may not be identical in every product.

faqs.question: Are double dog strollers harder to manoeuvre than single ones?
faqs.answer: They're generally larger and heavier given the extra space and structure, which is worth factoring in for storage and handling, though the wheelbase is typically designed to keep manoeuvring manageable.

strollers/dog-strollers/puppy-strollers.intro:
Before a puppy finishes their vaccination course, or before they're confidently mobile enough for a full walk, a stroller lets them still get outside, experience fresh air, new sounds and passing activity, without walking on the ground themselves. Puppy strollers are sized around a smaller, still-growing dog rather than an adult small breed, generally lighter and more compact than a standard dog stroller.

### Why Timing Matters Here

This is a genuinely useful stage-specific product rather than a permanent one. Once your puppy is confidently walking and fully vaccinated, most owners move away from a stroller in favour of actual walks, so it's worth thinking of this as bridging that early period rather than a long-term purchase, and buying accordingly.

### What to Check

A secure harness attachment matters just as much for a puppy as for an adult dog, since a young puppy can still attempt to climb or jump. Check the compartment gives a little room to grow rather than fitting exactly to their current tiny size, and confirm the canopy offers some shelter since puppies are still building tolerance to weather and temperature changes.

### As They Grow

Once your puppy is closer to their adult size and fully mobile, our [small dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/small-dog-strollers) range is generally the better long-term fit rather than continuing to size up within a puppy-specific stroller.
strollers/dog-strollers/puppy-strollers.why_choose:
A stroller sized around a puppy's actual current size, rather than an adult stroller with a lot of extra space, tends to feel more secure to a young dog who's still building confidence in unfamiliar situations. Too much empty room can leave a puppy sliding about rather than settled, which works against the calm, positive first experiences that shape how they feel about being out and about later on.

This stage is also relatively short, so ease of use matters more than long-term durability features that a stroller built to last years might prioritise. A stroller that's simple to fold, load and unload suits the busy, fast-changing weeks of early puppyhood better than a heavier, more elaborate design.
strollers/dog-strollers/puppy-strollers.sizing_guide: Measure and weigh your puppy at their current size, not an estimate of their adult weight, and choose a stroller that fits them comfortably now with a little room to grow rather than sizing for where they'll end up. Check the harness attachment adjusts down small enough to fit securely on a young puppy, since a harness sized for an adult dog may not hold a small puppy snugly. Plan to move to our small dog strollers range once your puppy is closer to their adult size and confidently mobile.

faqs.question: When can my puppy use a stroller?
faqs.answer: A stroller can be a useful way to get a young puppy outside before they've finished their vaccination course or built up confidence walking, but always follow your vet's specific guidance on when it's safe for your puppy to be around other animals and outdoor spaces.

faqs.question: How is a puppy stroller different from a small dog stroller?
faqs.answer: Puppy strollers are sized around a smaller, still-growing dog with a more secure, closer fit, while small dog strollers are built around an adult dog's stable size and weight.

faqs.question: When should I move my puppy to a small dog stroller?
faqs.answer: Once they're closer to their adult size and confidently mobile, our small dog strollers range will generally be a better long-term fit than continuing to use a puppy-specific stroller.

faqs.question: Does a puppy stroller need a harness?
faqs.answer: Yes, a secure harness attachment matters for puppies just as much as adult dogs, since a young puppy can still attempt to climb or jump out unexpectedly.

faqs.question: Can I use a puppy stroller instead of walking my puppy at all?
faqs.answer: A stroller is best used as a bridge before your puppy is ready for full walks, not a long-term replacement for the exercise and socialisation regular walks provide once they're able to.

strollers/cat-strollers.intro:
Cats generally don't walk on a lead the way dogs do, and letting a cat roam freely outside comes with risks many owners would rather avoid, from traffic to getting lost to encounters with other animals. A cat stroller offers a middle ground: genuine outdoor time, fresh air and a change of scenery, inside a fully enclosed, secure space your cat can't escape from.

### A More Enclosed Design

Unlike some dog strollers with a more open top, cat strollers tend to lean toward a fully enclosed mesh compartment, since cats are both more prone to trying to climb or jump out and generally less comfortable in a wide open space than many dogs are. Check the mesh is secure and fine enough that your cat can't push a paw through and work at the seam.

### Introducing Your Cat Gradually

Most cats need a gradual introduction to a stroller, starting indoors or in a quiet garden before attempting a busier walk, since the movement and new sounds can be overwhelming without that buildup. Watch for signs your cat is uncomfortable rather than pushing through a full walk on the first attempt.

### Other Small Pets

If your household also includes rabbits or guinea pigs, our [small animal strollers](/strollers/small-animal-strollers) range follows a similarly enclosed approach suited to their needs.
strollers/cat-strollers.why_choose:
A stroller gives a cat the sensory benefit of being outside, without the safety concerns that come with letting them roam freely. That combination, genuine outdoor exposure plus full containment, is difficult to achieve any other way for a cat who isn't used to walking on a harness and lead.

Security matters more here than for most other strollers, since cats are naturally inclined to test for a way out of an enclosed space they don't want to be in. A properly secured zip and fine, sturdy mesh are worth checking closely rather than assuming any enclosed compartment will hold up to a determined cat.
strollers/cat-strollers.sizing_guide: Measure your cat's length and height and check these against the stroller's internal dimensions, allowing enough room for them to stand, turn around and lie down without feeling cramped. Check the maximum weight capacity too, particularly for larger cat breeds. A snugger, calmer compartment generally suits a nervous cat better than a large open one, so more space isn't automatically the better choice here.

faqs.question: Will my cat actually enjoy a stroller?
faqs.answer: This varies by individual cat. A gradual introduction, starting indoors or in a quiet garden, gives your cat the best chance of settling into it rather than attempting a busy first walk straight away.

faqs.question: Can a cat escape from a stroller?
faqs.answer: A well-built cat stroller uses a fully enclosed, secure mesh compartment with a proper zip closure specifically to prevent this. Check the mesh and closures carefully, since cats are persistent about testing for a way out.

faqs.question: How do I introduce my cat to a stroller?
faqs.answer: Let them explore the stationary stroller indoors first, then try short, quiet outings before attempting a longer or busier walk, watching for signs of stress along the way.

faqs.question: Is a cat stroller safer than a harness and lead?
faqs.answer: A stroller keeps your cat fully enclosed rather than relying on a harness fit and your cat's tolerance for walking on a lead, which some cats never fully adapt to.

faqs.question: What size stroller does my cat need?
faqs.answer: Measure your cat's length and height and check against the internal compartment dimensions, leaving enough room to turn around and lie down without feeling cramped.

strollers/small-animal-strollers.intro:
Rabbits and guinea pigs can benefit from time outdoors, fresh air, grass smells and a change of scenery, without the risks that come with letting them roam in an open garden or on a lead. A small animal stroller gives them a fully enclosed, secure space to experience the outdoors from, with a solid base underneath rather than open ground.

### A Solid Base Still Matters

Just as with a carrier, rabbits and guinea pigs do better with a solid, non-slip floor to sit on rather than a mesh or wire base, so check this specifically rather than assuming every small animal stroller is built the same way as a cat or dog one. Good ventilation on the sides still matters, but the base should be solid and stable underfoot.

### Keeping the Trip Calm

Lining the stroller compartment with familiar bedding, and keeping the journey smooth and free of sudden stops, helps a small animal feel more settled during a stroller trip, much as it would for a carrier journey. Avoid direct sunlight and check on your pet regularly during longer outings.

### Cats Too

If your household includes a cat as well, our [cat strollers](/strollers/cat-strollers) range covers a similarly enclosed approach suited to their needs specifically.
strollers/small-animal-strollers.why_choose:
A stroller opens up outdoor time for small animals who wouldn't otherwise get much of it safely, given the real risks of predators, escape and unfamiliar hazards in an open garden or on a lead. A fully enclosed stroller compartment removes most of that risk while still giving your pet genuine fresh air and a change of scenery from their usual indoor space.

The base matters as much here as it does in a carrier. A solid, grippable floor lets a rabbit or guinea pig feel steady rather than unsettled by a surface that shifts underfoot every time the stroller moves.
strollers/small-animal-strollers.sizing_guide: Check the stroller's internal footprint against your pet's stretched-out length, since floor space matters more than height for rabbits and guinea pigs. Confirm the base is solid rather than mesh, and that there's room to line the floor with familiar bedding without crowding your pet's own space. Always check the weight guidance too, particularly for larger rabbit breeds.

faqs.question: Is a small animal stroller safe for rabbits and guinea pigs?
faqs.answer: A fully enclosed stroller with a solid base gives them a secure space to enjoy the outdoors, removing many of the risks of letting them roam freely. Check the base is solid rather than mesh before buying.

faqs.question: Should I put bedding in the stroller?
faqs.answer: Yes, familiar bedding from home helps your pet feel more settled, much as it would in a carrier.

faqs.question: How long can my rabbit or guinea pig stay in a stroller?
faqs.answer: Keep outings reasonably short and check on your pet regularly, watching for signs of stress or discomfort, and avoid leaving them in direct sunlight for extended periods.

faqs.question: What size stroller does my rabbit need?
faqs.answer: Check the internal floor space against your rabbit's stretched-out length rather than the overall external size, since floor space matters more than height for this kind of pet.

faqs.question: Can I use the same stroller for a rabbit and a guinea pig?
faqs.answer: Many small animal strollers suit both, given their similar need for a solid base and good ventilation, though check the specific product's size guidance for your particular pet.

strollers/multi-pet-strollers.intro:
Households with more than one pet, whether that's two dogs, a dog and a cat, or another combination, often need a stroller built around travelling together rather than managing separate single strollers or carriers side by side. Multi-pet strollers use a larger, divided or shared compartment sized for more than one animal at once.

### Compartment Layout Matters

Whether pets share one open compartment or have separated sections depends on the specific product, and it's worth thinking about how your particular pets get along and whether they're comfortable close together before choosing. Pets who are already settled around each other at home generally do better sharing a compartment than pets who aren't used to close contact.

### Checking Combined Weight and Space

As with a double stroller, the stated capacity on a multi-pet stroller generally covers the combined weight of all pets travelling together, so weigh each pet individually and add the totals rather than assuming the figure applies per pet. For two dogs specifically, our [double dog strollers](/strollers/dog-strollers/double-dog-strollers) range is built with a dog-specific divided layout that may suit your situation better than a general multi-pet design.

### The Wider Range

For single-pet options across every animal we cover, our [strollers](/strollers) hub is worth browsing alongside this multi-pet range.
strollers/multi-pet-strollers.why_choose:
The practical case for a multi-pet stroller is straightforward: one stroller to manage rather than juggling two, which matters if you're regularly heading out with more than one pet and want a single, manageable setup rather than two separate strollers or a stroller plus a carrier.

Getting the compartment arrangement right for your specific pets matters more here than the stroller's overall size. Two pets who are relaxed around each other will generally settle well sharing a space, while pets who aren't used to close contact may do better with a design that keeps them visibly separated within the same stroller.
strollers/multi-pet-strollers.sizing_guide: Weigh each pet individually and add the totals together, then check this combined figure against the stroller's stated capacity, since multi-pet strollers are generally rated for the total weight of all pets rather than each one separately. Check the compartment layout and individual space carefully too, since a generous combined capacity doesn't always mean each pet has equally comfortable room.

faqs.question: Is the weight limit on a multi-pet stroller combined or per pet?
faqs.answer: Generally combined for all pets together. Always check the specific product listing to confirm, and weigh each pet individually before adding the totals.

faqs.question: Can a dog and a cat share a multi-pet stroller?
faqs.answer: This depends on the specific product's compartment layout and how comfortable your particular pets are around each other. Pets already relaxed together at home generally settle better sharing a stroller.

faqs.question: Is a multi-pet stroller better than two single strollers?
faqs.answer: It depends on your situation. A multi-pet stroller means one stroller to manage, but two single strollers or a dedicated double dog stroller may suit better if your pets need clearly separated space.

faqs.question: What if my pets don't get along well in close quarters?
faqs.answer: Look for a design with clearly divided sections rather than one open shared compartment, or consider two separate strollers if your pets need more distance from each other.

faqs.question: Do multi-pet strollers work for more than two pets?
faqs.answer: This varies by product. Check the specific listing's stated capacity and compartment layout to confirm how many pets it's genuinely built to carry comfortably.

beds.intro:
A pet's bed is where they spend a genuinely large part of their day, so it's worth choosing properly rather than as an afterthought. What makes a good bed varies more by species and life stage than you might expect: a young puppy needs something durable and easy to clean, an older dog often benefits from more supportive cushioning, and a cat who loves to hide away wants something quite different to one who prefers to watch the world from a windowsill.

### Choosing by Pet

Our [dog beds](/beds/dog-beds) range covers everything from puppy-specific beds through to large breed and orthopaedic options. [Cat beds](/beds/cat-beds) includes enclosed cave-style designs, heated beds and window perches suited to different feline preferences. Our [small animal beds](/beds/small-animal-beds) range covers rabbits, guinea pigs and ferrets, each with different bedding and warmth needs.

### If Your Pet Travels

A familiar bed matters just as much away from home as it does day to day. Our [travel beds](/beds/travel-beds) collection covers portable, packable designs built for exactly that, across every pet we cover.

### What Tends to Matter Across the Range

Regardless of species, a washable cover, a filling that holds its shape rather than flattening quickly, and sizing that gives your pet room to stretch out fully all matter more than appearance alone. The buying guide further down this page covers sizing by species in more detail.
beds.why_choose:
A well-chosen bed supports your pet's body properly during rest, which matters more than it might seem for a good night's sleep or a restful afternoon nap, particularly as pets age or if they're prone to sleeping in the same position for long periods. The right level of cushioning and support underneath makes a genuine difference to comfort over time.

Beyond comfort, a dedicated bed gives a pet a consistent, familiar space of their own, which many pets come to associate with settling down and relaxing, rather than sleeping wherever happens to be convenient at the time.
beds.sizing_guide: Sizing varies considerably by species, so there's no single rule that applies across this whole range, but the underlying approach is the same: measure your pet lying down at full length and add a little extra room on top, rather than sizing too tightly. For dogs and cats, pay attention to the bed's weight guidance as well as its dimensions, since some beds are built with a specific level of support in mind. For rabbits, guinea pigs and other small animals, warmth and a snug, secure feel generally matter more than open space. Each animal-specific category further down this page has more detailed guidance for that pet.

faqs.question: What size bed does my pet need?
faqs.answer: Measure your pet lying down at full length and add a little extra room, rather than sizing too tightly or too loosely. Check the specific category for your pet for more detailed guidance.

faqs.question: Do you sell beds for pets other than dogs and cats?
faqs.answer: Yes, our small animal beds range covers rabbits, guinea pigs and ferrets, alongside the wider dog and cat ranges.

faqs.question: How often should I replace my pet's bed?
faqs.answer: This depends on use and the specific product, but a bed that's visibly flattened, torn or no longer supportive is generally worth replacing rather than persisting with.

faqs.question: Are pet beds machine washable?
faqs.answer: Many have a removable, washable cover. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page, since materials and washing guidance vary between items.

faqs.question: Do you offer free UK delivery on beds?
faqs.answer: Yes, orders over £50 qualify for free standard UK shipping, with a small delivery charge shown at checkout for orders under that. We also offer 30-day returns.

beds/dog-beds.intro:
Dogs vary enormously in size and life stage, and a bed that works well for one often isn't the right fit for another, which is why this range is organised around exactly those differences rather than one generic design. A growing puppy, a large adult breed, and an older dog managing stiffer joints all genuinely benefit from a bed built with their specific situation in mind.

### Shopping by Size and Age

Our [puppy beds](/beds/dog-beds/puppy-beds) range suits young, still-growing dogs with a softer, more secure shape, while [small dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/small-dog-beds) and [large dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds) cover adult dogs at either end of the size range. For older dogs or those with stiffer joints, our [orthopaedic dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/orthopaedic-dog-beds) range uses supportive foam designed to cushion pressure points more evenly than a standard filled bed.

### Shopping by Situation

Dogs who prefer to be raised off the floor, particularly in warmer weather, are often more comfortable in our [elevated dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds) range. If your dog needs a familiar bed to bring along when travelling or staying away, our [travel dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/travel-dog-beds) range is built to be portable without sacrificing comfort.

### The Wider Range

If you're comparing beds across other pets too, our [beds](/beds) hub covers cat and small animal beds alongside this dog-specific range.
beds/dog-beds.why_choose:
A dog bed matched to your dog's actual size and life stage tends to get used properly, rather than becoming somewhere they avoid in favour of the sofa or the floor. Too small and a dog can't stretch out fully; too large and some dogs feel less secure without the sides to lean against.

Life stage matters just as much as size. A young, still-growing puppy has different needs to an older dog managing stiffer joints, and buying with that specific stage in mind, rather than a single generic bed meant to last a dog's entire life unchanged, generally gives a better result at each point.
beds/dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length, nose to tail, and add a little extra room on top rather than sizing too tightly. Check the bed's weight guidance as well as its dimensions, since some beds are built with a specific level of support in mind for a particular size range. If your dog tends to sleep curled up, a slightly smaller bed with raised sides can feel cosier, while dogs who stretch out fully generally do better with a flatter, more open design.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right size dog bed?
faqs.answer: Measure your dog lying down at full length and add a little extra room, checking this against the specific product's stated dimensions and weight guidance rather than relying on breed alone.

faqs.question: Are orthopaedic dog beds worth it for older dogs?
faqs.answer: Many owners of older dogs, or dogs with stiffer joints, choose an orthopaedic bed for the more even, supportive cushioning it offers compared with a standard filled bed. Our orthopaedic dog beds range covers this specifically.

faqs.question: Do puppies need a different bed to adult dogs?
faqs.answer: Our puppy beds range is sized around a smaller, still-growing dog with a softer, more secure shape, generally more suitable than an adult-sized bed with a lot of extra space.

faqs.question: Why would I choose an elevated bed over a standard one?
faqs.answer: Dogs who prefer to be raised off the floor, particularly in warmer weather, are often more comfortable on an elevated bed. Our elevated dog beds range is built with this in mind.

faqs.question: Can I bring a dog bed when travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, our travel dog beds range is built to be portable and pack down easily, giving your dog a familiar place to rest away from home.

beds/dog-beds/puppy-beds.intro:
A growing puppy needs a bed that feels secure rather than one sized for the adult dog they'll eventually become. Puppy beds use a softer, more enclosed shape than a standard adult dog bed, generally with raised sides a puppy can settle against, which tends to suit a young dog still building confidence in unfamiliar situations.

### Built to Handle Puppy Life

Puppyhood tends to be messier and more chew-prone than later life, so a durable, easy to clean cover matters more here than it might for an adult dog's bed. A removable, washable cover is worth prioritising, since accidents and general mess are simply part of raising a young puppy.

### Sizing for Now, Not Later

It's tempting to buy ahead for the size your puppy will eventually reach, but a bed that's too large can leave a puppy feeling less secure rather than more comfortable. Size for their current measurements with a little room to grow, and plan to move up as they do.

### As Your Puppy Grows

Once your puppy reaches their adult size, our [small dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/small-dog-beds) or [large dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds) range, depending on their eventual size, will generally serve you better than continuing to use a puppy-specific bed they've outgrown.
beds/dog-beds/puppy-beds.why_choose:
A puppy's early experiences with their own sleeping space can shape how settled they feel about having somewhere consistent to rest. A bed sized and shaped around their current small size, with sides to settle against, tends to help a puppy feel secure faster than an oversized bed with a lot of empty space around them.

Durability matters more here than the appearance of the bed. A puppy explores the world partly through chewing and general mess, so a bed that holds up to regular washing and doesn't fall apart under investigation will genuinely last longer through this stage.
beds/dog-beds/puppy-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your puppy lying down at their current length, not an estimate of their adult size, and choose a bed that fits them snugly with a little room to grow rather than a large bed meant to last their whole life. Most puppies settle better in a bed with raised sides they can lean against than a completely flat, open design. Plan to move up in size as your puppy grows rather than buying ahead for their eventual adult measurements.

faqs.question: What size bed does my puppy need right now?
faqs.answer: Measure your puppy at their current length rather than estimating their adult size, and choose a bed that fits them snugly now, moving up in size as they grow.

faqs.question: Are puppy beds machine washable?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable cover, worth prioritising given how messy puppyhood tends to be. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page.

faqs.question: Should a puppy bed have raised sides?
faqs.answer: Many puppies settle better in a bed with raised sides to lean against, which tends to feel more secure than a completely flat, open design for a young dog still building confidence.

faqs.question: When should I move my puppy to an adult-sized bed?
faqs.answer: Once they're approaching their adult size, or if they're clearly outgrowing their current bed's dimensions, whichever comes first.

faqs.question: How do I stop my puppy chewing their bed?
faqs.answer: This comes down to general puppy training and providing appropriate chew toys separately, more than the bed itself, though a durable, well-stitched cover will hold up better to investigation.

beds/dog-beds/small-dog-beds.intro:
Small dog breeds generally prefer a bed with a bit more enclosure than a large, flat design offers, often settling more readily into a bed with raised or bolstered sides they can rest against. This range is sized around that preference, with a smaller footprint that suits a smaller dog without leaving excess unused space.

### Shape as Well as Size

Beyond overall dimensions, shape matters here. Bolster-style beds with raised edges suit dogs who like to curl up and rest their head on something, while a flatter design suits a dog who prefers to stretch out fully. Both are worth considering rather than assuming one shape suits every small dog equally well.

### If Your Dog Runs Warm

Some small dogs prefer to be raised off the floor rather than lying directly on it, particularly in warmer weather. Our [elevated dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds) range covers that alternative if a standard floor bed doesn't suit your dog.

### If Your Dog Is Growing

For a puppy not yet at their adult size, our [puppy beds](/beds/dog-beds/puppy-beds) range is built around their smaller, still-growing proportions rather than an adult small breed's stable size.
beds/dog-beds/small-dog-beds.why_choose:
A bed sized specifically for a small dog avoids the two common issues with using a larger, general-purpose bed: too much unused space, which some small dogs find less reassuring than a snugger fit, and a filling or support structure calibrated for a heavier dog's weight rather than a lighter one's.

Shape and enclosure matter more for small breeds than for larger dogs in many cases, since a lot of small dogs naturally prefer to curl up rather than stretch out fully, which is why bolster and raised-side designs feature heavily in this range.
beds/dog-beds/small-dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length and add a little extra room, checking this against the bed's stated dimensions rather than assuming any "small dog bed" fits every small breed equally well. If your dog tends to curl up rather than stretch out, a bolster-style bed with raised sides is worth prioritising over a flat, open design.

faqs.question: What size counts as a small dog bed?
faqs.answer: This varies by product, so check the specific dimensions against your dog's measured length lying down rather than relying on the category label alone.

faqs.question: Should I choose a bolster bed or a flat bed for a small dog?
faqs.answer: A bolster-style bed with raised sides suits dogs who like to curl up and rest their head against something, while a flatter design suits a dog who prefers to stretch out fully.

faqs.question: Are small dog beds suitable for puppies?
faqs.answer: It depends on your puppy's current size rather than their expected adult size. If they're still noticeably smaller than an adult small breed, our puppy beds range is sized more specifically for them.

faqs.question: How do I clean a small dog bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable cover. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page, since materials and washing guidance vary between items.

faqs.question: Do small dog beds come in raised, elevated styles too?
faqs.answer: Some small dogs prefer to be raised off the floor. Our elevated dog beds range covers that style specifically if a standard floor bed doesn't suit your dog.

beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds.intro:
Larger dog breeds need genuine room to stretch out fully, not a bed that's simply a bit bigger than a small dog design. This range is built with that extra length and width in mind, generally with a sturdier base and denser filling to hold up to a heavier dog's weight without flattening quickly.

### Support Matters More at This Size

A heavier dog puts more sustained pressure on a bed's filling than a smaller dog does, so the quality and density of that filling matters more here than for a compact bed. A bed that compresses quickly under weight will stop offering real support well before it looks worn out on the surface.

### If Your Dog Has Stiffer Joints

Many owners of larger, older dogs choose a bed built with more supportive foam specifically for this reason. Our [orthopaedic dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/orthopaedic-dog-beds) range uses foam designed to cushion pressure points more evenly than standard filling, worth considering alongside a standard large bed.

### Keeping Cool

Larger dogs can run warmer than smaller breeds, and some prefer to be raised slightly off the floor as a result. Our [elevated dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds) range is worth checking if that sounds like your dog.
beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds.why_choose:
Getting the size right matters enormously for a larger dog, since a bed that's even a little too small leaves them unable to stretch out fully, which defeats much of the point of having a dedicated bed rather than lying on the floor. Genuine length and width, not just a bed that looks large in photos, is what actually matters here.

The base and filling also need real structural capacity. A bed built for a lighter dog will compress and lose its shape faster under sustained heavier weight, so checking a product is actually built with a larger dog's weight in mind, not just its size, is worth doing before buying.
beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length, nose to tail, and add a reasonable amount of extra room, since larger dogs benefit from genuine space to stretch rather than a snug fit. Check the bed's weight guidance as well as its dimensions, since filling density varies and a bed rated for a lighter dog may compress quickly under a heavier one. If your dog has stiffer joints, it's worth comparing against our orthopaedic dog beds range for more supportive cushioning.

faqs.question: How much bigger should a large dog bed be than my dog?
faqs.answer: Measure your dog lying down at full length and add a reasonable margin so they can stretch out fully without their body extending past the edges of the bed.

faqs.question: Do large dog beds need denser filling?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since a heavier dog puts more sustained pressure on the filling. A bed built specifically for larger breeds tends to use a denser fill that holds its shape better under that weight.

faqs.question: Should I choose an orthopaedic bed for an older large dog?
faqs.answer: Many owners of older, larger dogs do, given the more even, supportive cushioning it offers. Our orthopaedic dog beds range covers this specifically.

faqs.question: Are large dog beds machine washable?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable cover, though check the specific product, since some larger covers may need washing at a launderette due to machine capacity.

faqs.question: Why would a large dog prefer an elevated bed?
faqs.answer: Larger dogs can run warmer than smaller breeds, and some prefer to be raised off the floor as a result. Our elevated dog beds range covers this style specifically.

beds/dog-beds/orthopaedic-dog-beds.intro:
Orthopaedic dog beds use supportive foam designed to cushion pressure points more evenly across a dog's body than a standard filled bed, which is why many owners choose one for older dogs or those with stiffer joints. The idea is straightforward: rather than a dog's weight sinking unevenly into loose filling, a firmer supportive base spreads that weight more consistently underneath them.

### What to Look For

A supportive foam base is the defining feature here, generally denser and firmer than the filling in a standard bed. A removable, washable cover still matters, and non-slip material underneath is worth checking for if your dog will be using the bed on a hard or smooth floor, so it doesn't shift around as they get in and out.

### A Note on What This Bed Does

An orthopaedic bed is designed for comfort and support, not as a treatment for any specific joint condition. If your dog has a diagnosed condition or you're concerned about their joints or mobility, speak to your vet about the best approach for your dog specifically, alongside choosing a supportive bed.

### For Larger Dogs Specifically

If your dog is also a larger breed, our [large dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds) range covers the sizing side of that combination, worth checking alongside this category for the right overall fit.
beds/dog-beds/orthopaedic-dog-beds.why_choose:
The appeal of a supportive foam base comes down to how evenly it distributes a dog's weight compared with loose, standard filling, which can compress unevenly under pressure points such as hips and shoulders over time. A more consistent, supportive surface tends to suit dogs who spend a lot of time resting, particularly as they get older.

Getting in and out of bed matters too for a dog who's a little stiffer than they used to be, so a lower profile bed with a non-slip base can make a genuine practical difference alongside the supportive foam itself.
beds/dog-beds/orthopaedic-dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length and choose a bed with enough room to stretch out fully on the supportive surface, rather than a snug fit that limits how they can position themselves. Check the bed's weight guidance carefully, since foam density and support are calibrated to a specific weight range, and a bed rated for a lighter dog won't offer the same support to a heavier one.

faqs.question: What makes a bed orthopaedic?
faqs.answer: Generally a supportive foam base designed to cushion pressure points more evenly than standard loose filling, rather than a specific certification or medical designation.

faqs.question: Will an orthopaedic bed help my dog's joint condition?
faqs.answer: An orthopaedic bed is designed for comfort and support, not as a treatment for a specific condition. If you're concerned about your dog's joints or mobility, speak to your vet about the best approach for your dog.

faqs.question: Is an orthopaedic bed only suitable for older dogs?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, though many owners of older dogs or those with stiffer joints choose one specifically for the more supportive cushioning. Any dog can rest on a supportive bed.

faqs.question: How is an orthopaedic bed different from a standard one?
faqs.answer: It generally uses a denser, more supportive foam base rather than loose filling, aiming to distribute weight more evenly across pressure points.

faqs.question: Can I wash an orthopaedic dog bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable cover over the foam base itself, which typically isn't machine washable. Always check the specific care instructions on the product page.

beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds.intro:
An elevated dog bed raises your dog off the floor on a taut, breathable base rather than a traditional filled cushion, which some dogs prefer, particularly in warmer weather or on warm flooring. Air can circulate underneath the bed rather than heat building up the way it can with a dog lying directly on a filled surface.

### Why Some Dogs Prefer This Style

Dogs who tend to seek out cooler spots, tiled floors or shaded ground, often take well to an elevated bed for the same reason. It's also worth considering for dogs who spend time outdoors, since raising them off cold or damp ground can make a real difference to comfort compared with a standard cushion resting directly on the surface.

### Frame and Stability

Check the frame is sturdy and the base fabric is taut rather than sagging, since a wobbly or loose-fitting elevated bed won't feel as stable to your dog as a well-built one. Non-slip feet matter too, particularly on smooth or tiled flooring.

### For Larger Dogs

If your dog is a larger breed, check the frame's weight capacity carefully alongside our [large dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/large-dog-beds) range, since an elevated frame needs genuine structural strength to support a heavier dog without flexing.
beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds.why_choose:
The main practical benefit of an elevated bed is airflow underneath your dog, which some dogs clearly seek out, especially in warmer weather or on warm flooring, in a way that a standard filled bed sitting directly on the ground can't replicate.

For dogs who spend time outdoors, an elevated design also keeps them off cold or damp ground, which a filled cushion resting directly on the surface doesn't do as effectively, since damp can work its way through the filling over time.
beds/dog-beds/elevated-dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length and check this against the bed's frame dimensions, leaving enough room to stretch out fully on the raised surface. Check the frame's weight capacity carefully, since this is the main limiting factor for an elevated design, more so than for a standard filled bed, and a frame rated below your dog's weight won't hold up reliably over time.

faqs.question: Why would I choose an elevated bed over a standard one?
faqs.answer: Some dogs prefer the airflow underneath an elevated bed, particularly in warmer weather or on warm flooring, and it can also keep a dog off cold or damp ground if used outdoors.

faqs.question: Are elevated beds suitable for large dogs?
faqs.answer: Many are, but check the frame's specific weight capacity carefully, since it needs genuine structural strength to support a heavier dog without flexing or sagging.

faqs.question: Can an elevated bed be used outdoors?
faqs.answer: Many are suitable for outdoor use, keeping a dog off cold or damp ground, though check the specific product's guidance on outdoor and weather exposure before relying on it outside regularly.

faqs.question: Is an elevated bed comfortable for older dogs?
faqs.answer: This varies by dog. Some older dogs appreciate the firmer, taut surface, while others may prefer the softer cushioning of a standard or orthopaedic bed. It often comes down to individual preference.

faqs.question: How do I clean an elevated dog bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable fabric base that can be removed from the frame for a more thorough clean. Check the specific product's care instructions for full guidance.

beds/dog-beds/travel-dog-beds.intro:
A dog who's used to a consistent bed at home often settles faster away from it too, whether that's a weekend trip, a stay with family, or simply a bed you keep in the car. Travel dog beds are built to pack down small and light without giving up the comfort of a proper bed, so your dog has something familiar to settle into wherever you end up.

### What Makes a Bed Travel-Friendly

Look for a bed that folds or rolls down compactly, ideally with its own carry bag or strap, and a durable, easy-to-wipe outer material, since travel beds tend to see more varied surfaces and conditions than a bed that stays in one place at home. A washable cover still matters, but quick-dry practicality often matters just as much for a bed on the move.

### Keeping the Familiar Feel

If possible, bring your dog's usual bed on a trip rather than switching to something entirely new at the same time as a new environment, since the familiar scent and feel can help them settle faster in unfamiliar surroundings.

### For the Journey Itself

If you're also looking at how your dog travels, not just where they'll rest once you arrive, our [dog car carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-car-carriers) range covers secure options for the journey.
beds/dog-beds/travel-dog-beds.why_choose:
The case for a dedicated travel bed over simply bringing a standard bed along comes down to practicality: a bed designed to pack down small genuinely takes up less space in a car or suitcase, and durable, easy-clean materials hold up better to varied surfaces and conditions than a bed built to stay in one spot at home.

Familiarity still matters more than the bed's specific design, so where possible, choosing a travel bed early and using it at home occasionally too, rather than only bringing it out for trips, helps your dog associate it with comfort rather than something new.
beds/dog-beds/travel-dog-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your dog lying down at full length as you would for any bed, but also weigh up how compactly the bed folds against how much room your dog actually needs, since travel beds often involve a small trade-off between packed size and full-length comfort. If your dog is a larger breed, check the packed dimensions fit your car or luggage before assuming a travel bed will be noticeably smaller to transport than a standard one.

faqs.question: How small do travel dog beds pack down?
faqs.answer: This varies by product, generally described in the listing alongside the bed's full-size dimensions. Check both figures if car boot or luggage space is limited.

faqs.question: Are travel dog beds as comfortable as a standard bed?
faqs.answer: Many are, though there's sometimes a small trade-off between how compactly a bed packs down and how much cushioning it offers. Check the specific product's filling and construction.

faqs.question: Can I use a travel bed as my dog's everyday bed?
faqs.answer: Yes, some owners do, and it can help a dog get used to the bed before relying on it away from home, since the familiarity matters more than which specific bed they're used to.

faqs.question: How do I clean a travel dog bed after a trip?
faqs.answer: Most have a durable, wipeable outer material, and many also have a removable washable cover. Check the specific product's care instructions.

faqs.question: Does a travel bed come with a carry bag?
faqs.answer: Many do, worth checking on the individual listing if this matters for how you'll be transporting it.

beds/cat-beds.intro:
Cats sleep for a large part of the day, and where they choose to do it says a lot about what they actually want from a bed, tucked away and hidden, raised up watching a window, or simply somewhere warm. This range is organised around those different preferences rather than one generic cat bed shape.

### Choosing by Preference

Our [cat cave beds](/beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds) range suits cats who love to hide away and feel enclosed, while [window cat beds](/beds/cat-beds/window-cat-beds) suit cats who'd rather watch the world go by from a windowsill. For cats who feel the cold, particularly older cats, our [heated cat beds](/beds/cat-beds/heated-cat-beds) range adds gentle warmth to the equation. If you have a young kitten, our [kitten beds](/beds/cat-beds/kitten-beds) range is sized and shaped specifically for a smaller, younger cat.

### Cats Often Want More Than One Bed

It's worth knowing that many cats happily use more than one bed depending on mood, time of day and temperature, so don't feel you need to find the single perfect bed that covers every preference at once.

### The Wider Range

If you're comparing beds across other pets in your household too, our [beds](/beds) hub covers dog and small animal beds alongside this cat-specific range.
beds/cat-beds.why_choose:
Cats have quite distinct sleeping preferences compared with dogs, often favouring a specific shape or level of enclosure over simple size and softness. A bed chosen with your particular cat's habits in mind, hiding away versus watching from height versus seeking warmth, tends to get used far more consistently than one picked on appearance alone.

Because cat preferences can also vary by season or mood, having a bed genuinely suited to how your cat actually behaves, rather than a generic cushion, often makes the difference between a bed that's used daily and one that's ignored in favour of a cardboard box or a warm patch of carpet.
beds/cat-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your cat curled up and stretched out separately, since cats sleep in both positions depending on mood and temperature, and check the bed's internal dimensions against both. Cave and enclosed beds generally suit a slightly snugger fit than open, flat beds, since the enclosure itself is part of the appeal. For window beds, check the weight capacity of any suction mount or fixing carefully before relying on it.

faqs.question: Why does my cat ignore the bed I bought them?
faqs.answer: Cat preferences are quite specific, some want to hide away, others want height or warmth. If your cat isn't using their current bed, it may simply not match their particular preference rather than being poorly made.

faqs.question: Do cats need more than one bed?
faqs.answer: Many cats happily use several beds around the home depending on mood, time of day and temperature, so it's common to have more than one style available.

faqs.question: What size bed does my cat need?
faqs.answer: Measure your cat both curled up and stretched out, and check the bed's internal dimensions against both, since cats sleep in different positions depending on mood and temperature.

faqs.question: Are cave beds suitable for all cats?
faqs.answer: Cave beds particularly suit cats who like to hide away and feel enclosed. A more nervous or shy cat often takes to this style especially well, though every cat has their own preference.

faqs.question: Do you offer beds specifically for kittens?
faqs.answer: Yes, our kitten beds range is sized and shaped around a young, smaller cat rather than being a scaled-down adult bed.

beds/cat-beds/kitten-beds.intro:
A young kitten benefits from a bed of their own that's sized to their small current size, generally softer and more enclosed than an adult cat bed, giving them somewhere secure to settle as they get used to a new home. A bed that's too large can feel less reassuring to a kitten than one that's snugly sized to them.

### A Secure, Enclosed Shape

Kittens often settle best in a bed with raised or enclosed sides, similar in principle to a cave bed, since the enclosure gives them something to feel tucked against. A soft, washable liner matters here too, given how much time a young kitten spends asleep and how likely a bed is to need regular washing at this age.

### Placement Matters Too

Where you put a kitten's bed can matter as much as the bed itself. A quiet corner away from heavy foot traffic generally helps a young kitten feel more settled than a bed placed somewhere busy.

### As Your Kitten Grows

Once your kitten reaches their adult size, our wider [cat beds](/beds/cat-beds) range, including [cat cave beds](/beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds) if they've shown a preference for enclosed spaces, will generally suit them better than continuing to use a kitten-specific bed.
beds/cat-beds/kitten-beds.why_choose:
A kitten's early experience of having their own secure resting space can shape how settled they feel in a new home more broadly. A bed sized and shaped around their current small size, rather than a large adult bed with excess space, tends to help a kitten feel more secure faster.

Because kittens sleep for such a large part of the day and are still developing routines, having a soft, easy to wash bed matters more practically here than it might for an adult cat's bed, simply given how much use it gets during this stage.
beds/cat-beds/kitten-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your kitten curled up rather than stretched out, since kittens tend to sleep curled for much of the day, and choose a bed that fits them snugly rather than one with a lot of extra space. Plan to move to our wider cat beds range once your kitten approaches their adult size rather than trying to make a kitten bed last indefinitely.

faqs.question: What size bed does my kitten need?
faqs.answer: Measure your kitten curled up rather than stretched out, and choose a bed that fits them snugly, since a kitten bed with a lot of extra space can feel less secure to them.

faqs.question: Where should I put my kitten's bed?
faqs.answer: A quiet corner away from heavy foot traffic generally helps a young kitten feel more settled than a bed placed somewhere busy or high traffic.

faqs.question: Are kitten beds washable?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable liner, worth prioritising given how much time a young kitten spends asleep and how often the bed may need cleaning.

faqs.question: When should I move my kitten to an adult cat bed?
faqs.answer: Once they're approaching their adult size, our wider cat beds range, including cave-style beds if they've shown a preference for enclosed spaces, will generally suit them better.

faqs.question: Do kittens prefer enclosed or open beds?
faqs.answer: Many kittens settle best in a bed with raised or enclosed sides, similar in principle to a cave bed, since the enclosure gives them something secure to settle against.

beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds.intro:
Many cats feel most relaxed somewhere enclosed, tucked away from open sightlines rather than resting out in the open. Cat cave beds are built around that instinct, with a covered, semi-enclosed shape a cat can burrow into rather than a flat open cushion, generally suiting cats who already seek out boxes, wardrobes or other hidden spots around the home.

### Why the Enclosure Matters

A covered shape gives a cat a sense of security that an open bed doesn't, particularly useful for a nervous or easily startled cat, or simply one whose natural preference leans toward hiding away to rest rather than being visible. The entrance size matters here too, generally snug enough to feel enclosed without being difficult for your cat to get in and out of comfortably.

### Material and Warmth

Because a cave bed encloses your cat more than an open design, the interior material and any insulation matter a little more here, since less airflow reaches inside than an open cushion. A soft, washable interior lining is worth checking for given how enclosed the space is.

### If Your Cat Prefers the Opposite

Not every cat wants to hide away. If yours prefers height and visibility instead, our [window cat beds](/beds/cat-beds/window-cat-beds) range covers that quite different preference.
beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds.why_choose:
The appeal of a cave bed comes down to matching a genuinely common feline instinct: seeking out an enclosed, hidden spot to rest rather than an open one. Cats who already choose boxes or wardrobes over an open bed at home are strong candidates for taking well to this style specifically.

A well-made cave bed also tends to hold its shape better than an open cushion over time, since the structured covered shape doesn't rely purely on loose filling to keep its form the way a flat bed does.
beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your cat curled up, since that's generally the position they'll rest in inside a cave bed, and check the internal space is snug enough to feel enclosed without being so tight your cat can't turn around or get comfortable. Check the entrance size too, making sure it's large enough for your cat to get in and out easily without squeezing.

faqs.question: How do I know if my cat will like a cave bed?
faqs.answer: Cats who already seek out boxes, wardrobes or other hidden spots to rest are strong candidates for a cave bed, since it caters to that same instinct to feel enclosed.

faqs.question: Is a cave bed too warm for a cat?
faqs.answer: Most are designed with breathable materials despite the enclosed shape, though it's worth checking the specific product if your home tends to run warm, since less airflow reaches inside than an open bed.

faqs.question: What size entrance should a cat cave bed have?
faqs.answer: Large enough for your cat to get in and out comfortably without squeezing, but snug enough that the enclosed feel is still there once they're inside.

faqs.question: Are cave beds good for nervous cats?
faqs.answer: Many nervous or easily startled cats respond well to the enclosed, hidden feel of a cave bed, though every cat has their own preference and it's worth observing how yours responds.

faqs.question: How do I clean a cat cave bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable interior lining. Check the specific product's care instructions, since the outer structured shell may need different care to the liner.

beds/cat-beds/heated-cat-beds.intro:
Cats who feel the cold, particularly older cats, often gravitate toward the warmest spot in the house, a patch of sun, near a radiator, or on top of the boiler. A heated cat bed brings that warmth to a dedicated resting spot instead, giving them somewhere consistently warm to settle rather than competing for the sunniest windowsill.

### What to Check Before Buying

Look for a bed with a low-voltage, pet-safe heating element and a cover that fully encloses the wiring, since safety around the heating component matters more here than with any other bed type. A removable, washable outer cover is still worth checking for, kept separate from the heating element itself during washing.

### A Note on Warmth and Health

A heated bed offers gentle warmth for comfort, it isn't a treatment for any specific health condition. If you're concerned about your cat's health, mobility or temperature regulation, speak to your vet rather than relying on a heated bed alone.

### If Enclosure Matters More Than Warmth

If your cat's main preference is for a hidden, enclosed space rather than specifically warmth, our [cat cave beds](/beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds) range may suit them better, or the two preferences can often be combined depending on the specific product.
beds/cat-beds/heated-cat-beds.why_choose:
Cats naturally seek out warm spots to rest, and a dedicated heated bed removes the competition for the sunniest windowsill or the warmest radiator spot, giving them a consistent, comfortable place to settle regardless of the weather or time of day.

Safety is the main thing that separates a well-built heated bed from a risk, so checking for a properly enclosed, low-voltage heating element and following the manufacturer's usage guidance matters more here than with a standard unheated bed.
beds/cat-beds/heated-cat-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your cat curled up, since that's generally how they'll rest on a heated bed, and check the heated area itself, not just the overall bed size, actually covers enough space for your cat to settle on it comfortably. Some heated beds only warm a section of the surface, so check the product details rather than assuming the entire bed is heated evenly.

faqs.question: Are heated cat beds safe to leave plugged in?
faqs.answer: Look for a bed with a low-voltage, pet-safe heating element and follow the manufacturer's specific usage guidance. Always check the product's safety information before leaving it unattended for extended periods.

faqs.question: Will a heated bed help my cat's joints?
faqs.answer: A heated bed offers gentle warmth for comfort, it isn't a treatment for a specific health condition. If you're concerned about your cat's joints or mobility, speak to your vet.

faqs.question: Can I wash a heated cat bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable outer cover, kept separate from the heating element during washing. Always check the specific product's care instructions.

faqs.question: Does the whole bed heat up or just part of it?
faqs.answer: This varies by product, some heat the entire surface while others warm a specific section. Check the individual listing rather than assuming even heating across the whole bed.

faqs.question: Is a heated bed suitable for kittens?
faqs.answer: Many are, though always check the specific product's guidance and supervise use, particularly with a young kitten who may not yet understand to move if the bed feels too warm.

beds/cat-beds/window-cat-beds.intro:
Some cats would rather watch the world go by than hide away, and a window bed gives them exactly that: a raised, secure perch fixed to a windowsill where they can watch birds, passers-by and general outdoor activity from a comfortable, elevated spot. It's a distinctly different preference to an enclosed cave bed, and worth choosing based on how your particular cat actually likes to spend their time.

### Checking the Fixing

Most window beds attach using strong suction cups or a mounting bracket, and this fixing is the single most important thing to get right, since it's supporting your cat's full weight against a vertical surface. Check the stated weight capacity carefully and follow the manufacturer's installation guidance closely, testing the fixing is fully secure before letting your cat use it unsupervised.

### Sunlight and Warmth

A window bed often doubles as a warm spot thanks to natural sunlight, which many cats find just as appealing as the view itself. Check the window's exposure through the day, since a bed in full sun for hours can get quite warm.

### If Your Cat Prefers to Hide

Not every cat wants height and visibility. If yours tends to seek out enclosed, hidden spots instead, our [cat cave beds](/beds/cat-beds/cat-cave-beds) range covers that opposite preference.
beds/cat-beds/window-cat-beds.why_choose:
A window bed taps into a cat's natural interest in watching their surroundings from a raised, secure vantage point, which many cats find genuinely engaging rather than simply a place to sleep. It's a different kind of appeal to a standard bed, combining rest with something to look at.

Getting the fixing right matters more here than for any other bed type on the site, since your cat's full weight rests against a vertical surface rather than the floor. A secure, well-tested mount is not optional, it's the single most important safety consideration for this style of bed.
beds/cat-beds/window-cat-beds.sizing_guide: Check the bed's weight capacity against your cat's actual current weight with a reasonable margin, since this matters more for a window-mounted bed than a floor bed, given the fixing is supporting that weight against a vertical surface. Measure your window's width to make sure the bed fits properly, and check the glass or frame is suitable for the specific mounting method before buying.

faqs.question: Are window cat beds safe?
faqs.answer: When installed correctly and used within the stated weight capacity, yes. Follow the manufacturer's installation guidance closely and test the fixing is fully secure before letting your cat use it unsupervised.

faqs.question: What weight can a window bed hold?
faqs.answer: This varies by product and is listed individually. Always check the stated capacity against your cat's actual current weight with a reasonable margin.

faqs.question: Will my window bed fit any window?
faqs.answer: This depends on your window's width and the type of glass or frame, since mounting methods vary. Check the specific product's requirements against your window before buying.

faqs.question: Does a window bed get too hot in direct sunlight?
faqs.answer: It can, depending on your window's exposure through the day. Check on your cat periodically if the bed sits in full sun for extended periods.

faqs.question: How do I clean a window cat bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a removable, washable cover. Check the specific product's care instructions, and check the mounting fixture periodically to make sure it remains secure over time.

beds/small-animal-beds.intro:
Small pets generally need warmth and enclosure more than open space when it comes to resting, quite different priorities to a dog or cat bed. This range is built around those specific needs for rabbits, guinea pigs and ferrets, each with their own bedding and burrowing habits.

### Choosing by Species

Our [rabbit beds](/beds/small-animal-beds/rabbit-beds) range gives rabbits a soft, insulated place to rest, suited to their tendency to sprawl out when fully relaxed. [Guinea pig beds](/beds/small-animal-beds/guinea-pig-beds) covers a similar approach for guinea pigs, who particularly like to burrow somewhere warm and enclosed. For ferrets, who often prefer to sleep tucked away and out of sight, our [ferret beds](/beds/small-animal-beds/ferret-beds) range leans toward a more fully enclosed design.

### Warmth and Insulation Matter More Here

Small pets lose heat more readily than larger animals, so insulation and a snug fit generally matter more for this range than open, spacious designs. A bed that feels almost too small for a dog or cat is often exactly right for a small animal seeking that enclosed, secure feeling.

### The Wider Range

If you're comparing beds across other pets in your household, our [beds](/beds) hub covers dog and cat beds alongside this small animal range.
beds/small-animal-beds.why_choose:
Small animals lose body heat faster relative to their size than larger pets do, which is why warmth and insulation feature so heavily in what makes a good bed for this range, more so than the open, spacious designs that suit a dog or cat. A snug, enclosed bed genuinely helps here rather than just being a stylistic choice.

Burrowing behaviour is common across rabbits, guinea pigs and other small pets, so a bed that allows for that, rather than a flat open cushion, tends to suit their natural instincts better and gets used more consistently as a result.
beds/small-animal-beds.sizing_guide: Small animal beds generally work best snug rather than spacious, since the enclosed, secure feeling matters more here than roominess. Check a bed's internal dimensions against your pet's size when curled up rather than fully stretched out, and prioritise insulation and a soft, warm lining over open space. Each species-specific category further down this page has more detailed guidance for that particular pet.

faqs.question: Do small animals need warmer beds than dogs and cats?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since small animals lose body heat faster relative to their size. Insulation and a snug, enclosed fit matter more here than the open designs that suit larger pets.

faqs.question: What size bed does my small pet need?
faqs.answer: Check a bed's internal dimensions against your pet's size when curled up rather than fully stretched out, since a snugger fit generally suits small animals better than a spacious one.

faqs.question: Do you sell beds for pets other than rabbits and guinea pigs?
faqs.answer: Yes, our ferret beds range covers ferrets specifically, who often prefer to sleep tucked away and out of sight, alongside our rabbit and guinea pig ranges.

faqs.question: Can I add bedding to a small animal bed?
