faqs.answer: Yes, most small animal beds work well with a layer of familiar hay or bedding added inside, which most small pets appreciate for the added warmth and familiar scent.

faqs.question: How do I clean a small animal bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable base and a washable liner or cover. Check the specific product's care instructions for full guidance.

beds/small-animal-beds/rabbit-beds.intro:
Rabbits appreciate a soft, insulated place to rest, generally sized to let them sprawl out fully when they're relaxed rather than staying curled up the whole time. Unlike the solid, non-slip base a rabbit needs from a carrier, a rabbit bed can lean into softness, since the priority here is comfort at rest rather than stability during movement.

### Insulation and Warmth

Rabbits benefit from a bed with genuine insulation underneath them, particularly if they spend time on a hard hutch floor or cold flooring, since a thin cushion alone won't do much to keep cold from coming up through the base.

### Chew-Resistant Where Possible

Rabbits are natural chewers, and a bed's material and stitching will get tested accordingly. A durable outer material and reinforced seams tend to hold up better to this than a delicate fabric, worth factoring in in particular for a rabbit who chews everything within reach.

### For Multiple Small Pets

If your household also includes guinea pigs, our [guinea pig beds](/beds/small-animal-beds/guinea-pig-beds) range follows a similar insulated approach, sized and shaped a little differently for their build.
beds/small-animal-beds/rabbit-beds.why_choose:
A dedicated rabbit bed gives them somewhere consistently warm and comfortable to rest, separate from wherever they happen to settle in their hutch or enclosure otherwise. Insulation matters more here than it might seem, since rabbits can lose a fair amount of body heat resting directly on a cold or hard surface.

Durability is worth taking seriously too, given how much rabbits naturally chew and dig at things within reach. A well-made bed with reinforced seams and a durable outer material will genuinely last longer than one built with lighter, more delicate materials.
beds/small-animal-beds/rabbit-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your rabbit both curled up and stretched out, since rabbits sprawl out fully when fully relaxed, and check the bed offers enough room for that rather than only fitting them curled. Larger rabbit breeds need proportionally more space than dwarf breeds, so check the specific product's dimensions against your rabbit's actual size rather than assuming one size suits all rabbits.

faqs.question: Do rabbits need a soft bed if they already have hay bedding?
faqs.answer: Many rabbits benefit from both, a dedicated bed adds insulation and a consistently comfortable spot, while hay bedding around the enclosure serves a different, more general purpose.

faqs.question: Will my rabbit chew their bed?
faqs.answer: This is common rabbit behaviour, and a durable outer material with reinforced seams will generally hold up better than delicate fabric. Some chewing is normal and difficult to fully prevent.

faqs.question: What size bed does my rabbit need?
faqs.answer: Measure your rabbit both curled up and fully stretched out, since rabbits sprawl out when relaxed, and choose a bed with enough room for that rather than only fitting them curled.

faqs.question: Why does insulation matter for a rabbit bed?
faqs.answer: Rabbits can lose body heat resting directly on a cold or hard hutch floor, so a bed with genuine insulation underneath makes a real difference to their comfort, particularly in colder weather.

faqs.question: How do I clean a rabbit bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable base and a washable liner or cover. Check the specific product's care instructions, and clean regularly given how much time rabbits spend resting in one place.

beds/small-animal-beds/guinea-pig-beds.intro:
Guinea pigs particularly like to burrow somewhere warm, which shapes what makes a good bed for them more than almost any other factor. A snug, enclosed design that they can tuck themselves into tends to suit guinea pigs better than an open, flat cushion, echoing the same burrowing instinct that shows up in how they use bedding and hideaways around their enclosure.

### Enclosed Over Open

Look for a bed with raised or covered sides rather than a completely flat design, since guinea pigs generally settle better somewhere they can burrow into rather than lying fully exposed. A soft, warm lining matters too, given how much time guinea pigs spend resting.

### Multiple Guinea Pigs

If you keep more than one guinea pig, and most do best living in pairs or small groups, check whether a bed is sized for one or built to comfortably fit more than one at a time, since guinea pigs often like to rest close together.

### For Other Small Pets

If your household also includes rabbits, our [rabbit beds](/beds/small-animal-beds/rabbit-beds) range follows a similar insulated, cosy approach, sized differently for their longer build.
beds/small-animal-beds/guinea-pig-beds.why_choose:
A bed that caters to a guinea pig's natural burrowing instinct, with sides they can tuck against rather than an open flat surface, tends to get used far more consistently than a generic cushion. This is a genuinely strong, consistent preference across the species, not just an occasional habit.

Since guinea pigs often live and rest in pairs or small groups, choosing a bed with their social habits in mind, rather than sizing purely for one guinea pig, can make a real difference to whether it actually gets used or ignored in favour of resting together elsewhere.
beds/small-animal-beds/guinea-pig-beds.sizing_guide: Check a bed's internal dimensions against your guinea pig's curled-up size rather than their fully stretched length, since guinea pigs favour a snug, enclosed fit over open space. If you keep more than one guinea pig, check whether the specific bed is sized to comfortably fit them together, since guinea pigs often prefer resting close to each other.

faqs.question: Should a guinea pig bed be open or enclosed?
faqs.answer: Enclosed generally suits guinea pigs better, given their strong instinct to burrow somewhere warm and covered rather than resting on an open, flat surface.

faqs.question: Can two guinea pigs share the same bed?
faqs.answer: Many guinea pigs like to rest close together, so a bed sized to comfortably fit more than one can work well if you keep a pair or small group. Check the specific product's size.

faqs.question: What size bed does my guinea pig need?
faqs.answer: Check the internal dimensions against your guinea pig's curled-up size rather than their fully stretched length, since a snug, enclosed fit generally suits them better.

faqs.question: Do guinea pigs need bedding inside their bed as well?
faqs.answer: Many owners add a layer of hay or familiar bedding inside for extra warmth and a reassuring scent, alongside the bed's own lining.

faqs.question: How do I clean a guinea pig bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a wipeable base and a washable liner. Check the specific product's care instructions, and clean regularly given how much time guinea pigs spend resting in one place.

beds/small-animal-beds/ferret-beds.intro:
Ferrets often prefer to sleep tucked away and out of sight, generally seeking a fully enclosed, den-like space rather than resting in the open the way some other small pets do. Ferret beds lean into that instinct, with a more fully covered design than a typical small animal bed, often shaped more like a hammock or tunnel than an open cushion.

### Enclosed Shapes Suit Ferrets Well

Hammock and tunnel-style beds are popular for ferrets specifically, since they mirror the burrowing, hidden spaces ferrets naturally seek out. A fully covered design generally gets used more consistently than an open bed for this reason.

### Durability Matters

Ferrets are active and playful even around their sleeping space, so a durable, well-stitched material holds up better than something delicate. Check seams and fastenings are secure, since ferrets will investigate and test any part of their environment.

### For Other Small Pets

If your household includes other small animals with different needs, our [small animal beds](/beds/small-animal-beds) hub covers rabbits and guinea pigs, who generally prefer a less fully enclosed design than a ferret does.
beds/small-animal-beds/ferret-beds.why_choose:
A bed genuinely built around a ferret's preference for tucked-away, enclosed spaces tends to get used far more than an open cushion designed with a different small pet in mind. Hammock and tunnel-style designs in particular reflect how ferrets naturally like to rest, hidden away rather than visible.

Ferrets are also more physically active around their environment than some other small pets, even near their sleeping space, so durability and secure stitching genuinely matter more here than for a calmer, less investigative animal.
beds/small-animal-beds/ferret-beds.sizing_guide: Ferret beds tend to favour a snug, fully enclosed fit over open space, so check a bed's internal dimensions against your ferret's curled-up size rather than a fully stretched measurement. Hammock and tunnel styles vary in size by product, so check the specific listing rather than assuming a standard size fits every ferret comfortably.

faqs.question: Why do ferrets prefer hammock or tunnel-style beds?
faqs.answer: These shapes mirror the enclosed, hidden spaces ferrets naturally seek out to rest, which tends to suit them better than an open, flat cushion designed for a different small pet.

faqs.question: Are ferret beds durable enough for an active pet?
faqs.answer: Look for a bed with well-stitched seams and secure fastenings, since ferrets are active and will investigate and test their environment, including their sleeping space.

faqs.question: What size bed does my ferret need?
faqs.answer: Check the internal dimensions against your ferret's curled-up size, since ferret beds generally favour a snug, fully enclosed fit over open space.

faqs.question: Can two ferrets share the same bed?
faqs.answer: Many ferrets who live together happily share a bed. Check the specific product's size to confirm it comfortably fits more than one ferret if needed.

faqs.question: How do I clean a ferret bed?
faqs.answer: Most have a washable cover or liner. Check the specific product's care instructions, since ferrets can have a stronger scent than some other small pets and benefit from regular washing.

beds/travel-beds.intro:
A pet who's used to a familiar bed at home often settles faster away from it too, whether that's a weekend away, a stay with family, or somewhere new for any reason. Travel beds are built to pack down compactly and travel easily, across dogs, cats and other pets, giving them somewhere familiar to rest wherever you end up.

### What Makes a Bed Travel-Friendly

Look for a bed that folds or rolls down compactly, ideally with a carry bag or strap, and durable, easy-to-wipe materials, since travel beds tend to see more varied surfaces and conditions than a bed that stays in one place at home. A washable cover still matters, but quick-dry practicality often matters just as much for a bed on the move.

### For Dogs Specifically

If you're shopping specifically for a dog, our [travel dog beds](/beds/dog-beds/travel-dog-beds) range covers this same portable approach sized and built around dogs in particular.

### Bringing the Familiar Feel

Where possible, use a travel bed at home occasionally too, rather than only bringing it out for trips, so your pet associates it with comfort rather than something unfamiliar that only appears during unsettling changes to their routine.
beds/travel-beds.why_choose:
The case for a dedicated travel bed over bringing a standard bed along comes down to practicality: a bed designed to pack down small genuinely takes up less space in a car or suitcase, and durable, easy-clean materials hold up better to varied surfaces and conditions than a bed built to stay in one spot.

Familiarity still matters more than the bed's specific design. A pet who recognises their travel bed as somewhere safe and comfortable, because they've used it before, will generally settle faster in unfamiliar surroundings than one encountering a brand new bed for the first time away from home.
beds/travel-beds.sizing_guide: Measure your pet lying down at full length as you would for any bed, but also weigh up how compactly the bed folds against how much room they actually need, since travel beds often involve a small trade-off between packed size and full-length comfort. Check the packed dimensions fit your car boot or luggage before assuming a travel bed will be noticeably smaller to transport than a standard one.

faqs.question: How small do travel beds pack down?
faqs.answer: This varies by product, generally described in the listing alongside the bed's full-size dimensions. Check both figures if car boot or luggage space is limited.

faqs.question: Are travel beds suitable for cats as well as dogs?
faqs.answer: Yes, this range covers pets generally. If you're shopping specifically for a dog, our travel dog beds range is built and sized around dogs in particular.

faqs.question: Can I use a travel bed as my pet's everyday bed?
faqs.answer: Yes, some owners do, and it can help a pet get used to the bed before relying on it away from home, since the familiarity matters more than which specific bed they're used to.

faqs.question: How do I clean a travel bed after a trip?
faqs.answer: Most have a durable, wipeable outer material, and many also have a removable washable cover. Check the specific product's care instructions.

faqs.question: Does a travel bed come with a carry bag?
faqs.answer: Many do, worth checking on the individual listing if this matters for how you'll be transporting it.

carriers/dog-carriers/dog-bike-carriers.intro:
A dog bike carrier gives a dog who can't run alongside a bike for the full distance, whether that's due to their size, age, or simply not being built for the pace, a secure way to still join the ride. Rather than being left at home, they travel enclosed in a basket or fixed carrier attached to the handlebars, frame or rear rack, so the whole outing includes them without asking more of their legs than is fair.

### Where the Carrier Attaches

Front-mounted baskets, usually fixed to the handlebars, keep a dog close and in view, which suits a dog who feels more settled being able to see you and what's ahead. Rear-mounted carriers, fixed over the back wheel, shift the weight further back and can feel more stable at speed, though your dog can't see you directly. Which suits your dog better often comes down to how they handle not having a clear view of you during the ride.

### What Matters Most Here

A secure, wobble-free mounting point is the single most important thing to get right, since an unstable carrier is unsettling for your dog and genuinely unsafe for you both at any real speed. A secure harness or tether inside the carrier matters too, so your dog can't attempt to jump out mid-ride. Check the carrier's maximum weight rating carefully, since bike-mounted carriers are generally built for smaller, lighter dogs than a backpack or standard carrier would be.

### If Your Dog Prefers to Be Carried on You

Not every dog settles well in a bike-mounted carrier, some feel more secure carried directly against you instead. Our [dog backpack carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/dog-backpack-carriers) range covers that alternative, worth considering if your dog is more of a hands-free-on-you candidate than a wheels-on-the-bike one.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-bike-carriers.why_choose:
A bike-mounted carrier lets a dog who can't manage the distance still be part of the ride, rather than being left behind entirely. For smaller dogs in particular, running alongside a bike for any real distance simply isn't realistic, and a secure carrier solves that without cutting them out of the outing.

Stability matters more here than on almost any other carrier format, since the carrier is fixed to a moving bike rather than carried by hand or worn on your body. A mounting point that flexes or wobbles undermines everything else about the carrier, regardless of how comfortable the interior is.
carriers/dog-carriers/dog-bike-carriers.sizing_guide: Check the maximum weight rating carefully, since bike-mounted carriers are generally built for smaller, lighter dogs than other formats, given the mounting point's own structural limits. Measure your dog's length and height and check these against the carrier's internal dimensions, making sure they can sit comfortably without pressing against the sides. Also check the carrier's fixing is compatible with your specific bike frame or handlebars before buying, since mounting systems vary between products.

faqs.question: What size dog is suitable for a bike carrier?
faqs.answer: Generally smaller, lighter dogs, since bike-mounted carriers have a lower weight rating than other formats due to the mounting point's own limits. Always check the specific product's stated capacity.

faqs.question: Is a front or rear-mounted bike carrier better?
faqs.answer: Front-mounted carriers keep your dog in view, which suits a dog who wants to see you, while rear-mounted carriers shift weight back and can feel more stable at speed, though your dog can't see you directly.

faqs.question: How do I keep my dog secure in a bike carrier?
faqs.answer: Look for a carrier with an internal harness or tether attachment, so your dog can't attempt to climb or jump out mid-ride, alongside a stable, wobble-free mounting point.

faqs.question: Will a bike carrier fit any bike?
faqs.answer: This depends on the specific mounting system and your bike's frame or handlebars. Check the product's compatibility details before buying rather than assuming a universal fit.

faqs.question: What if my dog doesn't settle in a bike carrier?
faqs.answer: Not every dog takes to being fixed to a moving bike. If yours seems unsettled, our dog backpack carriers range offers a hands-free alternative carried directly on you instead.

carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bicycle-carr.intro:
A puppy bicycle carrier lets a young puppy come along for a bike ride without being expected to run alongside you, which isn't appropriate for a young puppy's developing joints. These carriers attach to the bike itself, either mounted at the front on the handlebars or fitted to a rear rack, and hold your puppy in a secure, contained basket rather than a bag carried on your body.

### Front-Mounted vs Rear-Mounted

A front-mounted bicycle carrier keeps your puppy in view and close to the handlebars, which suits a nervous or very young puppy who benefits from being able to see you while you ride. A rear-mounted carrier sits behind the saddle instead, which can feel more stable at speed but means you can't see your puppy directly while cycling, so check the carrier's fixing points are genuinely secure before relying on either format.

### Weight Limits Matter More on a Bike

A bike is already balancing your weight, so a carrier's stated maximum weight capacity isn't just a comfort figure here, it affects handling too. Check this carefully against your puppy's current weight rather than an estimate, and reassess as they grow, since a puppy who fits comfortably now may outgrow a bicycle carrier within a few months.

### Getting Your Puppy Used to It

Introduce the carrier at home first, then try short, slow rides on quiet routes before attempting anything busier. A puppy who's calm being lifted in and out and sitting still in the carrier while stationary is in a much better position to cope with the movement and noise of an actual ride.

### Bicycle or Bike Carrier?

This range and our [puppy bike carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bike-carriers) range cover the same style of product, a basket or box carrier that fixes to the bike. Different products sit in each range, so it's worth checking both if you don't find the right fit here.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bicycle-carr.why_choose:
A bicycle carrier means your puppy can join you on rides that would otherwise be far too much for their legs and joints at this age, without leaving them at home. It also keeps them contained and off the ground entirely, away from passing traffic, other dogs, and the general unpredictability of a busy route.

Security matters more here than with most carrier types, since your puppy is moving at cycling speed rather than walking pace. Look for a genuinely secure attachment to the bike frame, a safety strap or harness clip inside the carrier itself, and enough ventilation to stay comfortable while you're both moving.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bicycle-carr.sizing_guide: Weigh your puppy at their current size and check this against the carrier's maximum weight capacity, leaving some margin rather than buying right at the limit. Measure the internal basket dimensions too, since a puppy needs enough room to sit and shift position slightly without feeling cramped or being able to climb out. As your puppy grows, recheck both figures rather than assuming the same carrier will still fit in a few months.

faqs.question: At what age can a puppy go in a bicycle carrier?
faqs.answer: This depends on your puppy's size and development rather than age alone. Always follow your vet's guidance on when your puppy is ready for this kind of outing, and start with short, slow rides rather than a long trip straightaway.

faqs.question: Is a front-mounted or rear-mounted bicycle carrier better for a puppy?
faqs.answer: A front-mounted carrier keeps your puppy in view and close to you, which often suits a younger or more nervous puppy better. A rear-mounted carrier can feel more stable but means you can't see your puppy directly while riding.

faqs.question: How do I know if a bicycle carrier is securely attached?
faqs.answer: Check the fixing points are rated for the carrier's loaded weight, not just the carrier's own weight, and test the attachment is firm with no movement before your puppy is inside.

faqs.question: Will my puppy be safe going faster on a bike than they would walking?
faqs.answer: A well-fitted, securely attached carrier keeps your puppy contained and off the ground throughout the ride. Start with short, slow, quiet routes so your puppy has a calm introduction before anything busier.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a bicycle carrier and a bike carrier?
faqs.answer: They describe the same style of product: a basket or box carrier that attaches to the bike itself. Our puppy bike carriers range covers similar options with some different builds.

carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bike-carrier.intro:
A puppy bike carrier is a basket or box-style carrier that fixes to your bicycle, giving your puppy a safe, contained space to ride in rather than running alongside you, which isn't appropriate for a young puppy's developing joints. Most designs clip onto the handlebars or a rear rack and open at the top for lifting your puppy in and out easily.

### Built Around Where Your Puppy Is Now

Just as with any other puppy carrier, size this around your puppy's current weight and build rather than guessing at their adult size. A bike carrier that's too roomy lets a puppy shift about and feel unsteady at speed, while one that's genuinely too small becomes uncomfortable fast, so check both the dimensions and the maximum weight rating before buying.

### Ventilation While Moving

A puppy in a bike carrier experiences more airflow and motion than one carried on foot, so mesh panelling that lets air through without letting your puppy climb or fall out is worth checking closely. A firm, flat base also helps your puppy stay balanced rather than sliding as the bike turns or slows.

### As Your Puppy Grows

A bike carrier sized for a small puppy will need replacing as they approach their adult weight, in the same way our [puppy carrier](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-carriers) range gets swapped for a small dog carrier over time. Keep an eye on the maximum weight rating and plan to size up rather than continuing to use a carrier your puppy has outgrown.

### Bike or Bicycle Carrier?

This range and our [puppy bicycle carriers](/carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bicycle-carriers) range cover the same style of product, a basket or box carrier that fixes to the bike. Different products sit in each range, so it's worth checking both if you don't find the right fit here.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bike-carrier.why_choose:
A bike carrier gives your puppy a genuine reason to come along on a ride they couldn't safely do on their own legs yet, kept contained, off the ground and away from traffic and other dogs the whole time. It also means cycling doesn't have to mean leaving your puppy behind.

Look for a secure clip-on fixing to the bike itself, a safety strap or clip inside the carrier so your puppy can't climb out mid-ride, and enough ventilation for a puppy who'll be moving through the air rather than sitting still. A washable liner is also worth having, since puppies aren't always tidy passengers.
carriers/dog-carriers/puppy-bike-carrier.sizing_guide: Check your puppy's current weight against the carrier's maximum capacity first, since this is a hard limit on a moving bike rather than a rough guide. Then check the internal basket dimensions, looking for enough room for your puppy to sit comfortably without being able to easily climb up and over the sides. Revisit both figures as your puppy grows, since a bike carrier is very much a current-size product rather than one bought with room to spare.

faqs.question: Is a bike carrier safe for a young puppy?
faqs.answer: A securely fitted carrier keeps your puppy contained and off the ground throughout the ride. Always check your vet's guidance on when your puppy is ready for this kind of outing, and start with short, slow, quiet rides.

faqs.question: How do I attach a bike carrier securely?
faqs.answer: Follow the product's fitting instructions closely and check there's no movement in the mounting before your puppy gets in. Test it a few times on a stationary bike before your first ride.

faqs.question: What size bike carrier does my puppy need?
faqs.answer: Weigh and measure your puppy at their current size, not an estimate of their adult size, and check this against the carrier's maximum weight rating and internal dimensions.

faqs.question: Can my puppy climb out of a bike carrier while riding?
faqs.answer: A carrier with a secure internal strap or clip and reasonably high sides reduces this risk considerably. Always check these features are present before buying, and never let your puppy travel unclipped.

faqs.question: What's the difference between this and a puppy bicycle carrier?
faqs.answer: They're the same style of product: a basket or box that fixes to the bike. Our puppy bicycle carriers range covers the same idea with some different builds, worth a look if you don't find the right fit here.
